The method has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, healthcare, and recommendation systems, addressing key challenges of inference latency, computational efficiency, and model interpretability.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Effective Techniques for Deploying Efficient Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This paper reviews the theoretical foundations, practical applications, and recent advances in knowledge distillation across various deep learning domains, demonstrating how these compression techniques enable efficient inference and broader accessibility of state-of-the-art models.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Cross-modal Knowledge Distillation for Vision-to-Sensor Action Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Human activity recognition (HAR) based on multi-modal approach has been recently shown to improve the accuracy performance of HAR. However, restricted computational resources associated with wearable devices, i.e., smartwatch, failed to directly support such advanced methods. To tackle this issue, this study introduces an end-to-end Vision-to-Sensor Knowledge Distillation (VSKD) framework. In this VSKD framework, only time-series data, i.e., accelerometer data, is needed from wearable devices during the testing phase. Therefore, this framework will not only reduce the computational demands on edge devices, but also produce a learning model that closely matches the performance of the computational expensive multi-modal approach. In order to retain the local temporal relationship and facilitate visual deep learning models, we first convert time-series data to two-dimensional images by applying the Gramian Angular Field ( GAF) based encoding method. We adopted ResNet18 and multi-scale TRN with BN-Inception as teacher and student network in this study, respectively. A novel loss function, named Distance and Angle-wised Semantic Knowledge loss (DASK), is proposed to mitigate the modality variations between the vision and the sensor domain. Extensive experimental results on UTD-MHAD, MMAct, and Berkeley-MHAD datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and competitiveness of the proposed VSKD model which can deployed on wearable sensors.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Crucial Technique for Effective Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential approach for compressing deep learning models while maintaining predictive performance. This technique involves training a smaller student model to mimic a larger, more capable teacher model, enabling efficient deployment without sacrificing accuracy. The method has proven particularly valuable across multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and machine translation, offering systematic solutions to reduce computational overhead and memory requirements in neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Approach to Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from a larger teacher model to a smaller student model, enabling practical deployment of deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The method has proven effective across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and speech processing, offering substantial computational savings with minimal accuracy degradation.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Releasing Graph Neural Networks with Differential Privacy Guarantees
papers_seen.abstract: With the increasing popularity of graph neural networks (GNNs) in several sensitive applications like healthcare and medicine, concerns have been raised over the privacy aspects of trained GNNs. More notably, GNNs are vulnerable to privacy attacks, such as membership inference attacks, even if only black-box access to the trained model is granted. We propose PrivGNN, a privacy-preserving framework for releasing GNN models in a centralized setting. Assuming an access to a public unlabeled graph, PrivGNN provides a framework to release GNN models trained explicitly on public data along with knowledge obtained from the private data in a privacy preserving manner. PrivGNN combines the knowledge-distillation framework with the two noise mechanisms, random subsampling, and noisy labeling, to ensure rigorous privacy guarantees. We theoretically analyze our approach in the Renyi differential privacy framework. Besides, we show the solid experimental performance of our method compared to several baselines adapted for graph-structured data. Our code is available at https://github.com/iyempissy/privGnn.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Unified Visual Transformer Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) have gained popularity recently. Even without customized image operators such as convolutions, ViTs can yield competitive performance when properly trained on massive data. However, the computational overhead of ViTs remains prohibitive, due to stacking multi-head self-attention modules and else. Compared to the vast literature and prevailing success in compressing convolutional neural networks, the study of Vision Transformer compression has also just emerged, and existing works focused on one or two aspects of compression. This paper proposes a unified ViT compression framework that seamlessly assembles three effective techniques: pruning, layer skipping, and knowledge distillation. We formulate a budget-constrained, end-to-end optimization framework, targeting jointly learning model weights, layer-wise pruning ratios/masks, and skip configurations, under a distillation loss. The optimization problem is then solved using the primal-dual algorithm. Experiments are conducted with several ViT variants, e.g. DeiT and T2T-ViT backbones on the ImageNet dataset, and our approach consistently outperforms recent competitors. For example, DeiT-Tiny can be trimmed down to 50\% of the original FLOPs almost without losing accuracy. Codes are available online:~\url{https://github.com/VITA-Group/UVC}.

papers_seen.author: Owens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are critical techniques for enabling the deployment of deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods address the fundamental challenge of maintaining model performance while significantly reducing computational costs, latency, and memory requirements. Through transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models, knowledge distillation achieves substantial improvements in efficiency without proportional losses in accuracy. This paper synthesizes recent advances in knowledge distillation techniques across multiple domains, including computer vision, natural language processing, and federated learning, demonstrating the versatility and practical importance of these approaches for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Daniels
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental model compression technique that enables the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, efficient student models. This approach addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems across domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems. By transferring learned representations and prediction patterns, knowledge distillation reduces inference latency, computational requirements, and memory footprints while maintaining competitive performance. The field has evolved to encompass diverse methodologies including multi-teacher selection strategies, architectural variations, fairness-aware approaches, and applications to specialized domains such as federated learning and adversarially robust models.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Compelling Strategy for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and essential technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By enabling the transfer of knowledge from large teacher networks to compact student models, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems across resource-constrained environments. This technique has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications, offering systematic solutions to reduce computational overhead and memory requirements without proportional accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are critical techniques for enabling the deployment of sophisticated deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, maintaining high performance while dramatically reducing inference time and memory requirements. This review examines the current state of knowledge distillation across computer vision and natural language processing domains, discussing key mechanisms, practical applications, and emerging challenges in the field.

papers_seen.author: Henson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Comprehensive Approach to Efficient Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining or improving performance. This approach enables deployment of sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across diverse applications including natural language processing, computer vision, and generative models. By transferring knowledge from teacher models to compact student networks, distillation addresses critical challenges in computational efficiency, inference latency, and practical deployment while preserving predictive accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for enabling the practical deployment of deep learning and natural language processing models in resource-constrained environments. These approaches transfer knowledge from large, complex teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student networks while maintaining competitive performance. Through mechanisms including output-level transfer, intermediate representation matching, and attention-based approaches, knowledge distillation achieves substantial reductions in model size and computational cost without proportional losses in accuracy. The technique has proven particularly valuable across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, federated learning, and specialized applications, making it essential for real-world model deployment scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: CoReD: Generalizing Fake Media Detection with Continual Representation using Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Over the last few decades, artificial intelligence research has made tremendous strides, but it still heavily relies on fixed datasets in stationary environments. Continual learning is a growing field of research that examines how AI systems can learn sequentially from a continuous stream of linked data in the same way that biological systems do. Simultaneously, fake media such as deepfakes and synthetic face images have emerged as significant to current multimedia technologies. Recently, numerous method has been proposed which can detect deepfakes with high accuracy. However, they suffer significantly due to their reliance on fixed datasets in limited evaluation settings. Therefore, in this work, we apply continuous learning to neural networks' learning dynamics, emphasizing its potential to increase data efficiency significantly. We propose Continual Representation using Distillation (CoReD) method that employs the concept of Continual Learning (CL), Representation Learning (RL), and Knowledge Distillation (KD). We design CoReD to perform sequential domain adaptation tasks on new deepfake and GAN-generated synthetic face datasets, while effectively minimizing the catastrophic forgetting in a teacher-student model setting. Our extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method is efficient at domain adaptation to detect low-quality deepfakes videos and GAN-generated images from several datasets, outperforming the-state-of-art baseline methods.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Understanding BERT Rankers Under Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep language models such as BERT pre-trained on large corpus have given a huge performance boost to the state-of-the-art information retrieval ranking systems. Knowledge embedded in such models allows them to pick up complex matching signals between passages and queries. However, the high computation cost during inference limits their deployment in real-world search scenarios. In this paper, we study if and how the knowledge for search within BERT can be transferred to a smaller ranker through distillation. Our experiments demonstrate that it is crucial to use a proper distillation procedure, which produces up to nine times speedup while preserving the state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: It is challenging to perform lifelong language learning (LLL) on a stream of different tasks without any performance degradation comparing to the multi-task counterparts. To address this issue, we present Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation (L2KD), a simple but efficient method that can be easily applied to existing LLL architectures in order to mitigate the degradation. Specifically, when the LLL model is trained on a new task, we assign a teacher model to first learn the new task, and pass the knowledge to the LLL model via knowledge distillation. Therefore, the LLL model can better adapt to the new task while keeping the previously learned knowledge. Experiments show that the proposed L2KD consistently improves previous state-of-the-art models, and the degradation comparing to multi-task models in LLL tasks is well mitigated for both sequence generation and text classification tasks.

papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: AdaBERT: Task-Adaptive BERT Compression with Differentiable Neural Architecture Search
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained language models such as BERT have shown their effectiveness in various natural language processing tasks. However, the huge parameter size makes them difficult to be deployed in real-time applications that require quick inference with limited resources. Existing methods compress BERT into small models while such compression is task-independent, i.e., the same compressed BERT for all different downstream tasks. Motivated by the necessity and benefits of task-oriented BERT compression, we propose a novel compression method, AdaBERT, that leverages differentiable Neural Architecture Search to automatically compress BERT into task-adaptive small models for specific tasks. We incorporate a task-oriented knowledge distillation loss to provide search hints and an efficiency-aware loss as search constraints, which enables a good trade-off between efficiency and effectiveness for task-adaptive BERT compression. We evaluate AdaBERT on several NLP tasks, and the results demonstrate that those task-adaptive compressed models are 12.7x to 29.3x faster than BERT in inference time and 11.5x to 17.0x smaller in terms of parameter size, while comparable performance is maintained.

papers_seen.author: Yu
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Advances and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into compact student models while maintaining or even improving performance. This approach transfers knowledge from a cumbersome teacher model to a lightweight student model, enabling efficient deployment on resource-constrained devices. The field has evolved significantly, with innovations addressing key challenges such as data augmentation strategies, multi-teacher architectures, internal representation transfer, and applications across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning. Recent developments emphasize the importance of feature-level distillation, attention mechanisms, and adversarial learning approaches for improving knowledge transfer effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Torres
papers_seen.title: The Indispensable Role of Knowledge Distillation in Modern Deep Learning: Enabling Efficient Deployment While Preserving Performance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and natural language processing. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student networks, simultaneously reducing memory footprint and inference time while maintaining competitive performance. The technique addresses critical challenges in deploying neural networks to resource-constrained environments and extends beyond simple model compression to applications in federated learning, domain adaptation, and robustness enhancement. Evidence across diverse domains demonstrates that knowledge distillation represents not merely a performance optimization technique, but a paradigm shift in how neural networks can be efficiently trained and deployed for practical real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Bowman
papers_seen.title: TRILLsson: Distilled Universal Paralinguistic Speech Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in self-supervision have dramatically improved the quality of speech representations. However, deployment of state-of-the-art embedding models on devices has been restricted due to their limited public availability and large resource footprint. Our work addresses these issues by publicly releasing a collection of paralinguistic speech models that are small and near state-of-the-art performance. Our approach is based on knowledge distillation, and our models are distilled on public data only. We explore different architectures and thoroughly evaluate our models on the Non-Semantic Speech (NOSS) benchmark. Our largest distilled model is less than 15% the size of the original model (314MB vs 2.2GB), achieves over 96% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks, and is trained on 6.5% the data. The smallest model is 1% in size (22MB) and achieves over 90% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks. Our models outperform the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 model on 6 of 7 tasks, and our smallest model outperforms the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 on both emotion recognition tasks despite being 7% the size.

papers_seen.author: Cobb
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from complex teacher networks to smaller, more deployable architectures across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks. By enabling the deployment of high-performance models in resource-constrained environments, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in practical deep learning applications while supporting various advanced objectives including robustness, fairness, and generalization.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Channel Distillation: Channel-Wise Attention for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is to transfer the knowledge from the data learned by the teacher network to the student network, so that the student has the advantage of less parameters and less calculations, and the accuracy is close to the teacher. In this paper, we propose a new distillation method, which contains two transfer distillation strategies and a loss decay strategy. The first transfer strategy is based on channel-wise attention, called Channel Distillation (CD). CD transfers the channel information from the teacher to the student. The second is Guided Knowledge Distillation (GKD). Unlike Knowledge Distillation (KD), which allows the student to mimic each sample's prediction distribution of the teacher, GKD only enables the student to mimic the correct output of the teacher. The last part is Early Decay Teacher (EDT). During the training process, we gradually decay the weight of the distillation loss. The purpose is to enable the student to gradually control the optimization rather than the teacher. Our proposed method is evaluated on ImageNet and CIFAR100. On ImageNet, we achieve 27.68% of top-1 error with ResNet18, which outperforms state-of-the-art methods. On CIFAR100, we achieve surprising result that the student outperforms the teacher. Code is available at https://github.com/zhouzaida/channel-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: BERT Learns to Teach: Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We present Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning (MetaDistil), a simple yet effective alternative to traditional knowledge distillation (KD) methods where the teacher model is fixed during training. We show the teacher network can learn to better transfer knowledge to the student network (i.e., learning to teach) with the feedback from the performance of the distilled student network in a meta learning framework. Moreover, we introduce a pilot update mechanism to improve the alignment between the inner-learner and meta-learner in meta learning algorithms that focus on an improved inner-learner. Experiments on various benchmarks show that MetaDistil can yield significant improvements compared with traditional KD algorithms and is less sensitive to the choice of different student capacity and hyperparameters, facilitating the use of KD on different tasks and models.

papers_seen.author: Richards
papers_seen.title: TextKD-GAN: Text Generation using KnowledgeDistillation and Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Text generation is of particular interest in many NLP applications such as machine translation, language modeling, and text summarization. Generative adversarial networks (GANs) achieved a remarkable success in high quality image generation in computer vision,and recently, GANs have gained lots of interest from the NLP community as well. However, achieving similar success in NLP would be more challenging due to the discrete nature of text. In this work, we introduce a method using knowledge distillation to effectively exploit GAN setup for text generation. We demonstrate how autoencoders (AEs) can be used for providing a continuous representation of sentences, which is a smooth representation that assign non-zero probabilities to more than one word. We distill this representation to train the generator to synthesize similar smooth representations. We perform a number of experiments to validate our idea using different datasets and show that our proposed approach yields better performance in terms of the BLEU score and Jensen-Shannon distance (JSD) measure compared to traditional GAN-based text generation approaches without pre-training.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful paradigm for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining performance. This approach involves training a student network to mimic the behavior of a larger teacher network, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices. Advances in knowledge distillation techniques have been applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and generative models, with innovations addressing challenges such as data scarcity, adversarial robustness, and multi-modal learning.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: DINE: Domain Adaptation from Single and Multiple Black-box Predictors
papers_seen.abstract: To ease the burden of labeling, unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) aims to transfer knowledge in previous and related labeled datasets (sources) to a new unlabeled dataset (target). Despite impressive progress, prior methods always need to access the raw source data and develop data-dependent alignment approaches to recognize the target samples in a transductive learning manner, which may raise privacy concerns from source individuals. Several recent studies resort to an alternative solution by exploiting the well-trained white-box model from the source domain, yet, it may still leak the raw data through generative adversarial learning. This paper studies a practical and interesting setting for UDA, where only black-box source models (i.e., only network predictions are available) are provided during adaptation in the target domain. To solve this problem, we propose a new two-step knowledge adaptation framework called DIstill and fine-tuNE (DINE). Taking into consideration the target data structure, DINE first distills the knowledge from the source predictor to a customized target model, then fine-tunes the distilled model to further fit the target domain. Besides, neural networks are not required to be identical across domains in DINE, even allowing effective adaptation on a low-resource device. Empirical results on three UDA scenarios (i.e., single-source, multi-source, and partial-set) confirm that DINE achieves highly competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art data-dependent approaches. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/tim-learn/DINE/}.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that enables the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student networks. This approach has become increasingly important in deep learning and natural language processing, where computational efficiency and practical deployment on resource-constrained devices are critical concerns. Knowledge distillation operates by having a student model learn from a teacher model's predictions or intermediate representations, effectively capturing the teacher's knowledge in a more compact form. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including machine translation, language understanding, visual recognition, and recommendation systems, achieving substantial reductions in model size and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance levels.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Private Model Compression via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The soaring demand for intelligent mobile applications calls for deploying powerful deep neural networks (DNNs) on mobile devices. However, the outstanding performance of DNNs notoriously relies on increasingly complex models, which in turn is associated with an increase in computational expense far surpassing mobile devices' capacity. What is worse, app service providers need to collect and utilize a large volume of users' data, which contain sensitive information, to build the sophisticated DNN models. Directly deploying these models on public mobile devices presents prohibitive privacy risk. To benefit from the on-device deep learning without the capacity and privacy concerns, we design a private model compression framework RONA. Following the knowledge distillation paradigm, we jointly use hint learning, distillation learning, and self learning to train a compact and fast neural network. The knowledge distilled from the cumbersome model is adaptively bounded and carefully perturbed to enforce differential privacy. We further propose an elegant query sample selection method to reduce the number of queries and control the privacy loss. A series of empirical evaluations as well as the implementation on an Android mobile device show that RONA can not only compress cumbersome models efficiently but also provide a strong privacy guarantee. For example, on SVHN, when a meaningful $(9.83,10^{-6})$-differential privacy is guaranteed, the compact model trained by RONA can obtain 20$\times$ compression ratio and 19$\times$ speed-up with merely 0.97% accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Higgins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Transferring Knowledge from Large Models to Efficient Student Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large teacher models to compact student networks. This approach addresses the critical challenge of deploying sophisticated neural networks in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. By leveraging the rich information encoded in teacher models, knowledge distillation provides effective compression across diverse applications including language understanding, machine translation, recommendation systems, and graph neural networks. papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Wide Neural Networks: Risk Bound, Data Efficiency and Imperfect Teacher
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a strategy of training a student network with guide of the soft output from a teacher network. It has been a successful method of model compression and knowledge transfer. However, currently knowledge distillation lacks a convincing theoretical understanding. On the other hand, recent finding on neural tangent kernel enables us to approximate a wide neural network with a linear model of the network's random features. In this paper, we theoretically analyze the knowledge distillation of a wide neural network. First we provide a transfer risk bound for the linearized model of the network. Then we propose a metric of the task's training difficulty, called data inefficiency. Based on this metric, we show that for a perfect teacher, a high ratio of teacher's soft labels can be beneficial. Finally, for the case of imperfect teacher, we find that hard labels can correct teacher's wrong prediction, which explains the practice of mixing hard and soft labels.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Adversarial Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) has made remarkable progress in the last few years and become a popular paradigm for model compression and knowledge transfer. However, almost all existing KD algorithms are data-driven, i.e., relying on a large amount of original training data or alternative data, which is usually unavailable in real-world scenarios. In this paper, we devote ourselves to this challenging problem and propose a novel adversarial distillation mechanism to craft a compact student model without any real-world data. We introduce a model discrepancy to quantificationally measure the difference between student and teacher models and construct an optimizable upper bound. In our work, the student and the teacher jointly act the role of the discriminator to reduce this discrepancy, when a generator adversarially produces some "hard samples" to enlarge it. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed data-free method yields comparable performance to existing data-driven methods. More strikingly, our approach can be directly extended to semantic segmentation, which is more complicated than classification, and our approach achieves state-of-the-art results. Code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/VainF/Data-Free-Adversarial-Distillation.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger, high-performing teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices without substantial performance degradation. Recent advances in knowledge distillation have expanded beyond simple output-level transfer to include intermediate representations, attention mechanisms, feature matching, and adversarial learning strategies. The technique has proven particularly valuable in NLP applications where pre-trained language models face computational and memory constraints, and in federated learning scenarios with heterogeneous devices. This synthesis reviews the fundamental mechanisms of knowledge distillation, its applications across different architectures and tasks, and emerging strategies for improving distillation effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: A Comprehensive Framework for Efficient Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression represent critical techniques for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, maintaining or improving performance while reducing computational costs. This paper examines the theoretical foundations and practical applications of knowledge distillation across various domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks. We argue that knowledge distillation is not merely a performance optimization technique, but a fundamental approach to understanding how neural networks learn and represent information, with broad implications for developing efficient, deployable AI systems.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression represent fundamental techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These approaches enable the transfer of knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance across diverse applications. papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Critical Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential and transformative technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, addressing critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. Applications span natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and graph neural networks, with innovations in training strategies, multi-teacher approaches, and domain-specific optimizations. The technique simultaneously reduces computational complexity, enables privacy-preserving model transfer, and improves model interpretability, establishing it as a fundamental paradigm for practical deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a training technique that transfers knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models, enabling efficient deployment of deep learning systems while maintaining competitive performance. This approach addresses critical challenges in modern machine learning by reducing computational costs, memory requirements, and inference latency. Applications span computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains including object detection, machine translation, and federated learning, demonstrating the broad applicability of knowledge distillation as a fundamental model compression technique.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These approaches enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, maintaining or improving performance while reducing computational costs and memory requirements. The techniques have been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, federated learning, and multimodal systems, addressing critical challenges in practical AI deployment.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Improved Feature Distillation via Projector Ensemble
papers_seen.abstract: In knowledge distillation, previous feature distillation methods mainly focus on the design of loss functions and the selection of the distilled layers, while the effect of the feature projector between the student and the teacher remains under-explored. In this paper, we first discuss a plausible mechanism of the projector with empirical evidence and then propose a new feature distillation method based on a projector ensemble for further performance improvement. We observe that the student network benefits from a projector even if the feature dimensions of the student and the teacher are the same. Training a student backbone without a projector can be considered as a multi-task learning process, namely achieving discriminative feature extraction for classification and feature matching between the student and the teacher for distillation at the same time. We hypothesize and empirically verify that without a projector, the student network tends to overfit the teacher's feature distributions despite having different architecture and weights initialization. This leads to degradation on the quality of the student's deep features that are eventually used in classification. Adding a projector, on the other hand, disentangles the two learning tasks and helps the student network to focus better on the main feature extraction task while still being able to utilize teacher features as a guidance through the projector. Motivated by the positive effect of the projector in feature distillation, we propose an ensemble of projectors to further improve the quality of student features. Experimental results on different datasets with a series of teacher-student pairs illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Deep Hierarchical Approach to Lifelong Learning in Minecraft
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a lifelong learning system that has the ability to reuse and transfer knowledge from one task to another while efficiently retaining the previously learned knowledge-base. Knowledge is transferred by learning reusable skills to solve tasks in Minecraft, a popular video game which is an unsolved and high-dimensional lifelong learning problem. These reusable skills, which we refer to as Deep Skill Networks, are then incorporated into our novel Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Network (H-DRLN) architecture using two techniques: (1) a deep skill array and (2) skill distillation, our novel variation of policy distillation (Rusu et. al. 2015) for learning skills. Skill distillation enables the HDRLN to efficiently retain knowledge and therefore scale in lifelong learning, by accumulating knowledge and encapsulating multiple reusable skills into a single distilled network. The H-DRLN exhibits superior performance and lower learning sample complexity compared to the regular Deep Q Network (Mnih et. al. 2015) in sub-domains of Minecraft.

papers_seen.author: Fletcher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Approaches and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying deep learning models efficiently in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Compressing Deep Graph Neural Networks via Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep graph neural networks (GNNs) have been shown to be expressive for modeling graph-structured data. Nevertheless, the over-stacked architecture of deep graph models makes it difficult to deploy and rapidly test on mobile or embedded systems. To compress over-stacked GNNs, knowledge distillation via a teacher-student architecture turns out to be an effective technique, where the key step is to measure the discrepancy between teacher and student networks with predefined distance functions. However, using the same distance for graphs of various structures may be unfit, and the optimal distance formulation is hard to determine. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel Adversarial Knowledge Distillation framework for graph models named GraphAKD, which adversarially trains a discriminator and a generator to adaptively detect and decrease the discrepancy. Specifically, noticing that the well-captured inter-node and inter-class correlations favor the success of deep GNNs, we propose to criticize the inherited knowledge from node-level and class-level views with a trainable discriminator. The discriminator distinguishes between teacher knowledge and what the student inherits, while the student GNN works as a generator and aims to fool the discriminator. To our best knowledge, GraphAKD is the first to introduce adversarial training to knowledge distillation in graph domains. Experiments on node-level and graph-level classification benchmarks demonstrate that GraphAKD improves the student performance by a large margin. The results imply that GraphAKD can precisely transfer knowledge from a complicated teacher GNN to a compact student GNN.

papers_seen.author: Conner
papers_seen.title: Distilling Task-Specific Knowledge from BERT into Simple Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: In the natural language processing literature, neural networks are becoming increasingly deeper and complex. The recent poster child of this trend is the deep language representation model, which includes BERT, ELMo, and GPT. These developments have led to the conviction that previous-generation, shallower neural networks for language understanding are obsolete. In this paper, however, we demonstrate that rudimentary, lightweight neural networks can still be made competitive without architecture changes, external training data, or additional input features. We propose to distill knowledge from BERT, a state-of-the-art language representation model, into a single-layer BiLSTM, as well as its siamese counterpart for sentence-pair tasks. Across multiple datasets in paraphrasing, natural language inference, and sentiment classification, we achieve comparable results with ELMo, while using roughly 100 times fewer parameters and 15 times less inference time.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Critical Approach to Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents the most practical and effective approach to model compression across deep learning and natural language processing applications. By enabling strategic knowledge transfer from teacher models to student models, distillation achieves substantial reductions in model size, computational requirements, and memory footprint while preserving the learned capabilities essential for real-world deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Orr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Techniques, Applications, and Advances
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation addresses fundamental challenges in model deployment across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks. Recent advances extend beyond traditional probability matching to encompass feature-level transfer, task-aware compression, and novel distillation frameworks that improve efficiency without substantial accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Velasquez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and transformative technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, resource-efficient student models, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices without significant accuracy degradation. The method extends across multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, federated learning, and speech recognition, addressing critical challenges of computational efficiency, memory footprint, and inference latency in modern deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Frost
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient architectures, making it particularly valuable for both deep learning and natural language processing applications. By enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in computational efficiency, memory requirements, and inference speed. Recent advances demonstrate diverse applications across multiple domains and introduce sophisticated distillation strategies beyond simple output-level matching.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Comprehensive Overview of Techniques and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a pivotal technique for model compression in deep learning, enabling the transfer of learned representations from large, computationally expensive teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach is particularly valuable for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments while maintaining predictive performance. The field encompasses diverse applications from computer vision to natural language processing, with innovations in feature-level distillation, adversarial learning strategies, and zero-shot compression methods. Theoretical understanding of why distillation works, combined with practical advancements in distillation strategies, has made this technique essential for modern deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become critical techniques for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, compute-intensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This paper synthesizes recent advances in knowledge distillation and compression, examining their applications across natural language processing, computer vision, federated learning, and domain-specific tasks. The evidence demonstrates that knowledge distillation is highly effective for model compression, though successful implementation requires careful consideration of distillation strategy, teacher selection, and task-aware design choices.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Understanding BERT Rankers Under Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep language models such as BERT pre-trained on large corpus have given a huge performance boost to the state-of-the-art information retrieval ranking systems. Knowledge embedded in such models allows them to pick up complex matching signals between passages and queries. However, the high computation cost during inference limits their deployment in real-world search scenarios. In this paper, we study if and how the knowledge for search within BERT can be transferred to a smaller ranker through distillation. Our experiments demonstrate that it is crucial to use a proper distillation procedure, which produces up to nine times speedup while preserving the state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Beck
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Strategic Approach to Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression represent essential techniques for deploying sophisticated neural networks in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. These methods transfer knowledge from large, complex teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student models, addressing critical challenges in practical deep learning applications. This paper examines the theoretical foundations, diverse applications, and empirical considerations surrounding knowledge distillation across natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Powerful Strategy for Neural Network Compression and Transfer Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining performance. This approach involves transferring knowledge from a large teacher network to a smaller student network through various mechanisms, including soft label matching, attention-based feature transfer, and meta-learning frameworks. Knowledge distillation has proven effective across diverse applications including natural language processing, computer vision, and complex reasoning tasks. The technique addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning models to resource-constrained environments while enabling faster inference times and reduced parameter requirements. Recent advances have extended distillation beyond simple probability matching to encompass layer-wise information transfer, task-adaptive compression, and collaborative learning schemes.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge From a Deep Pose Regressor Network
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a novel method to distill knowledge from a deep pose regressor network for efficient Visual Odometry (VO). Standard distillation relies on "dark knowledge" for successful knowledge transfer. As this knowledge is not available in pose regression and the teacher prediction is not always accurate, we propose to emphasize the knowledge transfer only when we trust the teacher. We achieve this by using teacher loss as a confidence score which places variable relative importance on the teacher prediction. We inject this confidence score to the main training task via Attentive Imitation Loss (AIL) and when learning the intermediate representation of the teacher through Attentive Hint Training (AHT) approach. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work which successfully distill the knowledge from a deep pose regression network. Our evaluation on the KITTI and Malaga dataset shows that we can keep the student prediction close to the teacher with up to 92.95% parameter reduction and 2.12x faster in computation time.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.author: Walls
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Approaches and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying efficient neural networks across diverse domains. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from larger, complex teacher models to smaller, lightweight student models while maintaining or improving performance. This synthesis examines the current state of knowledge distillation techniques, their applications to natural language processing and computer vision tasks, and recent innovations in multi-teacher frameworks and domain-specific approaches. The research demonstrates that knowledge distillation provides a flexible and practical solution for reducing computational costs and memory requirements in both discriminative and generative models, with particular success in transformer-based language models, neural machine translation, and graph neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Galloway
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Principles, Applications, and Advances in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful paradigm for training compact neural networks by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models. This approach enables efficient model deployment while maintaining performance across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized tasks. Recent developments have expanded knowledge distillation beyond simple logit matching to encompass feature-level transfer, adversarial training, and meta-learning frameworks, making it an increasingly versatile compression technique for modern deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Aguirre
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from a large, complex teacher model to a smaller, more efficient student model. This approach has become increasingly important for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments and for improving model efficiency across various tasks including image classification, object detection, natural language processing, and speech recognition. The technique enables significant reductions in model size and inference time while maintaining competitive performance with the original teacher model. Applications span from compressing pre-trained language models like BERT to developing efficient detectors for autonomous systems, with various methodological innovations addressing different challenges in the knowledge transfer process.

papers_seen.author: Walsh
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, complex teacher networks to smaller student networks, enabling efficient deployment in resource-constrained environments. This approach has become fundamental in deep learning and natural language processing, addressing critical challenges of computational cost and model size reduction. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including image classification, object detection, machine translation, and reading comprehension, demonstrating its versatility in creating deployable models while maintaining competitive performance.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Less is More: Task-aware Layer-wise Distillation for Language Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Layer-wise distillation is a powerful tool to compress large models (i.e. teacher models) into small ones (i.e., student models). The student distills knowledge from the teacher by mimicking the hidden representations of the teacher at every intermediate layer. However, layer-wise distillation is difficult. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Task-aware layEr-wise Distillation (TED). TED designs task-aware filters to align the hidden representations of the student and the teacher at each layer. The filters select the knowledge that is useful for the target task from the hidden representations. As such, TED reduces the knowledge gap between the two models and helps the student to fit better on the target task. We evaluate TED in two scenarios: continual pre-training and fine-tuning. TED demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over existing distillation methods in both scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/cliang1453/task-aware-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Critical Approach to Efficient Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from teacher models to student models across diverse applications in natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains. The technique encompasses various methodologies including output-level distillation, feature-based approaches, and task-aware strategies. Evidence demonstrates that distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments while addressing computational overhead and memory limitations without substantial accuracy losses.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Compressing GANs using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been used in several machine learning tasks such as domain transfer, super resolution, and synthetic data generation. State-of-the-art GANs often use tens of millions of parameters, making them expensive to deploy for applications in low SWAP (size, weight, and power) hardware, such as mobile devices, and for applications with real time capabilities. There has been no work found to reduce the number of parameters used in GANs. Therefore, we propose a method to compress GANs using knowledge distillation techniques, in which a smaller "student" GAN learns to mimic a larger "teacher" GAN. We show that the distillation methods used on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Celeb-A datasets can compress teacher GANs at ratios of 1669:1, 58:1, and 87:1, respectively, while retaining the quality of the generated image. From our experiments, we observe a qualitative limit for GAN's compression. Moreover, we observe that, with a fixed parameter budget, compressed GANs outperform GANs trained using standard training methods. We conjecture that this is partially owing to the optimization landscape of over-parameterized GANs which allows efficient training using alternating gradient descent. Thus, training an over-parameterized GAN followed by our proposed compression scheme provides a high quality generative model with a small number of parameters.

papers_seen.author: Harvey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression techniques have emerged as critical approaches for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments while maintaining predictive performance. This synthesis examines how these techniques leverage teacher-student frameworks to transfer knowledge from larger, more complex models to smaller, more efficient ones across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks. Key findings reveal the mechanisms by which soft labels facilitate knowledge transfer, the bias-variance tradeoffs involved in distillation, and practical applications in accelerating inference for real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: House
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Critical Technique for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models without substantial performance loss. This technique transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive accuracy. Knowledge distillation is particularly valuable in natural language processing, where modern pre-trained models like BERT impose significant computational burdens for inference. Beyond compression, distillation serves broader purposes including domain adaptation, heterogeneous federated learning, and improved model generalization. The versatility and effectiveness of knowledge distillation across diverse applications demonstrate its importance as a foundational technique in modern deep learning.

papers_seen.author: Powers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Essential Technique for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for compressing large neural networks into efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. Rather than being merely a supplementary compression method, knowledge distillation represents a fundamental paradigm shift in how we approach model training and deployment. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be considered not simply as model compression, but as a versatile learning framework applicable across diverse architectures, domains, and tasks in both computer vision and natural language processing. The evidence demonstrates that distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments while maintaining substantial performance gains, and its mechanisms reveal deeper insights about regularization and learning dynamics.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Releasing Graph Neural Networks with Differential Privacy Guarantees
papers_seen.abstract: With the increasing popularity of graph neural networks (GNNs) in several sensitive applications like healthcare and medicine, concerns have been raised over the privacy aspects of trained GNNs. More notably, GNNs are vulnerable to privacy attacks, such as membership inference attacks, even if only black-box access to the trained model is granted. We propose PrivGNN, a privacy-preserving framework for releasing GNN models in a centralized setting. Assuming an access to a public unlabeled graph, PrivGNN provides a framework to release GNN models trained explicitly on public data along with knowledge obtained from the private data in a privacy preserving manner. PrivGNN combines the knowledge-distillation framework with the two noise mechanisms, random subsampling, and noisy labeling, to ensure rigorous privacy guarantees. We theoretically analyze our approach in the Renyi differential privacy framework. Besides, we show the solid experimental performance of our method compared to several baselines adapted for graph-structured data. Our code is available at https://github.com/iyempissy/privGnn.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining high performance. This approach transfers knowledge from a large, well-trained teacher network to a smaller student network, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices. The method has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, healthcare, and recommendation systems, addressing key challenges of inference latency, computational efficiency, and model interpretability.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining performance. This approach involves training a smaller student network to mimic the predictions and representations of a larger teacher network. Applications span multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, generative models, and graph neural networks. Distillation methods vary significantly in their approach, from simple output matching to sophisticated layer-wise knowledge transfer mechanisms. Recent advances focus on handling multiple teachers, improving theoretical understanding, and addressing challenges in specific domains such as object detection and machine reading comprehension.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: ALP-KD: Attention-Based Layer Projection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is considered as a training and compression strategy in which two neural networks, namely a teacher and a student, are coupled together during training. The teacher network is supposed to be a trustworthy predictor and the student tries to mimic its predictions. Usually, a student with a lighter architecture is selected so we can achieve compression and yet deliver high-quality results. In such a setting, distillation only happens for final predictions whereas the student could also benefit from teacher's supervision for internal components.   Motivated by this, we studied the problem of distillation for intermediate layers. Since there might not be a one-to-one alignment between student and teacher layers, existing techniques skip some teacher layers and only distill from a subset of them. This shortcoming directly impacts quality, so we instead propose a combinatorial technique which relies on attention. Our model fuses teacher-side information and takes each layer's significance into consideration, then performs distillation between combined teacher layers and those of the student. Using our technique, we distilled a 12-layer BERT (Devlin et al. 2019) into 6-, 4-, and 2-layer counterparts and evaluated them on GLUE tasks (Wang et al. 2018). Experimental results show that our combinatorial approach is able to outperform other existing techniques.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-adopted technique for model compression that enables the training of efficient student models by transferring knowledge from larger, more powerful teacher models. This approach has become fundamental in deep learning and natural language processing, addressing the critical challenge of deploying high-performance models under computational constraints. Knowledge distillation methods transfer various types of knowledge including soft logits, intermediate feature representations, and attention patterns, enabling significant model size reduction while maintaining competitive accuracy across diverse applications including computer vision, machine translation, speech recognition, and recommendation systems.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Powerful Strategy for Neural Network Compression and Transfer Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining performance. This approach involves transferring knowledge from a large teacher network to a smaller student network through various mechanisms, including soft label matching, attention-based feature transfer, and meta-learning frameworks. Knowledge distillation has proven effective across diverse applications including natural language processing, computer vision, and complex reasoning tasks. The technique addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning models to resource-constrained environments while enabling faster inference times and reduced parameter requirements. Recent advances have extended distillation beyond simple probability matching to encompass layer-wise information transfer, task-adaptive compression, and collaborative learning schemes.

papers_seen.author: Kidd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Strategic Transfer of Learning from Large to Small Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful paradigm for model compression that enables the transfer of knowledge from large teacher networks to smaller student models. This approach addresses critical challenges in deploying deep neural networks across resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. Through strategic knowledge transfer mechanisms, distillation techniques have proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal learning. The success of these methods relies on sophisticated mechanisms for capturing and transferring both task-relevant information and feature representations. Modern distillation frameworks continue to evolve, incorporating adaptive weighting schemes, layer-wise knowledge transfer, and adversarial learning strategies to maximize compression efficiency while minimizing performance degradation.

papers_seen.author: Mason
papers_seen.title: Learning Student Networks via Feature Embedding
papers_seen.abstract: Deep convolutional neural networks have been widely used in numerous applications, but their demanding storage and computational resource requirements prevent their applications on mobile devices. Knowledge distillation aims to optimize a portable student network by taking the knowledge from a well-trained heavy teacher network. Traditional teacher-student based methods used to rely on additional fully-connected layers to bridge intermediate layers of teacher and student networks, which brings in a large number of auxiliary parameters. In contrast, this paper aims to propagate information from teacher to student without introducing new variables which need to be optimized. We regard the teacher-student paradigm from a new perspective of feature embedding. By introducing the locality preserving loss, the student network is encouraged to generate the low-dimensional features which could inherit intrinsic properties of their corresponding high-dimensional features from teacher network. The resulting portable network thus can naturally maintain the performance as that of the teacher network. Theoretical analysis is provided to justify the lower computation complexity of the proposed method. Experiments on benchmark datasets and well-trained networks suggest that the proposed algorithm is superior to state-of-the-art teacher-student learning methods in terms of computational and storage complexity.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from larger, more capable teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach has become increasingly important for deploying deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation operates by leveraging various forms of knowledge from teachers, including output predictions, intermediate representations, and behavioral patterns, to train compact student models that maintain competitive performance while significantly reducing computational and memory requirements. Applications span multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, recommender systems, and reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Comprehensive Overview of Techniques and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a pivotal technique for model compression in deep learning, enabling the transfer of learned representations from large, computationally expensive teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach is particularly valuable for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments while maintaining predictive performance. The field encompasses diverse applications from computer vision to natural language processing, with innovations in feature-level distillation, adversarial learning strategies, and zero-shot compression methods. Theoretical understanding of why distillation works, combined with practical advancements in distillation strategies, has made this technique essential for modern deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Does Knowledge Distillation Really Work?
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique for training a small student network to emulate a larger teacher model, such as an ensemble of networks. We show that while knowledge distillation can improve student generalization, it does not typically work as it is commonly understood: there often remains a surprisingly large discrepancy between the predictive distributions of the teacher and the student, even in cases when the student has the capacity to perfectly match the teacher. We identify difficulties in optimization as a key reason for why the student is unable to match the teacher. We also show how the details of the dataset used for distillation play a role in how closely the student matches the teacher -- and that more closely matching the teacher paradoxically does not always lead to better student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Learning Compact Metrics for MT
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in machine translation and multilingual text generation have led researchers to adopt trained metrics such as COMET or BLEURT, which treat evaluation as a regression problem and use representations from multilingual pre-trained models such as XLM-RoBERTa or mBERT. Yet studies on related tasks suggest that these models are most efficient when they are large, which is costly and impractical for evaluation. We investigate the trade-off between multilinguality and model capacity with RemBERT, a state-of-the-art multilingual language model, using data from the WMT Metrics Shared Task. We present a series of experiments which show that model size is indeed a bottleneck for cross-lingual transfer, then demonstrate how distillation can help addressing this bottleneck, by leveraging synthetic data generation and transferring knowledge from one teacher to multiple students trained on related languages. Our method yields up to 10.5% improvement over vanilla fine-tuning and reaches 92.6% of RemBERT's performance using only a third of its parameters.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining predictive performance. papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Approaches and Applications
