These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation operates through various mechanisms including output probability matching, intermediate representation alignment, and relational information transfer. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, recommender systems, and graph neural networks. Recent advances have extended the approach to address specialized challenges such as fairness, heterogeneous device deployment, and data-free scenarios, establishing knowledge distillation as a fundamental paradigm for creating practical, deployable AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-adopted technique for model compression that enables the training of efficient student models by transferring knowledge from larger, more powerful teacher models. This approach has become fundamental in deep learning and natural language processing, addressing the critical challenge of deploying high-performance models under computational constraints. Knowledge distillation methods transfer various types of knowledge including soft logits, intermediate feature representations, and attention patterns, enabling significant model size reduction while maintaining competitive accuracy across diverse applications including computer vision, machine translation, speech recognition, and recommendation systems.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression represent fundamental techniques for deploying deep neural networks efficiently across resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while preserving or enhancing predictive performance. This synthesis examines the core mechanisms, diverse applications, and innovations in knowledge distillation across domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks, demonstrating how distillation functions as both a compression technique and a powerful regularization mechanism.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful paradigm for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining performance. This approach involves training a student network to mimic the behavior of a larger teacher network, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices. Advances in knowledge distillation techniques have been applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and generative models, with innovations addressing challenges such as data scarcity, adversarial robustness, and multi-modal learning.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Powerful Strategy for Neural Network Compression and Transfer Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining performance. This approach involves transferring knowledge from a large teacher network to a smaller student network through various mechanisms, including soft label matching, attention-based feature transfer, and meta-learning frameworks. Knowledge distillation has proven effective across diverse applications including natural language processing, computer vision, and complex reasoning tasks. The technique addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning models to resource-constrained environments while enabling faster inference times and reduced parameter requirements. Recent advances have extended distillation beyond simple probability matching to encompass layer-wise information transfer, task-adaptive compression, and collaborative learning schemes.

papers_seen.author: Ortiz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as Essential Compression: Reconciling Theory and Practice in Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for deploying large neural networks on resource-constrained devices by enabling smaller student models to learn from larger teacher models. While the technique achieves significant reductions in model size and inference time, there remains considerable debate about how and why distillation works. This position argues that knowledge distillation is not merely a performance-preservation technique, but rather functions as a powerful form of learned regularization that offers benefits extending far beyond simple compression, including improved robustness and fairness, making it essential for practical deep learning deployment across diverse domains.

papers_seen.author: Beck
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Strategic Approach to Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression represent essential techniques for deploying sophisticated neural networks in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. These methods transfer knowledge from large, complex teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student models, addressing critical challenges in practical deep learning applications. This paper examines the theoretical foundations, diverse applications, and empirical considerations surrounding knowledge distillation across natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Collaborative Distillation for Ultra-Resolution Universal Style Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Universal style transfer methods typically leverage rich representations from deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (e.g., VGG-19) pre-trained on large collections of images. Despite the effectiveness, its application is heavily constrained by the large model size to handle ultra-resolution images given limited memory. In this work, we present a new knowledge distillation method (named Collaborative Distillation) for encoder-decoder based neural style transfer to reduce the convolutional filters. The main idea is underpinned by a finding that the encoder-decoder pairs construct an exclusive collaborative relationship, which is regarded as a new kind of knowledge for style transfer models. Moreover, to overcome the feature size mismatch when applying collaborative distillation, a linear embedding loss is introduced to drive the student network to learn a linear embedding of the teacher's features. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method when applied to different universal style transfer approaches (WCT and AdaIN), even if the model size is reduced by 15.5 times. Especially, on WCT with the compressed models, we achieve ultra-resolution (over 40 megapixels) universal style transfer on a 12GB GPU for the first time. Further experiments on optimization-based stylization scheme show the generality of our algorithm on different stylization paradigms. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/mingsun-tse/collaborative-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger, high-performing teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices without substantial performance degradation. Recent advances in knowledge distillation have expanded beyond simple output-level transfer to include intermediate representations, attention mechanisms, feature matching, and adversarial learning strategies. The technique has proven particularly valuable in NLP applications where pre-trained language models face computational and memory constraints, and in federated learning scenarios with heterogeneous devices. This synthesis reviews the fundamental mechanisms of knowledge distillation, its applications across different architectures and tasks, and emerging strategies for improving distillation effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning in Resource-Constrained Environments
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span computer vision, natural language processing, federated learning, and specialized domains such as recommender systems and graph neural networks. Recent advances include intermediate layer distillation, attention-based mechanisms, and task-adaptive compression strategies that further enhance the effectiveness of knowledge transfer.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from larger, more expressive teacher models to smaller student networks while maintaining competitive performance. This synthesis examines the theoretical foundations, methodological advances, and practical applications of knowledge distillation across computer vision and natural language processing tasks, including recent developments in handling soft labels, intermediate feature representations, and domain-specific adaptations.

papers_seen.author: Shaffer
papers_seen.title: Selective Knowledge Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Neural Machine Translation (NMT) models achieve state-of-the-art performance on many translation benchmarks. As an active research field in NMT, knowledge distillation is widely applied to enhance the model's performance by transferring teacher model's knowledge on each training sample. However, previous work rarely discusses the different impacts and connections among these samples, which serve as the medium for transferring teacher knowledge. In this paper, we design a novel protocol that can effectively analyze the different impacts of samples by comparing various samples' partitions. Based on above protocol, we conduct extensive experiments and find that the teacher's knowledge is not the more, the better. Knowledge over specific samples may even hurt the whole performance of knowledge distillation. Finally, to address these issues, we propose two simple yet effective strategies, i.e., batch-level and global-level selections, to pick suitable samples for distillation. We evaluate our approaches on two large-scale machine translation tasks, WMT'14 English->German and WMT'19 Chinese->English. Experimental results show that our approaches yield up to +1.28 and +0.89 BLEU points improvements over the Transformer baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Walsh
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, complex teacher networks to smaller student networks, enabling efficient deployment in resource-constrained environments. This approach has become fundamental in deep learning and natural language processing, addressing critical challenges of computational cost and model size reduction. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including image classification, object detection, machine translation, and reading comprehension, demonstrating its versatility in creating deployable models while maintaining competitive performance.

papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: AdaBERT: Task-Adaptive BERT Compression with Differentiable Neural Architecture Search
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained language models such as BERT have shown their effectiveness in various natural language processing tasks. However, the huge parameter size makes them difficult to be deployed in real-time applications that require quick inference with limited resources. Existing methods compress BERT into small models while such compression is task-independent, i.e., the same compressed BERT for all different downstream tasks. Motivated by the necessity and benefits of task-oriented BERT compression, we propose a novel compression method, AdaBERT, that leverages differentiable Neural Architecture Search to automatically compress BERT into task-adaptive small models for specific tasks. We incorporate a task-oriented knowledge distillation loss to provide search hints and an efficiency-aware loss as search constraints, which enables a good trade-off between efficiency and effectiveness for task-adaptive BERT compression. We evaluate AdaBERT on several NLP tasks, and the results demonstrate that those task-adaptive compressed models are 12.7x to 29.3x faster than BERT in inference time and 11.5x to 17.0x smaller in terms of parameter size, while comparable performance is maintained.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Enabling Efficient Deep Learning Through Targeted Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining performance. This approach transfers knowledge from a larger teacher network to a more compact student network, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices without sacrificing accuracy. Beyond traditional compression applications, knowledge distillation has been successfully extended to diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, domain adaptation, and privacy-preserving machine learning, demonstrating its versatility and effectiveness as a fundamental technique for efficient deep learning.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying large neural networks on resource-constrained devices. These methods enable smaller student models to learn from larger, more capable teacher models, achieving significant reductions in model size and inference time while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and graph neural networks, with various approaches addressing challenges such as heterogeneous architectures, domain adaptation, and ensemble compression.

papers_seen.author: Fisher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying large neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining performance. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, these approaches enable significant reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference latency. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents an essential paradigm for making state-of-the-art deep learning models practical and accessible across diverse applications including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Adaptation: Teaching to Adapt
papers_seen.abstract: Domain adaptation is crucial in many real-world applications where the distribution of the training data differs from the distribution of the test data. Previous Deep Learning-based approaches to domain adaptation need to be trained jointly on source and target domain data and are therefore unappealing in scenarios where models need to be adapted to a large number of domains or where a domain is evolving, e.g. spam detection where attackers continuously change their tactics.   To fill this gap, we propose Knowledge Adaptation, an extension of Knowledge Distillation (Bucilua et al., 2006; Hinton et al., 2015) to the domain adaptation scenario. We show how a student model achieves state-of-the-art results on unsupervised domain adaptation from multiple sources on a standard sentiment analysis benchmark by taking into account the domain-specific expertise of multiple teachers and the similarities between their domains.   When learning from a single teacher, using domain similarity to gauge trustworthiness is inadequate. To this end, we propose a simple metric that correlates well with the teacher's accuracy in the target domain. We demonstrate that incorporating high-confidence examples selected by this metric enables the student model to achieve state-of-the-art performance in the single-source scenario.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: R2L: Distilling Neural Radiance Field to Neural Light Field for Efficient Novel View Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Recent research explosion on Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) shows the encouraging potential to represent complex scenes with neural networks. One major drawback of NeRF is its prohibitive inference time: Rendering a single pixel requires querying the NeRF network hundreds of times. To resolve it, existing efforts mainly attempt to reduce the number of required sampled points. However, the problem of iterative sampling still exists. On the other hand, Neural Light Field (NeLF) presents a more straightforward representation over NeRF in novel view synthesis -- the rendering of a pixel amounts to one single forward pass without ray-marching. In this work, we present a deep residual MLP network (88 layers) to effectively learn the light field. We show the key to successfully learning such a deep NeLF network is to have sufficient data, for which we transfer the knowledge from a pre-trained NeRF model via data distillation. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world scenes show the merits of our method over other counterpart algorithms. On the synthetic scenes, we achieve 26-35x FLOPs reduction (per camera ray) and 28-31x runtime speedup, meanwhile delivering significantly better (1.4-2.8 dB average PSNR improvement) rendering quality than NeRF without any customized parallelism requirement.

papers_seen.author: Rios
papers_seen.title: Improving Neural Topic Models using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Topic models are often used to identify human-interpretable topics to help make sense of large document collections. We use knowledge distillation to combine the best attributes of probabilistic topic models and pretrained transformers. Our modular method can be straightforwardly applied with any neural topic model to improve topic quality, which we demonstrate using two models having disparate architectures, obtaining state-of-the-art topic coherence. We show that our adaptable framework not only improves performance in the aggregate over all estimated topics, as is commonly reported, but also in head-to-head comparisons of aligned topics.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Transformative Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and transformative technique for compressing large neural networks and transferring knowledge from complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems, including computational efficiency, memory footprint reduction, and inference latency, while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and federated learning, demonstrating the broad applicability and essential role of knowledge distillation in modern machine learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Mueller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression and efficient deployment of deep learning systems. This approach involves training a smaller, lightweight student model to match the predictions of a larger, more complex teacher model, enabling significant reductions in computational cost and model size while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, reinforcement learning, and beyond, demonstrating its versatility as a general-purpose compression technique.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student networks. This approach has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and federated learning. By leveraging soft target probabilities and intermediate representations from teachers, knowledge distillation achieves significant reductions in model size and computational cost while maintaining competitive performance. Recent advances have extended the technique to address challenges such as data-free distillation, adversarial robustness, heterogeneous models, and task-specific compression. The method has proven particularly valuable for deploying neural networks on resource-constrained devices and enabling real-time inference in practical applications.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Model Compression with Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation for Web Question Answering System
papers_seen.abstract: Deep pre-training and fine-tuning models (such as BERT and OpenAI GPT) have demonstrated excellent results in question answering areas. However, due to the sheer amount of model parameters, the inference speed of these models is very slow. How to apply these complex models to real business scenarios becomes a challenging but practical problem. Previous model compression methods usually suffer from information loss during the model compression procedure, leading to inferior models compared with the original one. To tackle this challenge, we propose a Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (TMKD for short) method for web Question Answering system. We first develop a general Q\&A distillation task for student model pre-training, and further fine-tune this pre-trained student model with multi-teacher knowledge distillation on downstream tasks (like Web Q\&A task, MNLI, SNLI, RTE tasks from GLUE), which effectively reduces the overfitting bias in individual teacher models, and transfers more general knowledge to the student model. The experiment results show that our method can significantly outperform the baseline methods and even achieve comparable results with the original teacher models, along with substantial speedup of model inference.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.author: Henson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Comprehensive Approach to Efficient Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining or improving performance. This approach enables deployment of sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across diverse applications including natural language processing, computer vision, and generative models. By transferring knowledge from teacher models to compact student networks, distillation addresses critical challenges in computational efficiency, inference latency, and practical deployment while preserving predictive accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: ALP-KD: Attention-Based Layer Projection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is considered as a training and compression strategy in which two neural networks, namely a teacher and a student, are coupled together during training. The teacher network is supposed to be a trustworthy predictor and the student tries to mimic its predictions. Usually, a student with a lighter architecture is selected so we can achieve compression and yet deliver high-quality results. In such a setting, distillation only happens for final predictions whereas the student could also benefit from teacher's supervision for internal components.   Motivated by this, we studied the problem of distillation for intermediate layers. Since there might not be a one-to-one alignment between student and teacher layers, existing techniques skip some teacher layers and only distill from a subset of them. This shortcoming directly impacts quality, so we instead propose a combinatorial technique which relies on attention. Our model fuses teacher-side information and takes each layer's significance into consideration, then performs distillation between combined teacher layers and those of the student. Using our technique, we distilled a 12-layer BERT (Devlin et al. 2019) into 6-, 4-, and 2-layer counterparts and evaluated them on GLUE tasks (Wang et al. 2018). Experimental results show that our combinatorial approach is able to outperform other existing techniques.

papers_seen.author: Allison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Fundamental Technique for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and natural language processing. This paper argues that knowledge distillation enables the creation of efficient, deployable models without sacrificing performance through strategic knowledge transfer from larger teacher networks to compact student networks. Beyond traditional compression, knowledge distillation extends to specialized domains including continual learning, privacy-preserving applications, and task-specific adaptation, demonstrating its versatility and fundamental importance in modern machine learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Compression of Deep Learning Models for Text: A Survey
papers_seen.abstract: In recent years, the fields of natural language processing (NLP) and information retrieval (IR) have made tremendous progress thanksto deep learning models like Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTMs)networks, and Transformer [120] based models like Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) [24], GenerativePre-training Transformer (GPT-2) [94], Multi-task Deep Neural Network (MT-DNN) [73], Extra-Long Network (XLNet) [134], Text-to-text transfer transformer (T5) [95], T-NLG [98] and GShard [63]. But these models are humongous in size. On the other hand,real world applications demand small model size, low response times and low computational power wattage. In this survey, wediscuss six different types of methods (Pruning, Quantization, Knowledge Distillation, Parameter Sharing, Tensor Decomposition, andSub-quadratic Transformer based methods) for compression of such models to enable their deployment in real industry NLP projects.Given the critical need of building applications with efficient and small models, and the large amount of recently published work inthis area, we believe that this survey organizes the plethora of work done by the 'deep learning for NLP' community in the past fewyears and presents it as a coherent story.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Advancing Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving performance. This approach transfers knowledge from a larger teacher model to a smaller student model, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices without sacrificing accuracy. The method extends across multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and federated learning, with applications ranging from mobile deployment to privacy-preserving distributed systems.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Collaborative Distillation for Ultra-Resolution Universal Style Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Universal style transfer methods typically leverage rich representations from deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (e.g., VGG-19) pre-trained on large collections of images. Despite the effectiveness, its application is heavily constrained by the large model size to handle ultra-resolution images given limited memory. In this work, we present a new knowledge distillation method (named Collaborative Distillation) for encoder-decoder based neural style transfer to reduce the convolutional filters. The main idea is underpinned by a finding that the encoder-decoder pairs construct an exclusive collaborative relationship, which is regarded as a new kind of knowledge for style transfer models. Moreover, to overcome the feature size mismatch when applying collaborative distillation, a linear embedding loss is introduced to drive the student network to learn a linear embedding of the teacher's features. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method when applied to different universal style transfer approaches (WCT and AdaIN), even if the model size is reduced by 15.5 times. Especially, on WCT with the compressed models, we achieve ultra-resolution (over 40 megapixels) universal style transfer on a 12GB GPU for the first time. Further experiments on optimization-based stylization scheme show the generality of our algorithm on different stylization paradigms. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/mingsun-tse/collaborative-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Freeman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from complex teacher models to compact student networks, addressing critical deployment challenges including computational efficiency, memory requirements, and inference latency. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized areas such as federated learning and graph neural networks, making it an indispensable tool in modern deep learning practice.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Towards Understanding Ensemble, Knowledge Distillation and Self-Distillation in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We formally study how ensemble of deep learning models can improve test accuracy, and how the superior performance of ensemble can be distilled into a single model using knowledge distillation. We consider the challenging case where the ensemble is simply an average of the outputs of a few independently trained neural networks with the SAME architecture, trained using the SAME algorithm on the SAME data set, and they only differ by the random seeds used in the initialization.   We show that ensemble/knowledge distillation in Deep Learning works very differently from traditional learning theory (such as boosting or NTKs, neural tangent kernels). To properly understand them, we develop a theory showing that when data has a structure we refer to as ``multi-view'', then ensemble of independently trained neural networks can provably improve test accuracy, and such superior test accuracy can also be provably distilled into a single model by training a single model to match the output of the ensemble instead of the true label. Our result sheds light on how ensemble works in deep learning in a way that is completely different from traditional theorems, and how the ``dark knowledge'' is hidden in the outputs of the ensemble and can be used in distillation. In the end, we prove that self-distillation can also be viewed as implicitly combining ensemble and knowledge distillation to improve test accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge From a Deep Pose Regressor Network
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a novel method to distill knowledge from a deep pose regressor network for efficient Visual Odometry (VO). Standard distillation relies on "dark knowledge" for successful knowledge transfer. As this knowledge is not available in pose regression and the teacher prediction is not always accurate, we propose to emphasize the knowledge transfer only when we trust the teacher. We achieve this by using teacher loss as a confidence score which places variable relative importance on the teacher prediction. We inject this confidence score to the main training task via Attentive Imitation Loss (AIL) and when learning the intermediate representation of the teacher through Attentive Hint Training (AHT) approach. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work which successfully distill the knowledge from a deep pose regression network. Our evaluation on the KITTI and Malaga dataset shows that we can keep the student prediction close to the teacher with up to 92.95% parameter reduction and 2.12x faster in computation time.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Releasing Graph Neural Networks with Differential Privacy Guarantees
papers_seen.abstract: With the increasing popularity of graph neural networks (GNNs) in several sensitive applications like healthcare and medicine, concerns have been raised over the privacy aspects of trained GNNs. More notably, GNNs are vulnerable to privacy attacks, such as membership inference attacks, even if only black-box access to the trained model is granted. We propose PrivGNN, a privacy-preserving framework for releasing GNN models in a centralized setting. Assuming an access to a public unlabeled graph, PrivGNN provides a framework to release GNN models trained explicitly on public data along with knowledge obtained from the private data in a privacy preserving manner. PrivGNN combines the knowledge-distillation framework with the two noise mechanisms, random subsampling, and noisy labeling, to ensure rigorous privacy guarantees. We theoretically analyze our approach in the Renyi differential privacy framework. Besides, we show the solid experimental performance of our method compared to several baselines adapted for graph-structured data. Our code is available at https://github.com/iyempissy/privGnn.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Transformative Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and transformative technique for compressing large neural networks and transferring knowledge from complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems, including computational efficiency, memory footprint reduction, and inference latency, while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and federated learning, demonstrating the broad applicability and essential role of knowledge distillation in modern machine learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Apprentice: Using Knowledge Distillation Techniques To Improve Low-Precision Network Accuracy
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning networks have achieved state-of-the-art accuracies on computer vision workloads like image classification and object detection. The performant systems, however, typically involve big models with numerous parameters. Once trained, a challenging aspect for such top performing models is deployment on resource constrained inference systems - the models (often deep networks or wide networks or both) are compute and memory intensive. Low-precision numerics and model compression using knowledge distillation are popular techniques to lower both the compute requirements and memory footprint of these deployed models. In this paper, we study the combination of these two techniques and show that the performance of low-precision networks can be significantly improved by using knowledge distillation techniques. Our approach, Apprentice, achieves state-of-the-art accuracies using ternary precision and 4-bit precision for variants of ResNet architecture on ImageNet dataset. We present three schemes using which one can apply knowledge distillation techniques to various stages of the train-and-deploy pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Powerful Yet Underappreciated Compression Technique in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a dominant technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. Despite its widespread adoption across computer vision and natural language processing, significant misconceptions persist about how and why distillation works. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is not primarily effective because teachers transfer rich categorical similarity information, but rather because it functions as a form of learned regularization. Moreover, we demonstrate that distillation's benefits extend far beyond simple performance preservation, enabling fairness improvements, robustness transfer, and enhanced interpretability in the resulting student models.

papers_seen.author: Hickman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Critical Approach to Efficient Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing deep neural networks while maintaining competitive performance. Rather than developing entirely new lightweight architectures, distillation enables the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller student models, addressing a fundamental challenge in deploying deep learning systems to resource-constrained environments. This approach has demonstrated success across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, offering a practical pathway to reduce computational costs without sacrificing model quality.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are essential techniques for deploying deep learning models efficiently in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from larger, computationally expensive models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This synthesis examines the theoretical foundations, methodological innovations, and practical applications of knowledge distillation across various domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and federated learning. The review covers training strategies, multi-teacher approaches, zero-shot methods, and task-specific compression techniques, while also addressing emerging challenges and opportunities for improving model efficiency without sacrificing accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Hancock
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Approaches and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression represent fundamental techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of learned representations and knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student networks while maintaining competitive predictive performance. The approach has been extensively applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, graph neural networks, and specialized applications such as reinforcement learning and federated learning. Recent innovations span feature-level distillation, adversarial learning strategies, multi-teacher approaches, and task-specific compression methods. Knowledge distillation has become essential for practical deep learning deployment by addressing fundamental challenges in making advanced models accessible for real-world applications with limited computational and storage resources.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models by transferring knowledge from a teacher network to a student network. This approach has become increasingly important for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments, particularly in natural language processing and computer vision tasks. The method works by leveraging soft target probabilities and intermediate representations from the teacher to regularize and guide student model training. Beyond traditional teacher-student frameworks, recent developments include self-distillation methods, multi-teacher approaches, and task-adaptive compression strategies. Knowledge distillation has demonstrated significant practical benefits, achieving substantial reductions in model size and inference time while maintaining competitive performance across diverse applications including image classification, object detection, language modeling, and machine translation.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are essential techniques for deploying deep neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, graph neural networks, and specialized tasks such as speech processing and question answering systems. The core principle involves training student networks to mimic teacher predictions, allowing for significant reductions in model size, inference time, and computational requirements without substantial accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Jacobs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Fundamental Approach to Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a cornerstone technique for creating efficient, deployable deep learning models without sacrificing performance. By enabling smaller student models to learn from larger teacher models, distillation achieves substantial reductions in model size and computational requirements while maintaining competitive accuracy. This approach addresses critical practical challenges in deploying state-of-the-art neural networks across diverse domains, from natural language processing to computer vision. The technique's versatility and effectiveness make it essential for real-world AI deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Torres
papers_seen.title: The Indispensable Role of Knowledge Distillation in Modern Deep Learning: Enabling Efficient Deployment While Preserving Performance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and natural language processing. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student networks, simultaneously reducing memory footprint and inference time while maintaining competitive performance. The technique addresses critical challenges in deploying neural networks to resource-constrained environments and extends beyond simple model compression to applications in federated learning, domain adaptation, and robustness enhancement. Evidence across diverse domains demonstrates that knowledge distillation represents not merely a performance optimization technique, but a paradigm shift in how neural networks can be efficiently trained and deployed for practical real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Critical Technique for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining predictive performance. This approach involves training a student model to mimic the behavior of a larger teacher model, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments. Despite its widespread adoption across various domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks, the mechanisms underlying knowledge distillation remain partially understood. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents an essential yet imperfect solution to the model compression challenge, with significant implications for practical deep learning applications while presenting important theoretical and practical limitations.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Learning Student-Friendly Teacher Networks for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel knowledge distillation approach to facilitate the transfer of dark knowledge from a teacher to a student. Contrary to most of the existing methods that rely on effective training of student models given pretrained teachers, we aim to learn the teacher models that are friendly to students and, consequently, more appropriate for knowledge transfer. In other words, at the time of optimizing a teacher model, the proposed algorithm learns the student branches jointly to obtain student-friendly representations. Since the main goal of our approach lies in training teacher models and the subsequent knowledge distillation procedure is straightforward, most of the existing knowledge distillation methods can adopt this technique to improve the performance of diverse student models in terms of accuracy and convergence speed. The proposed algorithm demonstrates outstanding accuracy in several well-known knowledge distillation techniques with various combinations of teacher and student models even in the case that their architectures are heterogeneous and there is no prior knowledge about student models at the time of training teacher networks.

papers_seen.author: Murillo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a pivotal technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach addresses critical deployment challenges by reducing computational cost, memory footprint, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. The technique spans diverse applications from computer vision to NLP, with innovations in feature-level distillation, adversarial learning strategies, and task-specific optimizations making it essential for modern deep learning deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Reinforced Multi-Teacher Selection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In natural language processing (NLP) tasks, slow inference speed and huge footprints in GPU usage remain the bottleneck of applying pre-trained deep models in production. As a popular method for model compression, knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from one or multiple large (teacher) models to a small (student) model. When multiple teacher models are available in distillation, the state-of-the-art methods assign a fixed weight to a teacher model in the whole distillation. Furthermore, most of the existing methods allocate an equal weight to every teacher model. In this paper, we observe that, due to the complexity of training examples and the differences in student model capability, learning differentially from teacher models can lead to better performance of student models distilled. We systematically develop a reinforced method to dynamically assign weights to teacher models for different training instances and optimize the performance of student model. Our extensive experimental results on several NLP tasks clearly verify the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Adversarial Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) has made remarkable progress in the last few years and become a popular paradigm for model compression and knowledge transfer. However, almost all existing KD algorithms are data-driven, i.e., relying on a large amount of original training data or alternative data, which is usually unavailable in real-world scenarios. In this paper, we devote ourselves to this challenging problem and propose a novel adversarial distillation mechanism to craft a compact student model without any real-world data. We introduce a model discrepancy to quantificationally measure the difference between student and teacher models and construct an optimizable upper bound. In our work, the student and the teacher jointly act the role of the discriminator to reduce this discrepancy, when a generator adversarially produces some "hard samples" to enlarge it. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed data-free method yields comparable performance to existing data-driven methods. More strikingly, our approach can be directly extended to semantic segmentation, which is more complicated than classification, and our approach achieves state-of-the-art results. papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Does Knowledge Distillation Really Work?
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique for training a small student network to emulate a larger teacher model, such as an ensemble of networks. We show that while knowledge distillation can improve student generalization, it does not typically work as it is commonly understood: there often remains a surprisingly large discrepancy between the predictive distributions of the teacher and the student, even in cases when the student has the capacity to perfectly match the teacher. We identify difficulties in optimization as a key reason for why the student is unable to match the teacher. We also show how the details of the dataset used for distillation play a role in how closely the student matches the teacher -- and that more closely matching the teacher paradoxically does not always lead to better student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Wise
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Review
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and natural language processing. This approach enables the deployment of large neural networks on resource-constrained devices by training smaller student networks to mimic the behavior of larger, more accurate teacher networks. Beyond simple output matching, modern distillation methods incorporate intermediate layer alignment, attention-based mechanisms, and adaptive weighting strategies. The technique demonstrates broad applicability across diverse domains including language models, computer vision, recommender systems, and multimodal learning, addressing critical challenges in model deployment while maintaining competitive performance.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Reinforced Multi-Teacher Selection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In natural language processing (NLP) tasks, slow inference speed and huge footprints in GPU usage remain the bottleneck of applying pre-trained deep models in production. As a popular method for model compression, knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from one or multiple large (teacher) models to a small (student) model. When multiple teacher models are available in distillation, the state-of-the-art methods assign a fixed weight to a teacher model in the whole distillation. Furthermore, most of the existing methods allocate an equal weight to every teacher model. In this paper, we observe that, due to the complexity of training examples and the differences in student model capability, learning differentially from teacher models can lead to better performance of student models distilled. We systematically develop a reinforced method to dynamically assign weights to teacher models for different training instances and optimize the performance of student model. Our extensive experimental results on several NLP tasks clearly verify the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Understanding and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing neural networks by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models. This approach addresses critical deployment challenges by reducing computational requirements, memory footprint, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal learning, making knowledge distillation an essential strategy for deploying powerful deep learning models on resource-constrained devices.

papers_seen.author: Mahoney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: An Essential Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical and increasingly indispensable technique for deploying efficient deep learning models across resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student networks, this approach enables practitioners to achieve substantial reductions in computational overhead, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. This position argues that knowledge distillation represents not merely an optimization technique but a fundamental necessity for making state-of-the-art deep learning models practical for real-world deployment across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Blair
papers_seen.title: Distilling Policy Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The transfer of knowledge from one policy to another is an important tool in Deep Reinforcement Learning. This process, referred to as distillation, has been used to great success, for example, by enhancing the optimisation of agents, leading to stronger performance faster, on harder domains [26, 32, 5, 8]. Despite the widespread use and conceptual simplicity of distillation, many different formulations are used in practice, and the subtle variations between them can often drastically change the performance and the resulting objective that is being optimised. In this work, we rigorously explore the entire landscape of policy distillation, comparing the motivations and strengths of each variant through theoretical and empirical analysis. Our results point to three distillation techniques, that are preferred depending on specifics of the task. Specifically a newly proposed expected entropy regularised distillation allows for quicker learning in a wide range of situations, while still guaranteeing convergence.

Advances in knowledge distillation techniques have been applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and generative models, with innovations addressing challenges such as data scarcity, adversarial robustness, and multi-modal learning.

papers_seen.author: Smith

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become indispensable techniques for deploying deep learning and NLP models in resource-constrained environments. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a fundamental paradigm shift in model deployment, offering practical solutions for real-world applications where latency, memory, and computational constraints are critical considerations. We examine various distillation approaches, their applications across diverse tasks, and their effectiveness in maintaining model performance while reducing computational overhead.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: BERT Learns to Teach: Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We present Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning (MetaDistil), a simple yet effective alternative to traditional knowledge distillation (KD) methods where the teacher model is fixed during training. We show the teacher network can learn to better transfer knowledge to the student network (i.e., learning to teach) with the feedback from the performance of the distilled student network in a meta learning framework. Moreover, we introduce a pilot update mechanism to improve the alignment between the inner-learner and meta-learner in meta learning algorithms that focus on an improved inner-learner. Experiments on various benchmarks show that MetaDistil can yield significant improvements compared with traditional KD algorithms and is less sensitive to the choice of different student capacity and hyperparameters, facilitating the use of KD on different tasks and models.

papers_seen.author: Tucker

papers_seen.author: Lee

papers_seen.author: Jacobs

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a cornerstone technique for creating efficient, deployable deep learning models without sacrificing performance. By enabling smaller student models to learn from larger teacher models, distillation achieves substantial reductions in model size and computational requirements while maintaining competitive accuracy. This approach addresses critical practical challenges in deploying state-of-the-art neural networks across diverse domains, from natural language processing to computer vision. The technique's versatility and effectiveness make it essential for real-world AI deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Powerful Strategy for Neural Network Compression and Transfer Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining performance. This approach involves transferring knowledge from a large teacher network to a smaller student network through various mechanisms, including soft label matching, attention-based feature transfer, and meta-learning frameworks. Knowledge distillation has proven effective across diverse applications including natural language processing, computer vision, and complex reasoning tasks. The technique addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning models to resource-constrained environments while enabling faster inference times and reduced parameter requirements. Recent advances have extended distillation beyond simple probability matching to encompass layer-wise information transfer, task-adaptive compression, and collaborative learning schemes.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Knowledge Distillation for CTR Prediction
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, deep learning-based models have been widely studied for click-through rate (CTR) prediction and lead to improved prediction accuracy in many industrial applications. However, current research focuses primarily on building complex network architectures to better capture sophisticated feature interactions and dynamic user behaviors. The increased model complexity may slow down online inference and hinder its adoption in real-time applications. Instead, our work targets at a new model training strategy based on knowledge distillation (KD). KD is a teacher-student learning framework to transfer knowledge learned from a teacher model to a student model. The KD strategy not only allows us to simplify the student model as a vanilla DNN model but also achieves significant accuracy improvements over the state-of-the-art teacher models. The benefits thus motivate us to further explore the use of a powerful ensemble of teachers for more accurate student model training. We also propose some novel techniques to facilitate ensembled CTR prediction, including teacher gating and early stopping by distillation loss. We conduct comprehensive experiments against 12 existing models and across three industrial datasets. Both offline and online A/B testing results show the effectiveness of our KD-based training strategy.

papers_seen.author: Wilson

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential technique for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, distillation enables substantial reductions in model size and computational requirements while maintaining competitive performance. This approach has demonstrated broad applicability across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, graph neural networks, and specialized applications, establishing it as a fundamental tool for practical deep learning deployment in real-world scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Rivera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Transformative Paradigm Essential for Modern Deep Learning and NLP Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and transformative technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining or even improving performance. This approach enables the practical deployment of deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices and in latency-sensitive applications. Beyond simple performance optimization, knowledge distillation represents a core paradigm shift in how deep learning models are trained and deployed, addressing multiple critical challenges including computational efficiency, privacy preservation, model interpretability, and robustness enhancement. The technique has proven versatile across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized architectures, making it essential for modern deep learning applications.

papers_seen.author: Calderon
papers_seen.title: Learning Generalizable Models for Vehicle Routing Problems via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent neural methods for vehicle routing problems always train and test the deep models on the same instance distribution (i.e., uniform). To tackle the consequent cross-distribution generalization concerns, we bring the knowledge distillation to this field and propose an Adaptive Multi-Distribution Knowledge Distillation (AMDKD) scheme for learning more generalizable deep models. Particularly, our AMDKD leverages various knowledge from multiple teachers trained on exemplar distributions to yield a light-weight yet generalist student model. Meanwhile, we equip AMDKD with an adaptive strategy that allows the student to concentrate on difficult distributions, so as to absorb hard-to-master knowledge more effectively. Extensive experimental results show that, compared with the baseline neural methods, our AMDKD is able to achieve competitive results on both unseen in-distribution and out-of-distribution instances, which are either randomly synthesized or adopted from benchmark datasets (i.e., TSPLIB and CVRPLIB). Notably, our AMDKD is generic, and consumes less computational resources for inference.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression techniques have emerged as critical approaches for reducing the computational and memory requirements of deep neural networks, particularly in natural language processing and computer vision applications. This synthesis examines the state of knowledge distillation methodologies, including selective knowledge transfer, feature-based approaches, adversarial learning strategies, and task-specific applications, while also exploring complementary compression techniques such as pruning and quantization. The research demonstrates that effective knowledge distillation can achieve significant model compression rates while maintaining or even improving performance, with applications spanning machine translation, language understanding, visual recognition, and medical imaging.

papers_seen.author: Chandler

Beyond basic compression, knowledge distillation serves diverse purposes including domain adaptation, improved generalization, and efficient federated learning. Recent advances have expanded distillation methods to include intermediate layer alignment, attention-based mechanisms, and theoretical frameworks that explain its effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Zamora

This synthesis examines the theoretical foundations, practical implementations, and applications of knowledge distillation, including selective distillation strategies, data augmentation interactions, feature-level knowledge transfer, and domain-specific applications in machine translation, reading comprehension, and language model compression.

papers_seen.author: Ortiz

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for deploying large neural networks on resource-constrained devices by enabling smaller student models to learn from larger teacher models. This position argues that knowledge distillation is not merely a performance-preservation technique, but rather functions as a powerful form of learned regularization that offers benefits extending far beyond simple compression, including improved robustness and fairness, making it essential for practical deep learning deployment across diverse domains.
