papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an indispensable technique for deploying powerful deep neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models, distillation addresses fundamental challenges in making advanced deep learning practical. This position argues that knowledge distillation is essential for real-world applications, demonstrates its effectiveness across diverse domains, and examines recent advances that have expanded its applicability beyond traditional supervised learning contexts.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: BERT-EMD: Many-to-Many Layer Mapping for BERT Compression with Earth Mover's Distance
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained language models (e.g., BERT) have achieved significant success in various natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, high storage and computational costs obstruct pre-trained language models to be effectively deployed on resource-constrained devices. In this paper, we propose a novel BERT distillation method based on many-to-many layer mapping, which allows each intermediate student layer to learn from any intermediate teacher layers. In this way, our model can learn from different teacher layers adaptively for various NLP tasks. %motivated by the intuition that different NLP tasks require different levels of linguistic knowledge contained in the intermediate layers of BERT. In addition, we leverage Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) to compute the minimum cumulative cost that must be paid to transform knowledge from teacher network to student network. EMD enables the effective matching for many-to-many layer mapping. %EMD can be applied to network layers with different sizes and effectively measures semantic distance between the teacher network and student network. Furthermore, we propose a cost attention mechanism to learn the layer weights used in EMD automatically, which is supposed to further improve the model's performance and accelerate convergence time. Extensive experiments on GLUE benchmark demonstrate that our model achieves competitive performance compared to strong competitors in terms of both accuracy and model compression.

papers_seen.author: Wong
papers_seen.title: Embracing the Dark Knowledge: Domain Generalization Using Regularized Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Though convolutional neural networks are widely used in different tasks, lack of generalization capability in the absence of sufficient and representative data is one of the challenges that hinder their practical application. In this paper, we propose a simple, effective, and plug-and-play training strategy named Knowledge Distillation for Domain Generalization (KDDG) which is built upon a knowledge distillation framework with the gradient filter as a novel regularization term. We find that both the ``richer dark knowledge" from the teacher network, as well as the gradient filter we proposed, can reduce the difficulty of learning the mapping which further improves the generalization ability of the model. We also conduct experiments extensively to show that our framework can significantly improve the generalization capability of deep neural networks in different tasks including image classification, segmentation, reinforcement learning by comparing our method with existing state-of-the-art domain generalization techniques. Last but not the least, we propose to adopt two metrics to analyze our proposed method in order to better understand how our proposed method benefits the generalization capability of deep neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Mitigating Gender Bias in Distilled Language Models via Counterfactual Role Reversal
papers_seen.abstract: Language models excel at generating coherent text, and model compression techniques such as knowledge distillation have enabled their use in resource-constrained settings. However, these models can be biased in multiple ways, including the unfounded association of male and female genders with gender-neutral professions. Therefore, knowledge distillation without any fairness constraints may preserve or exaggerate the teacher model's biases onto the distilled model. To this end, we present a novel approach to mitigate gender disparity in text generation by learning a fair model during knowledge distillation. We propose two modifications to the base knowledge distillation based on counterfactual role reversal$\unicode{x2014}$modifying teacher probabilities and augmenting the training set. We evaluate gender polarity across professions in open-ended text generated from the resulting distilled and finetuned GPT$\unicode{x2012}$2 models and demonstrate a substantial reduction in gender disparity with only a minor compromise in utility. Finally, we observe that language models that reduce gender polarity in language generation do not improve embedding fairness or downstream classification fairness.

papers_seen.author: Riley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are critical techniques for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation involves transferring knowledge from larger, high-capacity teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student networks, enabling effective model compression while maintaining performance. These methods span various applications including natural language processing, computer vision, medical imaging, and reinforcement learning. Recent advances include domain-adaptive approaches, data-free distillation, cross-modal knowledge transfer, and theoretical foundations that explain why distillation succeeds. The field has progressed from simple logit-matching approaches to sophisticated methods that transfer feature-level and attention-based knowledge, addressing practical deployment challenges across diverse domains.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Approaches and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models through various mechanisms including soft label matching, feature mimicking, and adversarial training. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, graph neural networks, and specialized tasks such as information retrieval and speech processing. Knowledge distillation enables practical deployment of powerful models in resource-constrained environments while addressing critical challenges in model efficiency, latency reduction, and inference cost.

papers_seen.author: Barnes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a pivotal technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach addresses critical deployment challenges where computational resources and inference speed are limited. While traditional knowledge distillation methods require access to training data, recent advances include data-free approaches and specialized variants for specific domains. Applications span natural language processing tasks, computer vision, federated learning, and other domains, with notable success in compressing BERT-based language models, improving translation systems, and enabling efficient inference on resource-constrained devices.

papers_seen.author: Charles
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Critical Tool for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, this approach addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems across resource-constrained environments. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a fundamental necessity for modern AI deployment, enabling practical implementation across natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains while significantly reducing computational overhead and memory requirements without sacrificing predictive accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Rios
papers_seen.title: Improving Neural Topic Models using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Topic models are often used to identify human-interpretable topics to help make sense of large document collections. We use knowledge distillation to combine the best attributes of probabilistic topic models and pretrained transformers. Our modular method can be straightforwardly applied with any neural topic model to improve topic quality, which we demonstrate using two models having disparate architectures, obtaining state-of-the-art topic coherence. We show that our adaptable framework not only improves performance in the aggregate over all estimated topics, as is commonly reported, but also in head-to-head comparisons of aligned topics.

papers_seen.author: Walls
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Approaches and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying efficient neural networks across diverse domains. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from larger, complex teacher models to smaller, lightweight student models while maintaining or improving performance. This synthesis examines the current state of knowledge distillation techniques, their applications to natural language processing and computer vision tasks, and recent innovations in multi-teacher frameworks and domain-specific approaches. The research demonstrates that knowledge distillation provides a flexible and practical solution for reducing computational costs and memory requirements in both discriminative and generative models, with particular success in transformer-based language models, neural machine translation, and graph neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Leblanc
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Deploying Deep Learning Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining comparable performance. This review examines key approaches including structural distillation, feature-based distillation, and application-specific compression strategies across various domains. The evidence demonstrates that knowledge distillation consistently enables substantial model size reduction with minimal accuracy loss, making it an indispensable tool for practical deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Moran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical Path to Efficient Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing neural networks while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from large, well-trained teacher models to smaller student models, enabling efficient deployment across resource-constrained environments. Recent advances demonstrate that distillation is particularly effective for language models, computer vision tasks, and specialized applications. The technique addresses the critical challenge of balancing model performance with computational efficiency, making it essential for practical deployment of deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These approaches enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, maintaining or improving performance while reducing computational costs and memory requirements. The techniques have been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, federated learning, and multimodal systems, addressing critical challenges in practical AI deployment.

papers_seen.author: Welch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Enabling Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression techniques have become essential approaches for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This paper synthesizes recent advances in knowledge distillation across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks, demonstrating the broad applicability and effectiveness of these compression techniques for practical deployment scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student networks. This approach has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and federated learning. By leveraging soft target probabilities and intermediate representations from teachers, knowledge distillation achieves significant reductions in model size and computational cost while maintaining competitive performance. Recent advances have extended the technique to address challenges such as data-free distillation, adversarial robustness, heterogeneous models, and task-specific compression. The method has proven particularly valuable for deploying neural networks on resource-constrained devices and enabling real-time inference in practical applications.

papers_seen.author: Joyce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models. This approach has become essential for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments and real-world applications where inference speed and memory footprint are critical constraints. The method has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks, demonstrating consistent improvements in model efficiency while maintaining competitive accuracy with the original teacher models.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Apprentice: Using Knowledge Distillation Techniques To Improve Low-Precision Network Accuracy
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning networks have achieved state-of-the-art accuracies on computer vision workloads like image classification and object detection. The performant systems, however, typically involve big models with numerous parameters. Once trained, a challenging aspect for such top performing models is deployment on resource constrained inference systems - the models (often deep networks or wide networks or both) are compute and memory intensive. Low-precision numerics and model compression using knowledge distillation are popular techniques to lower both the compute requirements and memory footprint of these deployed models. In this paper, we study the combination of these two techniques and show that the performance of low-precision networks can be significantly improved by using knowledge distillation techniques. Our approach, Apprentice, achieves state-of-the-art accuracies using ternary precision and 4-bit precision for variants of ResNet architecture on ImageNet dataset. We present three schemes using which one can apply knowledge distillation techniques to various stages of the train-and-deploy pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Current Approaches
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying deep neural networks in resource-constrained environments. This synthesis examines the diverse applications and methodologies of knowledge distillation across multiple domains including natural language processing, graph neural networks, computer vision, and speech recognition. We review various distillation strategies, including soft-label matching, intermediate representation matching, and adversarial learning approaches, demonstrating how these techniques effectively compress large models while maintaining or even improving performance. Special attention is given to domain-specific innovations such as distillation for non-autoregressive translation, BERT compression, and graph neural network acceleration.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation for Deep Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in model compression have provided procedures for compressing large neural networks to a fraction of their original size while retaining most if not all of their accuracy. However, all of these approaches rely on access to the original training set, which might not always be possible if the network to be compressed was trained on a very large dataset, or on a dataset whose release poses privacy or safety concerns as may be the case for biometrics tasks. We present a method for data-free knowledge distillation, which is able to compress deep neural networks trained on large-scale datasets to a fraction of their size leveraging only some extra metadata to be provided with a pretrained model release. We also explore different kinds of metadata that can be used with our method, and discuss tradeoffs involved in using each of them.

papers_seen.author: Harvey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression techniques have emerged as critical approaches for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments while maintaining predictive performance. This synthesis examines how these techniques leverage teacher-student frameworks to transfer knowledge from larger, more complex models to smaller, more efficient ones across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks. Key findings reveal the mechanisms by which soft labels facilitate knowledge transfer, the bias-variance tradeoffs involved in distillation, and practical applications in accelerating inference for real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Wheeler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique that enables the transfer of knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, reducing computational and memory requirements while maintaining performance. This approach has been widely adopted across various domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning, with applications spanning from domain adaptation and multi-task learning to adversarial robustness and fair model compression. Recent advances have introduced task-aware filtering, attention-based feature matching, and progressive training strategies to improve the effectiveness of knowledge transfer and student model learning.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a training technique that transfers knowledge from a large teacher model to a smaller, more efficient student model. This approach has become essential for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. Model compression through distillation addresses fundamental challenges in making modern neural networks practical, including reducing computational costs, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and federated learning settings.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing neural networks and improving model efficiency across multiple domains including computer vision and natural language processing. This approach transfers knowledge from larger, high-performing teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices without substantial performance degradation. Recent advances in knowledge distillation have expanded beyond simple output-level transfer to include intermediate representations, attention mechanisms, and adversarial learning strategies. The technique has proven particularly valuable in NLP applications where pre-trained language models face computational and memory constraints, and in federated learning scenarios with heterogeneous devices. This synthesis reviews the fundamental mechanisms of knowledge distillation, its applications across different architectures and tasks, and emerging strategies for improving distillation effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Obrien
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the practical deployment of advanced deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications. By transferring knowledge from teacher models to student models through various mechanisms, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in making sophisticated neural networks accessible for real-world applications with limited computational resources.

papers_seen.author: Wise
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Review
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and natural language processing. This approach enables the deployment of large neural networks on resource-constrained devices by training smaller student networks to mimic the behavior of larger, more accurate teacher networks. Beyond simple output matching, modern distillation methods incorporate intermediate layer alignment, attention-based mechanisms, and adaptive weighting strategies. The technique demonstrates broad applicability across diverse domains including language models, computer vision, recommender systems, and multimodal learning, addressing critical challenges in model deployment while maintaining competitive performance.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning: A Comprehensive Strategy for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile technique in deep learning, enabling the compression of large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from complex teacher networks to simpler student networks, addressing critical challenges in deploying deep learning models on resource-constrained devices. Recent advances span multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning, with innovations in distillation mechanisms, architectural designs, and theoretical foundations. The technique has proven effective not only for model compression but also for improving interpretability, enabling lifelong learning, and facilitating federated learning scenarios. Despite its widespread adoption, ongoing research continues to refine distillation methods and expand their applicability across diverse tasks and model types.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Approaches and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models by transferring knowledge from teacher models to student models. This approach addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, federated learning, and specialized applications like medical image segmentation and style transfer. Knowledge distillation enables significant reductions in model size and computational requirements while maintaining or improving performance compared to baseline models.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Fletcher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Approaches and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying deep learning models efficiently in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications.

papers_seen.author: Keith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are critical techniques that enable the deployment of large, sophisticated neural networks in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models, these methods maintain competitive performance while dramatically reducing computational requirements and memory footprint. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents an essential approach for practical AI deployment across diverse applications in deep learning and natural language processing, addressing the fundamental tension between model capability and computational efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Wolfe
papers_seen.title: Robust and Resource-Efficient Data-Free Knowledge Distillation by Generative Pseudo Replay
papers_seen.abstract: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation (KD) allows knowledge transfer from a trained neural network (teacher) to a more compact one (student) in the absence of original training data. Existing works use a validation set to monitor the accuracy of the student over real data and report the highest performance throughout the entire process. However, validation data may not be available at distillation time either, making it infeasible to record the student snapshot that achieved the peak accuracy. Therefore, a practical data-free KD method should be robust and ideally provide monotonically increasing student accuracy during distillation. This is challenging because the student experiences knowledge degradation due to the distribution shift of the synthetic data. A straightforward approach to overcome this issue is to store and rehearse the generated samples periodically, which increases the memory footprint and creates privacy concerns. We propose to model the distribution of the previously observed synthetic samples with a generative network. In particular, we design a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) with a training objective that is customized to learn the synthetic data representations optimally. The student is rehearsed by the generative pseudo replay technique, with samples produced by the VAE. Hence knowledge degradation can be prevented without storing any samples. Experiments on image classification benchmarks show that our method optimizes the expected value of the distilled model accuracy while eliminating the large memory overhead incurred by the sample-storing methods.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Critical Approach to Efficient Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from teacher models to student models across diverse applications in natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains. The technique encompasses various methodologies including output-level distillation, feature-based approaches, and task-aware strategies. Evidence demonstrates that distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments while addressing computational overhead and memory limitations without substantial accuracy losses.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a training technique that transfers knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models, enabling efficient deployment of deep learning systems while maintaining competitive performance. This approach addresses critical challenges in modern machine learning by reducing computational costs, memory requirements, and inference latency. Applications span computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains including object detection, machine translation, and federated learning, demonstrating the broad applicability of knowledge distillation as a fundamental model compression technique.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Robust Cross-Modal Representation Learning with Progressive Self-Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The learning objective of vision-language approach of CLIP does not effectively account for the noisy many-to-many correspondences found in web-harvested image captioning datasets, which contributes to its compute and data inefficiency. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel training framework based on cross-modal contrastive learning that uses progressive self-distillation and soft image-text alignments to more efficiently learn robust representations from noisy data. Our model distills its own knowledge to dynamically generate soft-alignment targets for a subset of images and captions in every minibatch, which are then used to update its parameters. Extensive evaluation across 14 benchmark datasets shows that our method consistently outperforms its CLIP counterpart in multiple settings, including: (a) zero-shot classification, (b) linear probe transfer, and (c) image-text retrieval, without incurring added computational cost. Analysis using an ImageNet-based robustness test-bed reveals that our method offers better effective robustness to natural distribution shifts compared to both ImageNet-trained models and CLIP itself. Lastly, pretraining with datasets spanning two orders of magnitude in size shows that our improvements over CLIP tend to scale with number of training examples.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Extract the Knowledge of Graph Neural Networks and Go Beyond it: An Effective Knowledge Distillation Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Semi-supervised learning on graphs is an important problem in the machine learning area. In recent years, state-of-the-art classification methods based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown their superiority over traditional ones such as label propagation. However, the sophisticated architectures of these neural models will lead to a complex prediction mechanism, which could not make full use of valuable prior knowledge lying in the data, e.g., structurally correlated nodes tend to have the same class. In this paper, we propose a framework based on knowledge distillation to address the above issues. Our framework extracts the knowledge of an arbitrary learned GNN model (teacher model), and injects it into a well-designed student model. The student model is built with two simple prediction mechanisms, i.e., label propagation and feature transformation, which naturally preserves structure-based and feature-based prior knowledge, respectively. In specific, we design the student model as a trainable combination of parameterized label propagation and feature transformation modules. As a result, the learned student can benefit from both prior knowledge and the knowledge in GNN teachers for more effective predictions. Moreover, the learned student model has a more interpretable prediction process than GNNs. We conduct experiments on five public benchmark datasets and employ seven GNN models including GCN, GAT, APPNP, SAGE, SGC, GCNII and GLP as the teacher models. Experimental results show that the learned student model can consistently outperform its corresponding teacher model by 1.4% - 4.7% on average. Code and data are available at https://github.com/BUPT-GAMMA/CPF

papers_seen.author: Aguirre
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from a large, complex teacher model to a smaller, more efficient student model. This approach has become increasingly important for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments and for improving model efficiency across various tasks including image classification, object detection, natural language processing, and speech recognition. The technique enables significant reductions in model size and inference time while maintaining competitive performance with the original teacher model. Applications span from compressing pre-trained language models like BERT to developing efficient detectors for autonomous systems, with various methodological innovations addressing different challenges in the knowledge transfer process.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Approaches and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models by transferring knowledge from teacher models to student models. This approach addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, federated learning, and specialized applications like medical image segmentation and style transfer. Knowledge distillation enables significant reductions in model size and computational requirements while maintaining or improving performance compared to baseline models.

papers_seen.author: Aguilar
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from larger, more expressive teacher models to smaller student networks while maintaining competitive performance. This synthesis examines the theoretical foundations, methodological approaches, and practical applications of knowledge distillation across computer vision and natural language processing tasks, including recent developments in handling soft labels, intermediate feature representations, and domain-specific adaptations.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Crucial Technique for Effective Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential approach for compressing deep learning models while maintaining predictive performance. This technique involves training a smaller student model to mimic a larger, more capable teacher model, enabling efficient deployment without sacrificing accuracy. The method has proven particularly valuable across multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and machine translation, offering systematic solutions to reduce computational overhead and memory requirements in neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Critical Tool for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential technique for making deep learning models practical in real-world deployments. By enabling the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller student networks, distillation addresses fundamental constraints in model deployment including computational efficiency, memory requirements, and inference speed. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is not merely an optimization technique but a foundational approach necessary for making state-of-the-art models accessible across diverse computing environments and applications.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Improved Accuracy in Spoken Question Answering
papers_seen.abstract: Spoken question answering (SQA) is a challenging task that requires the machine to fully understand the complex spoken documents. Automatic speech recognition (ASR) plays a significant role in the development of QA systems. However, the recent work shows that ASR systems generate highly noisy transcripts, which critically limit the capability of machine comprehension on the SQA task. To address the issue, we present a novel distillation framework. Specifically, we devise a training strategy to perform knowledge distillation (KD) from spoken documents and written counterparts. Our work makes a step towards distilling knowledge from the language model as a supervision signal to lead to better student accuracy by reducing the misalignment between automatic and manual transcriptions. Experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms several state-of-the-art language models on the Spoken-SQuAD dataset.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation for Deep Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in model compression have provided procedures for compressing large neural networks to a fraction of their original size while retaining most if not all of their accuracy. However, all of these approaches rely on access to the original training set, which might not always be possible if the network to be compressed was trained on a very large dataset, or on a dataset whose release poses privacy or safety concerns as may be the case for biometrics tasks. We present a method for data-free knowledge distillation, which is able to compress deep neural networks trained on large-scale datasets to a fraction of their size leveraging only some extra metadata to be provided with a pretrained model release. We also explore different kinds of metadata that can be used with our method, and discuss tradeoffs involved in using each of them.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: It is challenging to perform lifelong language learning (LLL) on a stream of different tasks without any performance degradation comparing to the multi-task counterparts. To address this issue, we present Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation (L2KD), a simple but efficient method that can be easily applied to existing LLL architectures in order to mitigate the degradation. Specifically, when the LLL model is trained on a new task, we assign a teacher model to first learn the new task, and pass the knowledge to the LLL model via knowledge distillation. Therefore, the LLL model can better adapt to the new task while keeping the previously learned knowledge. Experiments show that the proposed L2KD consistently improves previous state-of-the-art models, and the degradation comparing to multi-task models in LLL tasks is well mitigated for both sequence generation and text classification tasks.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Towards Model Agnostic Federated Learning Using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Is it possible to design an universal API for federated learning using which an ad-hoc group of data-holders (agents) collaborate with each other and perform federated learning? Such an API would necessarily need to be model-agnostic i.e. make no assumption about the model architecture being used by the agents, and also cannot rely on having representative public data at hand. Knowledge distillation (KD) is the obvious tool of choice to design such protocols. However, surprisingly, we show that most natural KD-based federated learning protocols have poor performance.   To investigate this, we propose a new theoretical framework, Federated Kernel ridge regression, which can capture both model heterogeneity as well as data heterogeneity. Our analysis shows that the degradation is largely due to a fundamental limitation of knowledge distillation under data heterogeneity. We further validate our framework by analyzing and designing new protocols based on KD. Their performance on real world experiments using neural networks, though still unsatisfactory, closely matches our theoretical predictions.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Distilled Semantics for Comprehensive Scene Understanding from Videos
papers_seen.abstract: Whole understanding of the surroundings is paramount to autonomous systems. Recent works have shown that deep neural networks can learn geometry (depth) and motion (optical flow) from a monocular video without any explicit supervision from ground truth annotations, particularly hard to source for these two tasks. In this paper, we take an additional step toward holistic scene understanding with monocular cameras by learning depth and motion alongside with semantics, with supervision for the latter provided by a pre-trained network distilling proxy ground truth images. We address the three tasks jointly by a) a novel training protocol based on knowledge distillation and self-supervision and b) a compact network architecture which enables efficient scene understanding on both power hungry GPUs and low-power embedded platforms. We thoroughly assess the performance of our framework and show that it yields state-of-the-art results for monocular depth estimation, optical flow and motion segmentation.

papers_seen.author: Murphy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for training smaller, more efficient neural networks by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to compact student networks. This approach has become essential for deploying deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across diverse applications including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains. By balancing model performance with computational efficiency and memory requirements, knowledge distillation enables practical deployment on mobile devices, edge computing systems, and latency-sensitive applications while maintaining competitive accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge From a Deep Pose Regressor Network
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a novel method to distill knowledge from a deep pose regressor network for efficient Visual Odometry (VO). Standard distillation relies on "dark knowledge" for successful knowledge transfer. As this knowledge is not available in pose regression and the teacher prediction is not always accurate, we propose to emphasize the knowledge transfer only when we trust the teacher. We achieve this by using teacher loss as a confidence score which places variable relative importance on the teacher prediction. We inject this confidence score to the main training task via Attentive Imitation Loss (AIL) and when learning the intermediate representation of the teacher through Attentive Hint Training (AHT) approach. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work which successfully distill the knowledge from a deep pose regression network. Our evaluation on the KITTI and Malaga dataset shows that we can keep the student prediction close to the teacher with up to 92.95% parameter reduction and 2.12x faster in computation time.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Adversarially Robust Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is effective for producing small, high-performance neural networks for classification, but these small networks are vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper studies how adversarial robustness transfers from teacher to student during knowledge distillation. We find that a large amount of robustness may be inherited by the student even when distilled on only clean images. Second, we introduce Adversarially Robust Distillation (ARD) for distilling robustness onto student networks. In addition to producing small models with high test accuracy like conventional distillation, ARD also passes the superior robustness of large networks onto the student. In our experiments, we find that ARD student models decisively outperform adversarially trained networks of identical architecture in terms of robust accuracy, surpassing state-of-the-art methods on standard robustness benchmarks. Finally, we adapt recent fast adversarial training methods to ARD for accelerated robust distillation.

papers_seen.author: Hickman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Critical Approach to Efficient Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing deep neural networks while maintaining competitive performance. Rather than developing entirely new lightweight architectures, distillation enables the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller student models, addressing a fundamental challenge in deploying deep learning systems to resource-constrained environments. This approach has demonstrated success across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, offering a practical pathway to reduce computational costs without sacrificing model quality.

papers_seen.author: Harris

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for developing efficient neural networks capable of deployment in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from larger, well-trained teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, reducing computational requirements while maintaining performance. Applications span across diverse domains including machine translation, natural language processing, computer vision, and generative models, addressing key challenges in inference speed, memory footprint, and practical deployment.

papers_seen.author: Fisher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying large neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining performance. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, these approaches enable significant reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference latency. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents an essential paradigm for making state-of-the-art deep learning models practical and accessible across diverse applications including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Critical Approach to Efficient Deep Learning Deployment

By enabling strategic knowledge transfer from teacher models to student models, distillation achieves substantial reductions in model size, computational requirements, and memory footprint while preserving the learned capabilities essential for real-world deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Chandler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices. The technique is particularly valuable in natural language processing and computer vision, where modern models impose significant computational burdens. Beyond basic compression, knowledge distillation serves diverse purposes including domain adaptation, improved generalization, and efficient federated learning. Recent advances have expanded distillation methods to include intermediate layer alignment, attention-based mechanisms, and theoretical frameworks that explain its effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Bowman
papers_seen.title: TRILLsson: Distilled Universal Paralinguistic Speech Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in self-supervision have dramatically improved the quality of speech representations. However, deployment of state-of-the-art embedding models on devices has been restricted due to their limited public availability and large resource footprint. Our work addresses these issues by publicly releasing a collection of paralinguistic speech models that are small and near state-of-the-art performance. Our approach is based on knowledge distillation, and our models are distilled on public data only. We explore different architectures and thoroughly evaluate our models on the Non-Semantic Speech (NOSS) benchmark. Our largest distilled model is less than 15% the size of the original model (314MB vs 2.2GB), achieves over 96% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks, and is trained on 6.5% the data. The smallest model is 1% in size (22MB) and achieves over 90% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks. Our models outperform the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 model on 6 of 7 tasks, and our smallest model outperforms the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 on both emotion recognition tasks despite being 7% the size.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression represent fundamental techniques for deploying deep neural networks efficiently across resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while preserving or enhancing predictive performance. This synthesis examines the core mechanisms, diverse applications, and innovations in knowledge distillation across domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks, demonstrating how distillation functions as both a compression technique and a powerful regularization mechanism.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Distilling portable Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are critical techniques for deploying deep neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This review synthesizes the current state of research across diverse applications including computer vision, natural language processing, generative models, and domain adaptation, examining both foundational approaches and recent advances in data-free and specialized distillation methods.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: An Essential Technique for Efficient Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to compact student networks, distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. This approach has proven effective across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, establishing itself as a critical tool for making deep learning practical in real-world scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful paradigm for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining performance. This approach involves training a student network to mimic the behavior of a larger teacher network, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices. Advances in knowledge distillation techniques have been applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and generative models, with innovations addressing challenges such as data scarcity, adversarial robustness, and multi-modal learning.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Private Model Compression via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The soaring demand for intelligent mobile applications calls for deploying powerful deep neural networks (DNNs) on mobile devices. However, the outstanding performance of DNNs notoriously relies on increasingly complex models, which in turn is associated with an increase in computational expense far surpassing mobile devices' capacity. What is worse, app service providers need to collect and utilize a large volume of users' data, which contain sensitive information, to build the sophisticated DNN models. Directly deploying these models on public mobile devices presents prohibitive privacy risk. To benefit from the on-device deep learning without the capacity and privacy concerns, we design a private model compression framework RONA. Following the knowledge distillation paradigm, we jointly use hint learning, distillation learning, and self learning to train a compact and fast neural network. The knowledge distilled from the cumbersome model is adaptively bounded and carefully perturbed to enforce differential privacy. We further propose an elegant query sample selection method to reduce the number of queries and control the privacy loss. A series of empirical evaluations as well as the implementation on an Android mobile device show that RONA can not only compress cumbersome models efficiently but also provide a strong privacy guarantee. For example, on SVHN, when a meaningful $(9.83,10^{-6})$-differential privacy is guaranteed, the compact model trained by RONA can obtain 20$\times$ compression ratio and 19$\times$ speed-up with merely 0.97% accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Adversarial Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) has made remarkable progress in the last few years and become a popular paradigm for model compression and knowledge transfer. However, almost all existing KD algorithms are data-driven, i.e., relying on a large amount of original training data or alternative data, which is usually unavailable in real-world scenarios. In this paper, we devote ourselves to this challenging problem and propose a novel adversarial distillation mechanism to craft a compact student model without any real-world data. We introduce a model discrepancy to quantificationally measure the difference between student and teacher models and construct an optimizable upper bound. In our work, the student and the teacher jointly act the role of the discriminator to reduce this discrepancy, when a generator adversarially produces some "hard samples" to enlarge it. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed data-free method yields comparable performance to existing data-driven methods. More strikingly, our approach can be directly extended to semantic segmentation, which is more complicated than classification, and our approach achieves state-of-the-art results. Code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/VainF/Data-Free-Adversarial-Distillation.

papers_seen.author: Ware
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach addresses critical challenges in deploying state-of-the-art neural networks to resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. By examining diverse applications and methodologies across multiple domains, knowledge distillation represents not merely a supplementary compression technique, but a versatile learning paradigm essential for practical deployment of deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge distillation from multi-modal to mono-modal segmentation networks
papers_seen.abstract: The joint use of multiple imaging modalities for medical image segmentation has been widely studied in recent years. The fusion of information from different modalities has demonstrated to improve the segmentation accuracy, with respect to mono-modal segmentations, in several applications. However, acquiring multiple modalities is usually not possible in a clinical setting due to a limited number of physicians and scanners, and to limit costs and scan time. Most of the time, only one modality is acquired. In this paper, we propose KD-Net, a framework to transfer knowledge from a trained multi-modal network (teacher) to a mono-modal one (student). The proposed method is an adaptation of the generalized distillation framework where the student network is trained on a subset (1 modality) of the teacher's inputs (n modalities). We illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in brain tumor segmentation with the BraTS 2018 dataset. Using different architectures, we show that the student network effectively learns from the teacher and always outperforms the baseline mono-modal network in terms of segmentation accuracy.

This approach spans multiple domains including natural language processing, speech processing, graph neural networks, and computer vision, offering flexible solutions for various model compression scenarios from standard settings to data-free contexts.
