Knowledge distillation operates by having a student model learn from a teacher model's predictions or intermediate representations, effectively capturing the teacher's knowledge in a more compact form. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including machine translation, language understanding, visual recognition, and recommendation systems, achieving substantial reductions in model size and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance levels.

papers_seen.author: Walton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing neural networks and transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models. This approach addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems, including computational efficiency, memory footprint reduction, and inference latency. Applications span across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, speech processing, and information retrieval. Recent advances explore novel architectures, multi-teacher frameworks, data-free scenarios, and task-specific optimizations to enhance both student model performance and practical deployability.

papers_seen.author: Hancock
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Approaches and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression represent fundamental techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of learned representations and knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student networks while maintaining competitive predictive performance. The approach has been extensively applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, graph neural networks, and specialized applications such as reinforcement learning and federated learning. Recent innovations span feature-level distillation, adversarial learning strategies, multi-teacher approaches, and task-specific compression methods. Knowledge distillation has become essential for practical deep learning deployment by addressing fundamental challenges in making advanced models accessible for real-world applications with limited computational and storage resources.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Does Knowledge Distillation Really Work?
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique for training a small student network to emulate a larger teacher model, such as an ensemble of networks. We show that while knowledge distillation can improve student generalization, it does not typically work as it is commonly understood: there often remains a surprisingly large discrepancy between the predictive distributions of the teacher and the student, even in cases when the student has the capacity to perfectly match the teacher. We identify difficulties in optimization as a key reason for why the student is unable to match the teacher. We also show how the details of the dataset used for distillation play a role in how closely the student matches the teacher -- and that more closely matching the teacher paradoxically does not always lead to better student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: An Essential Technique for Efficient Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to compact student networks, distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. This approach has proven effective across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, establishing itself as a critical tool for making deep learning practical in real-world scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: R2L: Distilling Neural Radiance Field to Neural Light Field for Efficient Novel View Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Recent research explosion on Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) shows the encouraging potential to represent complex scenes with neural networks. One major drawback of NeRF is its prohibitive inference time: Rendering a single pixel requires querying the NeRF network hundreds of times. To resolve it, existing efforts mainly attempt to reduce the number of required sampled points. However, the problem of iterative sampling still exists. On the other hand, Neural Light Field (NeLF) presents a more straightforward representation over NeRF in novel view synthesis -- the rendering of a pixel amounts to one single forward pass without ray-marching. In this work, we present a deep residual MLP network (88 layers) to effectively learn the light field. We show the key to successfully learning such a deep NeLF network is to have sufficient data, for which we transfer the knowledge from a pre-trained NeRF model via data distillation. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world scenes show the merits of our method over other counterpart algorithms. On the synthetic scenes, we achieve 26-35x FLOPs reduction (per camera ray) and 28-31x runtime speedup, meanwhile delivering significantly better (1.4-2.8 dB average PSNR improvement) rendering quality than NeRF without any customized parallelism requirement.

papers_seen.author: Pham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Critical Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential and transformative technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, addressing critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. Applications span natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and graph neural networks, with innovations in training strategies, multi-teacher approaches, and domain-specific optimizations. The technique simultaneously reduces computational complexity, enables privacy-preserving model transfer, and improves model interpretability, establishing it as a fundamental paradigm for practical deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Crucial Technique for Effective Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential approach for compressing deep learning models while maintaining predictive performance. This technique involves training a smaller student model to mimic a larger, more capable teacher model, enabling efficient deployment without sacrificing accuracy. The method has proven particularly valuable across multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and machine translation, offering systematic solutions to reduce computational overhead and memory requirements in neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large teacher networks to smaller student networks, enabling efficient deployment of deep learning models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach has become increasingly important across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and speech processing. Knowledge distillation operates through various mechanisms including output probability matching, feature-level transfer, and adversarial learning, with recent advances extending its applicability to generative models, recommendation systems, and other specialized architectures.

papers_seen.author: Leonard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Vital Approach for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Systems
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student models, reducing inference time and memory requirements while maintaining competitive performance. This paper examines the fundamental principles, applications, and theoretical foundations of knowledge distillation across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized tasks, demonstrating how these compression techniques address real-world deployment challenges in modern deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Shields
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach involves transferring knowledge from large teacher networks to smaller student networks through various mechanisms, enabling practical deployment in resource-constrained environments. Applications span multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and federated learning, with recent advances addressing domain adaptation, fairness concerns, adversarial robustness, and theoretical foundations of the distillation process.

papers_seen.author: Patterson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Transformative Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for enabling the deployment of large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to compact student networks, these approaches maintain competitive performance while dramatically reducing computational and storage requirements. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a fundamental paradigm shift in model training and deployment, offering practical solutions for diverse applications across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge distillation from multi-modal to mono-modal segmentation networks
papers_seen.abstract: The joint use of multiple imaging modalities for medical image segmentation has been widely studied in recent years. The fusion of information from different modalities has demonstrated to improve the segmentation accuracy, with respect to mono-modal segmentations, in several applications. However, acquiring multiple modalities is usually not possible in a clinical setting due to a limited number of physicians and scanners, and to limit costs and scan time. Most of the time, only one modality is acquired. In this paper, we propose KD-Net, a framework to transfer knowledge from a trained multi-modal network (teacher) to a mono-modal one (student). The proposed method is an adaptation of the generalized distillation framework where the student network is trained on a subset (1 modality) of the teacher's inputs (n modalities). We illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in brain tumor segmentation with the BraTS 2018 dataset. Using different architectures, we show that the student network effectively learns from the teacher and always outperforms the baseline mono-modal network in terms of segmentation accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for transferring knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach enables model compression while maintaining competitive performance across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, recommender systems, and federated learning. The technique involves training a student network to emulate a teacher model's behavior, effectively reducing computational requirements and memory footprint for deployment on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation has been adapted and extended for various applications, including domain adaptation, privacy-preserving learning, and specialized architectures like vision transformers and graph neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Heath
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are critical techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These approaches enable the transfer of knowledge from large "teacher" models to smaller "student" networks, reducing computational costs and parameter counts while maintaining competitive performance. Recent work spans diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, federated learning, and reinforcement learning, demonstrating the broad applicability of these compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation in Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Since deep learning became a key player in natural language processing (NLP), many deep learning models have been showing remarkable performances in a variety of NLP tasks, and in some cases, they are even outperforming humans. Such high performance can be explained by efficient knowledge representation of deep learning models. While many methods have been proposed to learn more efficient representation, knowledge distillation from pretrained deep networks suggest that we can use more information from the soft target probability to train other neural networks. In this paper, we propose a new knowledge distillation method self-knowledge distillation, based on the soft target probabilities of the training model itself, where multimode information is distilled from the word embedding space right below the softmax layer. Due to the time complexity, our method approximates the soft target probabilities. In experiments, we applied the proposed method to two different and fundamental NLP tasks: language model and neural machine translation. The experiment results show that our proposed method improves performance on the tasks.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-adopted technique for model compression that enables the training of efficient student models by transferring knowledge from larger, more powerful teacher models. This approach has become fundamental in deep learning and natural language processing, addressing the critical challenge of deploying high-performance models under computational constraints. Knowledge distillation methods transfer various types of knowledge including soft logits, intermediate feature representations, and attention patterns, enabling significant model size reduction while maintaining competitive accuracy across diverse applications including computer vision, machine translation, speech recognition, and recommendation systems.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that trains a smaller student network to mimic a larger teacher network, enabling deployment of high-performing models on resource-constrained devices. This approach has been successfully applied across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and generative models. The technique leverages knowledge transfer mechanisms to maintain performance while reducing computational and memory requirements, making it valuable for practical applications where efficiency is critical.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are critical techniques for enabling the deployment of sophisticated deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, maintaining high performance while dramatically reducing inference time and memory requirements. This review examines the current state of knowledge distillation across computer vision and natural language processing domains, discussing key mechanisms, practical applications, and emerging challenges in the field.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Enabling Multimodal Generation on CLIP via Vision-Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The recent large-scale vision-language pre-training (VLP) of dual-stream architectures (e.g., CLIP) with a tremendous amount of image-text pair data, has shown its superiority on various multimodal alignment tasks. Despite its success, the resulting models are not capable of multimodal generative tasks due to the weak text encoder. To tackle this problem, we propose to augment the dual-stream VLP model with a textual pre-trained language model (PLM) via vision-language knowledge distillation (VLKD), enabling the capability for multimodal generation. VLKD is pretty data- and computation-efficient compared to the pre-training from scratch. Experimental results show that the resulting model has strong zero-shot performance on multimodal generation tasks, such as open-ended visual question answering and image captioning. For example, it achieves 44.5% zero-shot accuracy on the VQAv2 dataset, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art zero-shot model with $7\times$ fewer parameters. Furthermore, the original textual language understanding and generation ability of the PLM is maintained after VLKD, which makes our model versatile for both multimodal and unimodal tasks.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying deep neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation has proven effective across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, offering practical solutions for reducing computational costs and memory requirements without substantial accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Scott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Transformative Paradigm for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining or exceeding performance. This approach transfers knowledge from teacher models to student models across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and graph neural networks, addressing critical challenges in deploying sophisticated models on resource-constrained devices. Recent advances have expanded distillation techniques beyond simple logit matching to encompass feature-level transfer, attention-based mechanisms, adversarial training, and multi-teacher frameworks, making it an essential paradigm for modern deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Alvarado
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are essential techniques for enabling the efficient deployment of neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, graph neural networks, federated learning, and specialized tasks, demonstrating the broad applicability and importance of these techniques for practical AI system deployment.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Preserving Privacy in Federated Learning with Ensemble Cross-Domain Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a machine learning paradigm where local nodes collaboratively train a central model while the training data remains decentralized. Existing FL methods typically share model parameters or employ co-distillation to address the issue of unbalanced data distribution. However, they suffer from communication bottlenecks. More importantly, they risk privacy leakage. In this work, we develop a privacy preserving and communication efficient method in a FL framework with one-shot offline knowledge distillation using unlabeled, cross-domain public data. We propose a quantized and noisy ensemble of local predictions from completely trained local models for stronger privacy guarantees without sacrificing accuracy. Based on extensive experiments on image classification and text classification tasks, we show that our privacy-preserving method outperforms baseline FL algorithms with superior performance in both accuracy and communication efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Bowman
papers_seen.title: TRILLsson: Distilled Universal Paralinguistic Speech Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in self-supervision have dramatically improved the quality of speech representations. However, deployment of state-of-the-art embedding models on devices has been restricted due to their limited public availability and large resource footprint. Our work addresses these issues by publicly releasing a collection of paralinguistic speech models that are small and near state-of-the-art performance. Our approach is based on knowledge distillation, and our models are distilled on public data only. We explore different architectures and thoroughly evaluate our models on the Non-Semantic Speech (NOSS) benchmark. Our largest distilled model is less than 15% the size of the original model (314MB vs 2.2GB), achieves over 96% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks, and is trained on 6.5% the data. The smallest model is 1% in size (22MB) and achieves over 90% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks. Our models outperform the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 model on 6 of 7 tasks, and our smallest model outperforms the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 on both emotion recognition tasks despite being 7% the size.

papers_seen.author: Decker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying deep neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive models to smaller, more efficient student networks while maintaining competitive performance. This synthesis examines the diverse applications and approaches within knowledge distillation across deep learning and natural language processing domains, highlighting the mechanisms, strategies, and practical implementations that make these techniques effective for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Transformative Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and transformative technique for compressing large neural networks and transferring knowledge from complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems, including computational efficiency, memory footprint reduction, and inference latency, while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and federated learning, demonstrating the broad applicability and essential role of knowledge distillation in modern machine learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression and efficient deployment of deep learning systems. By transferring knowledge from large teacher networks to compact student models, this approach maintains competitive performance while significantly reducing computational overhead and memory requirements. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is essential for making state-of-the-art deep learning models practical for real-world applications across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech processing, and graph neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Preserving Privacy in Federated Learning with Ensemble Cross-Domain Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a machine learning paradigm where local nodes collaboratively train a central model while the training data remains decentralized. Existing FL methods typically share model parameters or employ co-distillation to address the issue of unbalanced data distribution. However, they suffer from communication bottlenecks. More importantly, they risk privacy leakage. In this work, we develop a privacy preserving and communication efficient method in a FL framework with one-shot offline knowledge distillation using unlabeled, cross-domain public data. We propose a quantized and noisy ensemble of local predictions from completely trained local models for stronger privacy guarantees without sacrificing accuracy. Based on extensive experiments on image classification and text classification tasks, we show that our privacy-preserving method outperforms baseline FL algorithms with superior performance in both accuracy and communication efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Blair
papers_seen.title: Distilling Policy Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The transfer of knowledge from one policy to another is an important tool in Deep Reinforcement Learning. This process, referred to as distillation, has been used to great success, for example, by enhancing the optimisation of agents, leading to stronger performance faster, on harder domains [26, 32, 5, 8]. Despite the widespread use and conceptual simplicity of distillation, many different formulations are used in practice, and the subtle variations between them can often drastically change the performance and the resulting objective that is being optimised. In this work, we rigorously explore the entire landscape of policy distillation, comparing the motivations and strengths of each variant through theoretical and empirical analysis. Our results point to three distillation techniques, that are preferred depending on specifics of the task. Specifically a newly proposed expected entropy regularised distillation allows for quicker learning in a wide range of situations, while still guaranteeing convergence.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student networks. This approach has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and federated learning. By leveraging soft target probabilities and intermediate representations from teachers, knowledge distillation achieves significant reductions in model size and computational cost while maintaining competitive performance. Recent advances have extended the technique to address challenges such as data-free distillation, adversarial robustness, heterogeneous models, and task-specific compression. The method has proven particularly valuable for deploying neural networks on resource-constrained devices and enabling real-time inference in practical applications.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are essential techniques for deploying deep learning and NLP models in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from larger, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This synthesis examines the theoretical foundations, methodological innovations, and practical applications of knowledge distillation across diverse domains, covering training strategies, multi-teacher approaches, data-free methods, and task-specific compression techniques, while addressing emerging challenges in maintaining model accuracy without sacrificing efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Object DGCNN: 3D Object Detection using Dynamic Graphs
papers_seen.abstract: 3D object detection often involves complicated training and testing pipelines, which require substantial domain knowledge about individual datasets. Inspired by recent non-maximum suppression-free 2D object detection models, we propose a 3D object detection architecture on point clouds. Our method models 3D object detection as message passing on a dynamic graph, generalizing the DGCNN framework to predict a set of objects. In our construction, we remove the necessity of post-processing via object confidence aggregation or non-maximum suppression. To facilitate object detection from sparse point clouds, we also propose a set-to-set distillation approach customized to 3D detection. This approach aligns the outputs of the teacher model and the student model in a permutation-invariant fashion, significantly simplifying knowledge distillation for the 3D detection task. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on autonomous driving benchmarks. We also provide abundant analysis of the detection model and distillation framework.

papers_seen.author: Waller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Fundamental Approach to Efficient Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a dominant paradigm for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. This technique enables the transfer of knowledge from larger teacher networks to smaller student networks, making deep learning systems practical for resource-constrained environments. Beyond simple performance preservation, knowledge distillation functions as a form of learned regularization and offers broader benefits including robustness transfer, fairness improvements, and enhanced interpretability. The field has evolved significantly to address diverse scenarios and applications across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Bentley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Technique for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach addresses the critical challenge of deploying sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments by transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student networks. Beyond simple performance preservation, knowledge distillation provides broader benefits including improved interpretability, enhanced robustness, and effective implementation across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommendation systems. The technique has evolved from simple logit-matching approaches to sophisticated methods incorporating feature-level and attention-based knowledge transfer, establishing itself as an essential strategy for making state-of-the-art models practical for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Deep Hierarchical Approach to Lifelong Learning in Minecraft
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a lifelong learning system that has the ability to reuse and transfer knowledge from one task to another while efficiently retaining the previously learned knowledge-base. Knowledge is transferred by learning reusable skills to solve tasks in Minecraft, a popular video game which is an unsolved and high-dimensional lifelong learning problem. These reusable skills, which we refer to as Deep Skill Networks, are then incorporated into our novel Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Network (H-DRLN) architecture using two techniques: (1) a deep skill array and (2) skill distillation, our novel variation of policy distillation (Rusu et. al. 2015) for learning skills. Skill distillation enables the HDRLN to efficiently retain knowledge and therefore scale in lifelong learning, by accumulating knowledge and encapsulating multiple reusable skills into a single distilled network. The H-DRLN exhibits superior performance and lower learning sample complexity compared to the regular Deep Q Network (Mnih et. al. 2015) in sub-domains of Minecraft.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from large teacher models to compact student networks, this approach enables deployment in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks. The technique addresses critical challenges in inference speed, memory footprint, and computational efficiency without substantial accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Riley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are critical techniques for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation involves transferring knowledge from larger, high-capacity teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student networks, enabling effective model compression while maintaining performance. These methods span various applications including natural language processing, computer vision, medical imaging, and reinforcement learning. Recent advances include domain-adaptive approaches, data-free distillation, cross-modal knowledge transfer, and theoretical foundations that explain why distillation succeeds. The field has progressed from simple logit-matching approaches to sophisticated methods that transfer feature-level and attention-based knowledge, addressing practical deployment challenges across diverse domains.

papers_seen.author: Walsh
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, complex teacher networks to smaller student networks, enabling efficient deployment in resource-constrained environments. This approach has become fundamental in deep learning and natural language processing, addressing critical challenges of computational cost and model size reduction. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including image classification, object detection, machine translation, and reading comprehension, demonstrating its versatility in creating deployable models while maintaining competitive performance.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks. The method leverages soft label matching, feature-level alignment, and sophisticated transfer mechanisms to achieve significant model compression with minimal accuracy degradation.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Advancing Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving performance. This approach transfers knowledge from a larger teacher model to a smaller student model, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices without sacrificing accuracy. The method extends across multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and federated learning, with applications ranging from mobile deployment to privacy-preserving distributed systems.

papers_seen.author: Fletcher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Approaches and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying deep learning models efficiently in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation in Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Since deep learning became a key player in natural language processing (NLP), many deep learning models have been showing remarkable performances in a variety of NLP tasks, and in some cases, they are even outperforming humans. Such high performance can be explained by efficient knowledge representation of deep learning models. While many methods have been proposed to learn more efficient representation, knowledge distillation from pretrained deep networks suggest that we can use more information from the soft target probability to train other neural networks. In this paper, we propose a new knowledge distillation method self-knowledge distillation, based on the soft target probabilities of the training model itself, where multimode information is distilled from the word embedding space right below the softmax layer. Due to the time complexity, our method approximates the soft target probabilities. In experiments, we applied the proposed method to two different and fundamental NLP tasks: language model and neural machine translation. The experiment results show that our proposed method improves performance on the tasks.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: Towards Efficient 3D Object Detection with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite substantial progress in 3D object detection, advanced 3D detectors often suffer from heavy computation overheads. To this end, we explore the potential of knowledge distillation (KD) for developing efficient 3D object detectors, focusing on popular pillar- and voxel-based detectors.In the absence of well-developed teacher-student pairs, we first study how to obtain student models with good trade offs between accuracy and efficiency from the perspectives of model compression and input resolution reduction. Then, we build a benchmark to assess existing KD methods developed in the 2D domain for 3D object detection upon six well-constructed teacher-student pairs. Further, we propose an improved KD pipeline incorporating an enhanced logit KD method that performs KD on only a few pivotal positions determined by teacher classification response, and a teacher-guided student model initialization to facilitate transferring teacher model's feature extraction ability to students through weight inheritance. Finally, we conduct extensive experiments on the Waymo dataset. Our best performing model achieves $65.75\%$ LEVEL 2 mAPH, surpassing its teacher model and requiring only $44\%$ of teacher flops. Our most efficient model runs 51 FPS on an NVIDIA A100, which is $2.2\times$ faster than PointPillar with even higher accuracy. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/CVMI-Lab/SparseKD}.

papers_seen.author: Chapman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling efficient deployment while maintaining performance. This approach has been extensively applied across computer vision and natural language processing tasks. Distillation can transfer various forms of knowledge including class probabilities, intermediate feature representations, and relational information between predictions. The technique has proven particularly valuable for compressing complex language models and improving the efficiency of neural networks without sacrificing accuracy. Recent advances have extended distillation to address fairness, adversarial robustness, multimodal learning, and multi-task settings, establishing it as a fundamental approach for creating deployable AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large teacher networks to smaller student networks, enabling efficient deployment of deep learning models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach has become increasingly important across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and speech processing. Knowledge distillation operates through various mechanisms including output probability matching, feature-level transfer, and adversarial learning, with recent advances extending its applicability to generative models, recommendation systems, and other specialized architectures.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a training technique that transfers knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach has emerged as a critical strategy for model compression in deep learning, enabling the deployment of high-performing models on resource-constrained devices without significant performance degradation. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, graph neural networks, and multimodal learning. By leveraging soft target probabilities and intermediate representations from teacher networks, distillation enables practical deployment while maintaining competitive performance levels.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Understanding and Improving Lexical Choice in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is essential for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models by reducing the complexity of the raw data with an autoregressive teacher model. In this study, we empirically show that as a side effect of this training, the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words are propagated to the NAT model from the teacher model. To alleviate this problem, we propose to expose the raw data to NAT models to restore the useful information of low-frequency words, which are missed in the distilled data. To this end, we introduce an extra Kullback-Leibler divergence term derived by comparing the lexical choice of NAT model and that embedded in the raw data. Experimental results across language pairs and model architectures demonstrate the effectiveness and universality of the proposed approach. Extensive analyses confirm our claim that our approach improves performance by reducing the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach pushes the SOTA NAT performance on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets up to 27.8 and 33.8 BLEU points, respectively. The source code will be released.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining high performance. This approach transfers knowledge from a large, well-trained teacher network to a smaller student network, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices. The method has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, healthcare, and recommendation systems, addressing key challenges of inference latency, computational efficiency, and model interpretability.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Mitigating Gender Bias in Distilled Language Models via Counterfactual Role Reversal
papers_seen.abstract: Language models excel at generating coherent text, and model compression techniques such as knowledge distillation have enabled their use in resource-constrained settings. However, these models can be biased in multiple ways, including the unfounded association of male and female genders with gender-neutral professions. Therefore, knowledge distillation without any fairness constraints may preserve or exaggerate the teacher model's biases onto the distilled model. To this end, we present a novel approach to mitigate gender disparity in text generation by learning a fair model during knowledge distillation. We propose two modifications to the base knowledge distillation based on counterfactual role reversal$\unicode{x2014}$modifying teacher probabilities and augmenting the training set. We evaluate gender polarity across professions in open-ended text generated from the resulting distilled and finetuned GPT$\unicode{x2012}$2 models and demonstrate a substantial reduction in gender disparity with only a minor compromise in utility. Finally, we observe that language models that reduce gender polarity in language generation do not improve embedding fairness or downstream classification fairness.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Distilled Semantics for Comprehensive Scene Understanding from Videos
papers_seen.abstract: Whole understanding of the surroundings is paramount to autonomous systems. Recent works have shown that deep neural networks can learn geometry (depth) and motion (optical flow) from a monocular video without any explicit supervision from ground truth annotations, particularly hard to source for these two tasks. In this paper, we take an additional step toward holistic scene understanding with monocular cameras by learning depth and motion alongside with semantics, with supervision for the latter provided by a pre-trained network distilling proxy ground truth images. We address the three tasks jointly by a) a novel training protocol based on knowledge distillation and self-supervision and b) a compact network architecture which enables efficient scene understanding on both power hungry GPUs and low-power embedded platforms. We thoroughly assess the performance of our framework and show that it yields state-of-the-art results for monocular depth estimation, optical flow and motion segmentation.

papers_seen.author: Huff
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are critical techniques for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a fundamental shift in how we approach model efficiency, enabling practical deployment across diverse applications from computer vision to natural language processing without sacrificing accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Apprentice: Using Knowledge Distillation Techniques To Improve Low-Precision Network Accuracy
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning networks have achieved state-of-the-art accuracies on computer vision workloads like image classification and object detection. The performant systems, however, typically involve big models with numerous parameters. Once trained, a challenging aspect for such top performing models is deployment on resource constrained inference systems - the models (often deep networks or wide networks or both) are compute and memory intensive. Low-precision numerics and model compression using knowledge distillation are popular techniques to lower both the compute requirements and memory footprint of these deployed models. In this paper, we study the combination of these two techniques and show that the performance of low-precision networks can be significantly improved by using knowledge distillation techniques. Our approach, Apprentice, achieves state-of-the-art accuracies using ternary precision and 4-bit precision for variants of ResNet architecture on ImageNet dataset. We present three schemes using which one can apply knowledge distillation techniques to various stages of the train-and-deploy pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Zamora
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Understanding and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing neural networks by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models. This approach has been extensively applied across deep learning and NLP tasks to reduce computational costs, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining performance. This synthesis examines the theoretical foundations, practical implementations, and applications of knowledge distillation, including selective distillation strategies, data augmentation interactions, feature-level knowledge transfer, and domain-specific applications in machine translation, reading comprehension, and language model compression.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that enables the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student networks. This approach has become increasingly important in deep learning and natural language processing, where computational efficiency and practical deployment on resource-constrained devices are critical concerns. Knowledge distillation operates by having a student model learn from a teacher model's predictions or intermediate representations, effectively capturing the teacher's knowledge in a more compact form. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including machine translation, language understanding, visual recognition, and recommendation systems, achieving substantial reductions in model size and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance levels.

papers_seen.author: Leonard

These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student models, reducing inference time and memory requirements while maintaining competitive performance. This paper examines the fundamental principles, applications, and theoretical foundations of knowledge distillation across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized tasks, demonstrating how these compression techniques address real-world deployment challenges in modern deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Charles
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Critical Tool for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a fundamental necessity for modern AI deployment, enabling practical implementation across natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains while significantly reducing computational overhead and memory requirements without sacrificing predictive accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Shaw
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are essential techniques for creating efficient neural networks that maintain high performance while reducing computational and storage requirements. These methods involve training compact student networks to emulate larger, more powerful teacher networks through knowledge transfer mechanisms. Applications span multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and graph neural networks, enabling the deployment of powerful models on resource-constrained devices.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: VPN++: Rethinking Video-Pose embeddings for understanding Activities of Daily Living
papers_seen.abstract: Many attempts have been made towards combining RGB and 3D poses for the recognition of Activities of Daily Living (ADL). ADL may look very similar and often necessitate to model fine-grained details to distinguish them. Because the recent 3D ConvNets are too rigid to capture the subtle visual patterns across an action, this research direction is dominated by methods combining RGB and 3D Poses. But the cost of computing 3D poses from RGB stream is high in the absence of appropriate sensors. This limits the usage of aforementioned approaches in real-world applications requiring low latency. Then, how to best take advantage of 3D Poses for recognizing ADL? To this end, we propose an extension of a pose driven attention mechanism: Video-Pose Network (VPN), exploring two distinct directions. One is to transfer the Pose knowledge into RGB through a feature-level distillation and the other towards mimicking pose driven attention through an attention-level distillation. Finally, these two approaches are integrated into a single model, we call VPN++. We show that VPN++ is not only effective but also provides a high speed up and high resilience to noisy Poses. VPN++, with or without 3D Poses, outperforms the representative baselines on 4 public datasets. Code is available at https://github.com/srijandas07/vpnplusplus.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for model compression that enables the efficient deployment of deep neural networks in resource-constrained environments. The method transfers knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach has become essential across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks, addressing critical challenges of inference latency, memory requirements, and computational efficiency without sacrificing model quality.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Critical Tool for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential technique for making deep learning models practical in real-world deployments. By enabling the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller student networks, distillation addresses fundamental constraints in model deployment including computational efficiency, memory requirements, and inference speed. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is not merely an optimization technique but a foundational approach necessary for making state-of-the-art models accessible across diverse computing environments and applications.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: Robust Re-Identification by Multiple Views Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: To achieve robustness in Re-Identification, standard methods leverage tracking information in a Video-To-Video fashion. However, these solutions face a large drop in performance for single image queries (e.g., Image-To-Video setting). Recent works address this severe degradation by transferring temporal information from a Video-based network to an Image-based one. In this work, we devise a training strategy that allows the transfer of a superior knowledge, arising from a set of views depicting the target object. Our proposal - Views Knowledge Distillation (VKD) - pins this visual variety as a supervision signal within a teacher-student framework, where the teacher educates a student who observes fewer views. As a result, the student outperforms not only its teacher but also the current state-of-the-art in Image-To-Video by a wide margin (6.3% mAP on MARS, 8.6% on Duke-Video-ReId and 5% on VeRi-776). A thorough analysis - on Person, Vehicle and Animal Re-ID - investigates the properties of VKD from a qualitatively and quantitatively perspective. Code is available at https://github.com/aimagelab/VKD.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Transferring Inductive Biases through Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Having the right inductive biases can be crucial in many tasks or scenarios where data or computing resources are a limiting factor, or where training data is not perfectly representative of the conditions at test time. However, defining, designing and efficiently adapting inductive biases is not necessarily straightforward. In this paper, we explore the power of knowledge distillation for transferring the effect of inductive biases from one model to another. We consider families of models with different inductive biases, LSTMs vs. Transformers and CNNs vs. MLPs, in the context of tasks and scenarios where having the right inductive biases is critical. We study the effect of inductive biases on the solutions the models converge to and investigate how and to what extent the effect of inductive biases is transferred through knowledge distillation, in terms of not only performance but also different aspects of converged solutions.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Compressing GANs using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been used in several machine learning tasks such as domain transfer, super resolution, and synthetic data generation. State-of-the-art GANs often use tens of millions of parameters, making them expensive to deploy for applications in low SWAP (size, weight, and power) hardware, such as mobile devices, and for applications with real time capabilities. There has been no work found to reduce the number of parameters used in GANs. Therefore, we propose a method to compress GANs using knowledge distillation techniques, in which a smaller "student" GAN learns to mimic a larger "teacher" GAN. We show that the distillation methods used on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Celeb-A datasets can compress teacher GANs at ratios of 1669:1, 58:1, and 87:1, respectively, while retaining the quality of the generated image. From our experiments, we observe a qualitative limit for GAN's compression. Moreover, we observe that, with a fixed parameter budget, compressed GANs outperform GANs trained using standard training methods. We conjecture that this is partially owing to the optimization landscape of over-parameterized GANs which allows efficient training using alternating gradient descent. Thus, training an over-parameterized GAN followed by our proposed compression scheme provides a high quality generative model with a small number of parameters.

papers_seen.author: Lin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Transformative Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining or improving performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student models, knowledge distillation addresses fundamental challenges in deploying deep learning systems to resource-constrained environments. This approach has demonstrated significant practical benefits across diverse domains, enabling efficient inference with minimal accuracy degradation. The technique encompasses multiple strategies including soft target matching, feature-level alignment, and advanced frameworks such as federated distillation and online distillation.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Improved Accuracy in Spoken Question Answering
papers_seen.abstract: Spoken question answering (SQA) is a challenging task that requires the machine to fully understand the complex spoken documents. Automatic speech recognition (ASR) plays a significant role in the development of QA systems. However, the recent work shows that ASR systems generate highly noisy transcripts, which critically limit the capability of machine comprehension on the SQA task. To address the issue, we present a novel distillation framework. Specifically, we devise a training strategy to perform knowledge distillation (KD) from spoken documents and written counterparts. Our work makes a step towards distilling knowledge from the language model as a supervision signal to lead to better student accuracy by reducing the misalignment between automatic and manual transcriptions. Experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms several state-of-the-art language models on the Spoken-SQuAD dataset.

papers_seen.author: Kidd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Strategic Transfer of Learning from Large to Small Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful paradigm for model compression that enables the transfer of knowledge from large teacher networks to smaller student models. This approach addresses critical challenges in deploying deep neural networks across resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. Through strategic knowledge transfer mechanisms, distillation techniques have proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal learning. The success of these methods relies on sophisticated mechanisms for capturing and transferring both task-relevant information and feature representations. Modern distillation frameworks continue to evolve, incorporating adaptive weighting schemes, layer-wise knowledge transfer, and adversarial learning strategies to maximize compression efficiency while minimizing performance degradation.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Preserving Privacy in Federated Learning with Ensemble Cross-Domain Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a machine learning paradigm where local nodes collaboratively train a central model while the training data remains decentralized. Existing FL methods typically share model parameters or employ co-distillation to address the issue of unbalanced data distribution. However, they suffer from communication bottlenecks. More importantly, they risk privacy leakage. In this work, we develop a privacy preserving and communication efficient method in a FL framework with one-shot offline knowledge distillation using unlabeled, cross-domain public data. We propose a quantized and noisy ensemble of local predictions from completely trained local models for stronger privacy guarantees without sacrificing accuracy. Based on extensive experiments on image classification and text classification tasks, we show that our privacy-preserving method outperforms baseline FL algorithms with superior performance in both accuracy and communication efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Collaborative Distillation for Ultra-Resolution Universal Style Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Universal style transfer methods typically leverage rich representations from deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (e.g., VGG-19) pre-trained on large collections of images. Despite the effectiveness, its application is heavily constrained by the large model size to handle ultra-resolution images given limited memory. In this work, we present a new knowledge distillation method (named Collaborative Distillation) for encoder-decoder based neural style transfer to reduce the convolutional filters. The main idea is underpinned by a finding that the encoder-decoder pairs construct an exclusive collaborative relationship, which is regarded as a new kind of knowledge for style transfer models. Moreover, to overcome the feature size mismatch when applying collaborative distillation, a linear embedding loss is introduced to drive the student network to learn a linear embedding of the teacher's features. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method when applied to different universal style transfer approaches (WCT and AdaIN), even if the model size is reduced by 15.5 times. Especially, on WCT with the compressed models, we achieve ultra-resolution (over 40 megapixels) universal style transfer on a 12GB GPU for the first time. Further experiments on optimization-based stylization scheme show the generality of our algorithm on different stylization paradigms. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/mingsun-tse/collaborative-distillation.
