papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are critical techniques for deploying deep neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This review synthesizes the current state of research across diverse applications including computer vision, natural language processing, generative models, and domain adaptation, examining both foundational approaches and recent advances in data-free and specialized distillation methods.

papers_seen.author: Donovan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and NLP, enabling the deployment of large neural networks on resource-constrained devices. This approach involves training a smaller student network to mimic the behavior of a larger, more accurate teacher network. Recent advances have expanded distillation methods beyond simple output matching to include intermediate layer alignment, attention-based mechanisms, and adaptive weighting strategies. Applications span diverse domains including language models, computer vision, graph neural networks, and multimodal learning, demonstrating the broad applicability of these compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Pope
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying large neural networks on resource-constrained devices. These methods enable smaller student models to learn from larger, more capable teacher models, achieving significant reductions in model size and inference time while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and graph neural networks, with various approaches addressing challenges such as heterogeneous architectures, domain adaptation, and ensemble compression.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing, enabling the efficient transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher networks to smaller, more deployable student networks. This approach addresses critical challenges of computational cost, model size reduction, and resource constraints while maintaining competitive performance. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including image classification, object detection, machine translation, reading comprehension, and specialized tasks such as spoken question answering and activity recognition. Knowledge distillation represents an essential paradigm for practical deep learning deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Critical Approach to Efficient Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing neural networks while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, enabling practical deployment in resource-constrained environments. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents an essential methodology for addressing the deployment challenges of modern deep learning across diverse domains including natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.author: Tran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression in deep learning, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large teacher models to compact student networks. This approach addresses critical challenges in deploying neural networks to resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. By examining applications across natural language processing and computer vision, this paper argues that knowledge distillation is not merely an optimization technique but a necessary strategy for making state-of-the-art models practical and accessible in real-world deployment scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Critical Approach to Efficient Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from teacher models to student models across diverse applications in natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains. The technique encompasses various methodologies including output-level distillation, feature-based approaches, and task-aware strategies. Evidence demonstrates that distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments while addressing computational overhead and memory limitations without substantial accuracy losses.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: CoReD: Generalizing Fake Media Detection with Continual Representation using Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Over the last few decades, artificial intelligence research has made tremendous strides, but it still heavily relies on fixed datasets in stationary environments. Continual learning is a growing field of research that examines how AI systems can learn sequentially from a continuous stream of linked data in the same way that biological systems do. Simultaneously, fake media such as deepfakes and synthetic face images have emerged as significant to current multimedia technologies. Recently, numerous method has been proposed which can detect deepfakes with high accuracy. However, they suffer significantly due to their reliance on fixed datasets in limited evaluation settings. Therefore, in this work, we apply continuous learning to neural networks' learning dynamics, emphasizing its potential to increase data efficiency significantly. We propose Continual Representation using Distillation (CoReD) method that employs the concept of Continual Learning (CL), Representation Learning (RL), and Knowledge Distillation (KD). We design CoReD to perform sequential domain adaptation tasks on new deepfake and GAN-generated synthetic face datasets, while effectively minimizing the catastrophic forgetting in a teacher-student model setting. Our extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method is efficient at domain adaptation to detect low-quality deepfakes videos and GAN-generated images from several datasets, outperforming the-state-of-art baseline methods.

papers_seen.author: Rios
papers_seen.title: Improving Neural Topic Models using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Topic models are often used to identify human-interpretable topics to help make sense of large document collections. We use knowledge distillation to combine the best attributes of probabilistic topic models and pretrained transformers. Our modular method can be straightforwardly applied with any neural topic model to improve topic quality, which we demonstrate using two models having disparate architectures, obtaining state-of-the-art topic coherence. We show that our adaptable framework not only improves performance in the aggregate over all estimated topics, as is commonly reported, but also in head-to-head comparisons of aligned topics.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for enabling the deployment of large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from larger, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student networks while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and reinforcement learning, addressing the fundamental challenges of reducing computational costs, memory requirements, and inference latency. The field has progressed from simple approaches to sophisticated methods that transfer feature-level and attention-based knowledge, with recent advances including multi-teacher strategies, data-free distillation, and cross-modal knowledge transfer.

papers_seen.author: Zuniga
papers_seen.title: Large scale distributed neural network training through online distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Techniques such as ensembling and distillation promise model quality improvements when paired with almost any base model. However, due to increased test-time cost (for ensembles) and increased complexity of the training pipeline (for distillation), these techniques are challenging to use in industrial settings. In this paper we explore a variant of distillation which is relatively straightforward to use as it does not require a complicated multi-stage setup or many new hyperparameters. Our first claim is that online distillation enables us to use extra parallelism to fit very large datasets about twice as fast. Crucially, we can still speed up training even after we have already reached the point at which additional parallelism provides no benefit for synchronous or asynchronous stochastic gradient descent. Two neural networks trained on disjoint subsets of the data can share knowledge by encouraging each model to agree with the predictions the other model would have made. These predictions can come from a stale version of the other model so they can be safely computed using weights that only rarely get transmitted. Our second claim is that online distillation is a cost-effective way to make the exact predictions of a model dramatically more reproducible. We support our claims using experiments on the Criteo Display Ad Challenge dataset, ImageNet, and the largest to-date dataset used for neural language modeling, containing $6\times 10^{11}$ tokens and based on the Common Crawl repository of web data.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: ALP-KD: Attention-Based Layer Projection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is considered as a training and compression strategy in which two neural networks, namely a teacher and a student, are coupled together during training. The teacher network is supposed to be a trustworthy predictor and the student tries to mimic its predictions. Usually, a student with a lighter architecture is selected so we can achieve compression and yet deliver high-quality results. In such a setting, distillation only happens for final predictions whereas the student could also benefit from teacher's supervision for internal components.   Motivated by this, we studied the problem of distillation for intermediate layers. Since there might not be a one-to-one alignment between student and teacher layers, existing techniques skip some teacher layers and only distill from a subset of them. This shortcoming directly impacts quality, so we instead propose a combinatorial technique which relies on attention. Our model fuses teacher-side information and takes each layer's significance into consideration, then performs distillation between combined teacher layers and those of the student. Using our technique, we distilled a 12-layer BERT (Devlin et al. 2019) into 6-, 4-, and 2-layer counterparts and evaluated them on GLUE tasks (Wang et al. 2018). Experimental results show that our combinatorial approach is able to outperform other existing techniques.

papers_seen.author: Mills
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a pivotal technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks. Knowledge distillation provides a practical solution to the challenge of deploying state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. The methodology encompasses various approaches including soft target distillation, feature-based distillation, and self-distillation, each offering distinct advantages depending on the specific application and task requirements.

papers_seen.author: Nunez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Fundamental Approach for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a cornerstone technique for creating efficient, deployable deep learning models without sacrificing performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents the most practical and effective approach to model compression across diverse applications in both computer vision and natural language processing. By enabling smaller student models to learn from larger teacher models, distillation achieves substantial reductions in model size and computational requirements while maintaining competitive accuracy. The technique's versatility is demonstrated through successful applications ranging from neural machine translation to domain-specific language models, and its theoretical foundations support its continued development as a critical tool for practical AI deployment.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks. The method leverages soft label matching, feature-level alignment, and sophisticated transfer mechanisms to achieve significant model compression with minimal accuracy degradation.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Powerful Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a highly effective approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive accuracy. This technique transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight student networks through various mechanisms, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments. This position paper argues that knowledge distillation is superior to alternative compression methods due to its flexibility, broad applicability across different domains and architectures, and proven ability to achieve substantial speedups with minimal accuracy degradation. Evidence demonstrates that distillation can be applied effectively in NLP, computer vision, and specialized domains, and offers unique advantages over traditional compression techniques through its ability to capture and transfer both feature-level and prediction-level knowledge.

papers_seen.author: Alvarado
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are essential techniques for enabling the efficient deployment of neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, graph neural networks, federated learning, and specialized tasks, demonstrating the broad applicability and importance of these techniques for practical AI system deployment.

papers_seen.author: Parsons
papers_seen.title: Curriculum Learning for Dense Retrieval Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent work has shown that more effective dense retrieval models can be obtained by distilling ranking knowledge from an existing base re-ranking model. In this paper, we propose a generic curriculum learning based optimization framework called CL-DRD that controls the difficulty level of training data produced by the re-ranking (teacher) model. CL-DRD iteratively optimizes the dense retrieval (student) model by increasing the difficulty of the knowledge distillation data made available to it. In more detail, we initially provide the student model coarse-grained preference pairs between documents in the teacher's ranking and progressively move towards finer-grained pairwise document ordering requirements. In our experiments, we apply a simple implementation of the CL-DRD framework to enhance two state-of-the-art dense retrieval models. Experiments on three public passage retrieval datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed framework.

papers_seen.author: Larson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from teacher networks to student networks across diverse domains, including computer vision, natural language processing, and graph neural networks. The method addresses critical challenges in model deployment by reducing computational costs and memory requirements while preserving the learned representations and prediction capabilities of larger models. Various distillation strategies have been developed to optimize knowledge transfer, improve data efficiency, and handle domain-specific complexities.

papers_seen.author: Jacobs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Fundamental Approach to Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a cornerstone technique for creating efficient, deployable deep learning models without sacrificing performance. By enabling smaller student models to learn from larger teacher models, distillation achieves substantial reductions in model size and computational requirements while maintaining competitive accuracy. This approach addresses critical practical challenges in deploying state-of-the-art neural networks across diverse domains, from natural language processing to computer vision. The technique's versatility and effectiveness make it essential for real-world AI deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Critical Approach to Efficient Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from teacher models to student models across diverse applications in natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains. The technique encompasses various methodologies including output-level distillation, feature-based approaches, and task-aware strategies. Evidence demonstrates that distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments while addressing computational overhead and memory limitations without substantial accuracy losses.

papers_seen.author: Leonard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Vital Approach for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Systems
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student models, reducing inference time and memory requirements while maintaining competitive performance. This paper examines the fundamental principles, applications, and theoretical foundations of knowledge distillation across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized tasks, demonstrating how these compression techniques address real-world deployment challenges in modern deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Feature-map-level Online Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Feature maps contain rich information about image intensity and spatial correlation. However, previous online knowledge distillation methods only utilize the class probabilities. Thus in this paper, we propose an online knowledge distillation method that transfers not only the knowledge of the class probabilities but also that of the feature map using the adversarial training framework. We train multiple networks simultaneously by employing discriminators to distinguish the feature map distributions of different networks. Each network has its corresponding discriminator which discriminates the feature map from its own as fake while classifying that of the other network as real. By training a network to fool the corresponding discriminator, it can learn the other network's feature map distribution. We show that our method performs better than the conventional direct alignment method such as L1 and is more suitable for online distillation. Also, we propose a novel cyclic learning scheme for training more than two networks together. We have applied our method to various network architectures on the classification task and discovered a significant improvement of performance especially in the case of training a pair of a small network and a large one.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation in Deep Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation deals with the problem of training a smaller model (Student) from a high capacity source model (Teacher) so as to retain most of its performance. Existing approaches use either the training data or meta-data extracted from it in order to train the Student. However, accessing the dataset on which the Teacher has been trained may not always be feasible if the dataset is very large or it poses privacy or safety concerns (e.g., bio-metric or medical data). Hence, in this paper, we propose a novel data-free method to train the Student from the Teacher. Without even using any meta-data, we synthesize the Data Impressions from the complex Teacher model and utilize these as surrogates for the original training data samples to transfer its learning to Student via knowledge distillation. We, therefore, dub our method "Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation" and demonstrate that our framework results in competitive generalization performance as achieved by distillation using the actual training data samples on multiple benchmark datasets.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and increasingly essential technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from high-capacity teacher networks to lightweight student networks, addressing critical challenges in deploying sophisticated deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices and latency-sensitive applications. By leveraging various mechanisms including soft target matching, layer-wise feature imitation, and task-aware knowledge transfer, knowledge distillation has demonstrated remarkable effectiveness across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized architectures. Recent advances have extended the technique to address challenges such as heterogeneous model compression, adversarial robustness, and cross-modal knowledge transfer.

papers_seen.author: Reid
papers_seen.title: Moonshine: Distilling with Cheap Convolutions
papers_seen.abstract: Many engineers wish to deploy modern neural networks in memory-limited settings; but the development of flexible methods for reducing memory use is in its infancy, and there is little knowledge of the resulting cost-benefit. We propose structural model distillation for memory reduction using a strategy that produces a student architecture that is a simple transformation of the teacher architecture: no redesign is needed, and the same hyperparameters can be used. Using attention transfer, we provide Pareto curves/tables for distillation of residual networks with four benchmark datasets, indicating the memory versus accuracy payoff. We show that substantial memory savings are possible with very little loss of accuracy, and confirm that distillation provides student network performance that is better than training that student architecture directly on data.

papers_seen.author: Kim
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Powerful Approach to Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a crucial technique for compressing large, complex neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining or even improving performance. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight student networks, making deep learning systems practical for real-world deployment in resource-constrained environments. Distillation techniques have been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks, demonstrating both theoretical soundness and practical utility.

papers_seen.author: Estes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from complex teacher models to simpler, more deployable architectures, enabling practical deployment in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation is increasingly applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and federated learning, with innovative mechanisms ranging from soft label matching to layer-wise feature transfer.

papers_seen.author: Humphrey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Benefits, Applications, and Empirical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for training compact neural networks by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models. This approach enables the deployment of deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive performance across diverse applications including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph learning. This paper examines the theoretical foundations, practical applications, and empirical findings surrounding knowledge distillation and model compression, highlighting both the effectiveness of the technique and important considerations for its successful implementation.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Does Knowledge Distillation Really Work?
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique for training a small student network to emulate a larger teacher model, such as an ensemble of networks. We show that while knowledge distillation can improve student generalization, it does not typically work as it is commonly understood: there often remains a surprisingly large discrepancy between the predictive distributions of the teacher and the student, even in cases when the student has the capacity to perfectly match the teacher. We identify difficulties in optimization as a key reason for why the student is unable to match the teacher. We also show how the details of the dataset used for distillation play a role in how closely the student matches the teacher -- and that more closely matching the teacher paradoxically does not always lead to better student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Conner
papers_seen.title: Distilling Task-Specific Knowledge from BERT into Simple Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: In the natural language processing literature, neural networks are becoming increasingly deeper and complex. The recent poster child of this trend is the deep language representation model, which includes BERT, ELMo, and GPT. These developments have led to the conviction that previous-generation, shallower neural networks for language understanding are obsolete. In this paper, however, we demonstrate that rudimentary, lightweight neural networks can still be made competitive without architecture changes, external training data, or additional input features. We propose to distill knowledge from BERT, a state-of-the-art language representation model, into a single-layer BiLSTM, as well as its siamese counterpart for sentence-pair tasks. Across multiple datasets in paraphrasing, natural language inference, and sentiment classification, we achieve comparable results with ELMo, while using roughly 100 times fewer parameters and 15 times less inference time.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing, enabling the efficient transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher networks to smaller, more deployable student networks. This approach addresses critical challenges of computational cost, model size reduction, and resource constraints while maintaining competitive performance. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including image classification, object detection, machine translation, reading comprehension, and specialized tasks such as spoken question answering and activity recognition. Knowledge distillation represents an essential paradigm for practical deep learning deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Cruz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining or improving predictive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models through multiple mechanisms including soft label matching, feature mimicking, and adversarial training. The technique has proven essential for deploying powerful models in resource-constrained environments across diverse applications spanning computer vision, natural language processing, generative models, and specialized tasks such as 3D object detection and federated learning.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are critical techniques for enabling the deployment of sophisticated deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, maintaining high performance while dramatically reducing inference time and memory requirements. This review examines the current state of knowledge distillation across computer vision and natural language processing domains, discussing key mechanisms, practical applications, and emerging challenges in the field.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Powerful Yet Underappreciated Compression Technique in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a dominant technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. Despite its widespread adoption across computer vision and natural language processing, significant misconceptions persist about how and why distillation works. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is not primarily effective because teachers transfer rich categorical similarity information, but rather because it functions as a form of learned regularization. Moreover, we demonstrate that distillation's benefits extend far beyond simple performance preservation, enabling fairness improvements, robustness transfer, and enhanced interpretability in the resulting student models.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that enables the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student networks. This approach has become increasingly important in deep learning and natural language processing, where computational efficiency and practical deployment on resource-constrained devices are critical concerns. Knowledge distillation operates by having a student model learn from a teacher model's predictions or intermediate representations, effectively capturing the teacher's knowledge in a more compact form. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including machine translation, language understanding, visual recognition, and recommendation systems, achieving substantial reductions in model size and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance levels.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Highlight Every Step: Knowledge Distillation via Collaborative Teaching
papers_seen.abstract: High storage and computational costs obstruct deep neural networks to be deployed on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation aims to train a compact student network by transferring knowledge from a larger pre-trained teacher model. However, most existing methods on knowledge distillation ignore the valuable information among training process associated with training results. In this paper, we provide a new Collaborative Teaching Knowledge Distillation (CTKD) strategy which employs two special teachers. Specifically, one teacher trained from scratch (i.e., scratch teacher) assists the student step by step using its temporary outputs. It forces the student to approach the optimal path towards the final logits with high accuracy. The other pre-trained teacher (i.e., expert teacher) guides the student to focus on a critical region which is more useful for the task. The combination of the knowledge from two special teachers can significantly improve the performance of the student network in knowledge distillation. The results of experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN and Tiny ImageNet datasets verify that the proposed knowledge distillation method is efficient and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Ibarra
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Essential Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as the fundamental technique for enabling practical deployment of deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, efficient student networks, knowledge distillation achieves substantial reductions in model size and computational requirements while maintaining competitive performance. This approach demonstrates remarkable versatility across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and generative models, addressing critical practical challenges in modern deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Crosby
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying sophisticated neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This synthesis examines the theoretical foundations, methodological approaches, and practical applications of knowledge distillation across computer vision and natural language processing domains, highlighting both the broad applicability of these compression techniques and the emerging challenges in their implementation.

papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: AdaBERT: Task-Adaptive BERT Compression with Differentiable Neural Architecture Search
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained language models such as BERT have shown their effectiveness in various natural language processing tasks. However, the huge parameter size makes them difficult to be deployed in real-time applications that require quick inference with limited resources. Existing methods compress BERT into small models while such compression is task-independent, i.e., the same compressed BERT for all different downstream tasks. Motivated by the necessity and benefits of task-oriented BERT compression, we propose a novel compression method, AdaBERT, that leverages differentiable Neural Architecture Search to automatically compress BERT into task-adaptive small models for specific tasks. We incorporate a task-oriented knowledge distillation loss to provide search hints and an efficiency-aware loss as search constraints, which enables a good trade-off between efficiency and effectiveness for task-adaptive BERT compression. We evaluate AdaBERT on several NLP tasks, and the results demonstrate that those task-adaptive compressed models are 12.7x to 29.3x faster than BERT in inference time and 11.5x to 17.0x smaller in terms of parameter size, while comparable performance is maintained.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Adversarial Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) has made remarkable progress in the last few years and become a popular paradigm for model compression and knowledge transfer. However, almost all existing KD algorithms are data-driven, i.e., relying on a large amount of original training data or alternative data, which is usually unavailable in real-world scenarios. In this paper, we devote ourselves to this challenging problem and propose a novel adversarial distillation mechanism to craft a compact student model without any real-world data. We introduce a model discrepancy to quantificationally measure the difference between student and teacher models and construct an optimizable upper bound. In our work, the student and the teacher jointly act the role of the discriminator to reduce this discrepancy, when a generator adversarially produces some "hard samples" to enlarge it. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed data-free method yields comparable performance to existing data-driven methods. More strikingly, our approach can be directly extended to semantic segmentation, which is more complicated than classification, and our approach achieves state-of-the-art results. Code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/VainF/Data-Free-Adversarial-Distillation.

papers_seen.author: Calderon
papers_seen.title: Learning Generalizable Models for Vehicle Routing Problems via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent neural methods for vehicle routing problems always train and test the deep models on the same instance distribution (i.e., uniform). To tackle the consequent cross-distribution generalization concerns, we bring the knowledge distillation to this field and propose an Adaptive Multi-Distribution Knowledge Distillation (AMDKD) scheme for learning more generalizable deep models. Particularly, our AMDKD leverages various knowledge from multiple teachers trained on exemplar distributions to yield a light-weight yet generalist student model. Meanwhile, we equip AMDKD with an adaptive strategy that allows the student to concentrate on difficult distributions, so as to absorb hard-to-master knowledge more effectively. Extensive experimental results show that, compared with the baseline neural methods, our AMDKD is able to achieve competitive results on both unseen in-distribution and out-of-distribution instances, which are either randomly synthesized or adopted from benchmark datasets (i.e., TSPLIB and CVRPLIB). Notably, our AMDKD is generic, and consumes less computational resources for inference.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Advances and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression and efficient neural network training, enabling the transfer of knowledge from larger teacher models to compact student networks. This paper surveys the current state of knowledge distillation research across multiple domains, examining its applications to language models, computer vision tasks, and federated learning scenarios. We discuss key methodological advances including intermediate layer distillation, feature-based matching approaches, and attention-based mechanisms for improved knowledge transfer. Furthermore, we explore how distillation addresses practical challenges such as domain adaptation, model heterogeneity, and resource constraints in edge computing environments. The evidence demonstrates that distillation remains a versatile and effective strategy for creating deployable, efficient models without substantial sacrifice in performance.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher networks to compact student models, enabling practical deployment of deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. Applications span natural language processing, computer vision, multi-modal learning, and specialized domains including medical imaging and machine translation. Recent advances extend beyond simple output matching to incorporate intermediate layer distillation, attention-based mechanisms, and specialized architectures for diverse compression scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks. The method leverages soft label matching, feature-level alignment, and sophisticated transfer mechanisms to achieve significant model compression with minimal accuracy degradation.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential Strategy for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for enabling practical deployment of deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. This paper argues that knowledge distillation, combined with model compression strategies, is essential for bridging the gap between state-of-the-art performance and real-world computational constraints. By examining applications across diverse domains including neural machine translation, graph neural networks, speech processing, and information retrieval, this work demonstrates that knowledge distillation provides an effective, scalable solution for transferring knowledge from large teacher models to compact student models without significant performance degradation.

papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge from Deep Networks with Applications to Healthcare Domain
papers_seen.abstract: Exponential growth in Electronic Healthcare Records (EHR) has resulted in new opportunities and urgent needs for discovery of meaningful data-driven representations and patterns of diseases in Computational Phenotyping research. Deep Learning models have shown superior performance for robust prediction in computational phenotyping tasks, but suffer from the issue of model interpretability which is crucial for clinicians involved in decision-making. In this paper, we introduce a novel knowledge-distillation approach called Interpretable Mimic Learning, to learn interpretable phenotype features for making robust prediction while mimicking the performance of deep learning models. Our framework uses Gradient Boosting Trees to learn interpretable features from deep learning models such as Stacked Denoising Autoencoder and Long Short-Term Memory. Exhaustive experiments on a real-world clinical time-series dataset show that our method obtains similar or better performance than the deep learning models, and it provides interpretable phenotypes for clinical decision making.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Unified Visual Transformer Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) have gained popularity recently. Even without customized image operators such as convolutions, ViTs can yield competitive performance when properly trained on massive data. However, the computational overhead of ViTs remains prohibitive, due to stacking multi-head self-attention modules and else. Compared to the vast literature and prevailing success in compressing convolutional neural networks, the study of Vision Transformer compression has also just emerged, and existing works focused on one or two aspects of compression. This paper proposes a unified ViT compression framework that seamlessly assembles three effective techniques: pruning, layer skipping, and knowledge distillation. We formulate a budget-constrained, end-to-end optimization framework, targeting jointly learning model weights, layer-wise pruning ratios/masks, and skip configurations, under a distillation loss. The optimization problem is then solved using the primal-dual algorithm. Experiments are conducted with several ViT variants, e.g. DeiT and T2T-ViT backbones on the ImageNet dataset, and our approach consistently outperforms recent competitors. For example, DeiT-Tiny can be trimmed down to 50\% of the original FLOPs almost without losing accuracy. Codes are available online:~\url{https://github.com/VITA-Group/UVC}.

papers_seen.title: Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer via Adversarial Belief Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Performing knowledge transfer from a large teacher network to a smaller student is a popular task in modern deep learning applications. However, due to growing dataset sizes and stricter privacy regulations, it is increasingly common not to have access to the data that was used to train the teacher. We propose a novel method which trains a student to match the predictions of its teacher without using any data or metadata. We achieve this by training an adversarial generator to search for images on which the student poorly matches the teacher, and then using them to train the student. Our resulting student closely approximates its teacher for simple datasets like SVHN, and on CIFAR10 we improve on the state-of-the-art for few-shot distillation (with 100 images per class), despite using no data. Finally, we also propose a metric to quantify the degree of belief matching between teacher and student in the vicinity of decision boundaries, and observe a significantly higher match between our zero-shot student and the teacher, than between a student distilled with real data and the teacher. Code available at: https://github.com/polo5/ZeroShotKnowledgeTransfer

papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a method to interpret the success of knowledge distillation by quantifying and analyzing task-relevant and task-irrelevant visual concepts that are encoded in intermediate layers of a deep neural network (DNN). More specifically, three hypotheses are proposed as follows. 1. Knowledge distillation makes the DNN learn more visual concepts than learning from raw data. 2. Knowledge distillation ensures that the DNN is prone to learning various visual concepts simultaneously. papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge From a Deep Pose Regressor Network
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a novel method to distill knowledge from a deep pose regressor network for efficient Visual Odometry (VO). Standard distillation relies on "dark knowledge" for successful knowledge transfer. As this knowledge is not available in pose regression and the teacher prediction is not always accurate, we propose to emphasize the knowledge transfer only when we trust the teacher. We achieve this by using teacher loss as a confidence score which places variable relative importance on the teacher prediction. We inject this confidence score to the main training task via Attentive Imitation Loss (AIL) and when learning the intermediate representation of the teacher through Attentive Hint Training (AHT) approach. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work which successfully distill the knowledge from a deep pose regression network. Our evaluation on the KITTI and Malaga dataset shows that we can keep the student prediction close to the teacher with up to 92.95% parameter reduction and 2.12x faster in computation time.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Does Knowledge Distillation Really Work?
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique for training a small student network to emulate a larger teacher model, such as an ensemble of networks. We show that while knowledge distillation can improve student generalization, it does not typically work as it is commonly understood: there often remains a surprisingly large discrepancy between the predictive distributions of the teacher and the student, even in cases when the student has the capacity to perfectly match the teacher. We identify difficulties in optimization as a key reason for why the student is unable to match the teacher. We also show how the details of the dataset used for distillation play a role in how closely the student matches the teacher -- and that more closely matching the teacher paradoxically does not always lead to better student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Carr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Fundamental Technique for Enabling Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential technique for deploying deep learning and NLP models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, distillation enables the practical deployment of state-of-the-art neural networks without proportional sacrifices in performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is not merely an optional optimization technique, but rather a fundamental necessity for bridging the critical gap between model capability and practical deployability in real-world applications.
