papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: VPN++: Rethinking Video-Pose embeddings for understanding Activities of Daily Living
papers_seen.abstract: Many attempts have been made towards combining RGB and 3D poses for the recognition of Activities of Daily Living (ADL). ADL may look very similar and often necessitate to model fine-grained details to distinguish them. Because the recent 3D ConvNets are too rigid to capture the subtle visual patterns across an action, this research direction is dominated by methods combining RGB and 3D Poses. But the cost of computing 3D poses from RGB stream is high in the absence of appropriate sensors. This limits the usage of aforementioned approaches in real-world applications requiring low latency. Then, how to best take advantage of 3D Poses for recognizing ADL? To this end, we propose an extension of a pose driven attention mechanism: Video-Pose Network (VPN), exploring two distinct directions. One is to transfer the Pose knowledge into RGB through a feature-level distillation and the other towards mimicking pose driven attention through an attention-level distillation. Finally, these two approaches are integrated into a single model, we call VPN++. We show that VPN++ is not only effective but also provides a high speed up and high resilience to noisy Poses. VPN++, with or without 3D Poses, outperforms the representative baselines on 4 public datasets. Code is available at https://github.com/srijandas07/vpnplusplus.

papers_seen.author: Duncan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Methods and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student networks. This approach is increasingly applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal learning. Current methods employ various knowledge transfer mechanisms, from simple output probability matching to sophisticated feature-level and adversarial approaches. While primarily used to reduce memory footprint and computational requirements for deployment on resource-constrained devices, knowledge distillation also demonstrates benefits for robustness, fairness, and generalization. Recent work has extended distillation beyond traditional supervised settings to federated learning, multi-task learning, and generative models, establishing it as a versatile framework for neural network optimization and knowledge transfer.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Current Approaches and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach addresses the critical challenge of deploying powerful deep learning models on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive performance. Beyond traditional teacher-student paradigms, knowledge distillation has been extended to diverse applications including federated learning, natural language processing, object detection, and adversarial robustness. Recent advances explore data-free distillation, online collaborative learning among student networks, and task-adaptive compression strategies. The field continues to expand with novel methods for understanding the theoretical foundations of distillation and developing practical compression techniques applicable across various deep learning domains.

papers_seen.author: Torres
papers_seen.title: The Indispensable Role of Knowledge Distillation in Modern Deep Learning: Enabling Efficient Deployment While Preserving Performance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and natural language processing. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student networks, simultaneously reducing memory footprint and inference time while maintaining competitive performance. The technique addresses critical challenges in deploying neural networks to resource-constrained environments and extends beyond simple model compression to applications in federated learning, domain adaptation, and robustness enhancement. Evidence across diverse domains demonstrates that knowledge distillation represents not merely a performance optimization technique, but a paradigm shift in how neural networks can be efficiently trained and deployed for practical real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning: A Comprehensive Strategy for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile technique in deep learning, enabling the compression of large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from complex teacher networks to simpler student networks, addressing critical challenges in deploying deep learning models on resource-constrained devices. Recent advances span multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning, with innovations in distillation mechanisms, architectural designs, and theoretical foundations. The technique has proven effective not only for model compression but also for improving interpretability, enabling lifelong learning, and facilitating federated learning scenarios. Despite its widespread adoption, ongoing research continues to refine distillation methods and expand their applicability across diverse tasks and model types.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Transformative Paradigm for Deep Learning and NLP Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as one of the most effective and versatile techniques for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and NLP. Rather than treating it merely as a tool for improving accuracy, knowledge distillation represents a fundamental shift in how we approach model training and deployment. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be adopted as a core paradigm in deep learning systems because it simultaneously addresses multiple critical challenges: reducing computational complexity, enabling privacy-preserving model transfer, improving model interpretability, and facilitating the training of efficient models that match or exceed the performance of their larger counterparts. We examine diverse applications across computer vision, NLP, and graph neural networks to demonstrate the broad applicability and robustness of distillation-based approaches.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from larger, more capable teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach has become increasingly important for deploying deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation operates by leveraging various forms of knowledge from teachers, including output predictions, intermediate representations, and behavioral patterns, to train compact student models that maintain competitive performance while significantly reducing computational and memory requirements. Applications span multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, recommender systems, and reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Crucial Technique for Effective Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential approach for compressing deep learning models while maintaining predictive performance. This technique involves training a smaller student model to mimic a larger, more capable teacher model, enabling efficient deployment without sacrificing accuracy. The method has proven particularly valuable across multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and machine translation, offering systematic solutions to reduce computational overhead and memory requirements in neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation for Deep Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in model compression have provided procedures for compressing large neural networks to a fraction of their original size while retaining most if not all of their accuracy. However, all of these approaches rely on access to the original training set, which might not always be possible if the network to be compressed was trained on a very large dataset, or on a dataset whose release poses privacy or safety concerns as may be the case for biometrics tasks. We present a method for data-free knowledge distillation, which is able to compress deep neural networks trained on large-scale datasets to a fraction of their size leveraging only some extra metadata to be provided with a pretrained model release. We also explore different kinds of metadata that can be used with our method, and discuss tradeoffs involved in using each of them.

papers_seen.author: Shaw
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are essential techniques for creating efficient neural networks that maintain high performance while reducing computational and storage requirements. These methods involve training compact student networks to emulate larger, more powerful teacher networks through knowledge transfer mechanisms. Applications span multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and graph neural networks, enabling the deployment of powerful models on resource-constrained devices.

papers_seen.author: Allison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Fundamental Technique for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and natural language processing. This paper argues that knowledge distillation enables the creation of efficient, deployable models without sacrificing performance through strategic knowledge transfer from larger teacher networks to compact student networks. Beyond traditional compression, knowledge distillation extends to specialized domains including continual learning, privacy-preserving applications, and task-specific adaptation, demonstrating its versatility and fundamental importance in modern machine learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Richards
papers_seen.title: TextKD-GAN: Text Generation using KnowledgeDistillation and Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Text generation is of particular interest in many NLP applications such as machine translation, language modeling, and text summarization. Generative adversarial networks (GANs) achieved a remarkable success in high quality image generation in computer vision,and recently, GANs have gained lots of interest from the NLP community as well. However, achieving similar success in NLP would be more challenging due to the discrete nature of text. In this work, we introduce a method using knowledge distillation to effectively exploit GAN setup for text generation. We demonstrate how autoencoders (AEs) can be used for providing a continuous representation of sentences, which is a smooth representation that assign non-zero probabilities to more than one word. We distill this representation to train the generator to synthesize similar smooth representations. We perform a number of experiments to validate our idea using different datasets and show that our proposed approach yields better performance in terms of the BLEU score and Jensen-Shannon distance (JSD) measure compared to traditional GAN-based text generation approaches without pre-training.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are critical techniques for deploying deep neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This review synthesizes the current state of research across diverse applications including computer vision, natural language processing, generative models, and domain adaptation, examining both foundational approaches and recent advances in data-free and specialized distillation methods.

papers_seen.author: Fisher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying large neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining performance. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, these approaches enable significant reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference latency. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents an essential paradigm for making state-of-the-art deep learning models practical and accessible across diverse applications including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Compressing GANs using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been used in several machine learning tasks such as domain transfer, super resolution, and synthetic data generation. State-of-the-art GANs often use tens of millions of parameters, making them expensive to deploy for applications in low SWAP (size, weight, and power) hardware, such as mobile devices, and for applications with real time capabilities. There has been no work found to reduce the number of parameters used in GANs. Therefore, we propose a method to compress GANs using knowledge distillation techniques, in which a smaller "student" GAN learns to mimic a larger "teacher" GAN. We show that the distillation methods used on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Celeb-A datasets can compress teacher GANs at ratios of 1669:1, 58:1, and 87:1, respectively, while retaining the quality of the generated image. From our experiments, we observe a qualitative limit for GAN's compression. Moreover, we observe that, with a fixed parameter budget, compressed GANs outperform GANs trained using standard training methods. We conjecture that this is partially owing to the optimization landscape of over-parameterized GANs which allows efficient training using alternating gradient descent. Thus, training an over-parameterized GAN followed by our proposed compression scheme provides a high quality generative model with a small number of parameters.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models by transferring knowledge from a teacher network to a student network. This approach has become increasingly important for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments, particularly in natural language processing and computer vision tasks. The method works by leveraging soft target probabilities and intermediate representations from the teacher to regularize and guide student model training. Beyond traditional teacher-student frameworks, recent developments include self-distillation methods, multi-teacher approaches, and task-adaptive compression strategies. Knowledge distillation has demonstrated significant practical benefits, achieving substantial reductions in model size and inference time while maintaining competitive performance across diverse applications including image classification, object detection, language modeling, and machine translation.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Is Label Smoothing Truly Incompatible with Knowledge Distillation: An Empirical Study
papers_seen.abstract: This work aims to empirically clarify a recently discovered perspective that label smoothing is incompatible with knowledge distillation. We begin by introducing the motivation behind on how this incompatibility is raised, i.e., label smoothing erases relative information between teacher logits. We provide a novel connection on how label smoothing affects distributions of semantically similar and dissimilar classes. Then we propose a metric to quantitatively measure the degree of erased information in sample's representation. After that, we study its one-sidedness and imperfection of the incompatibility view through massive analyses, visualizations and comprehensive experiments on Image Classification, Binary Networks, and Neural Machine Translation. Finally, we broadly discuss several circumstances wherein label smoothing will indeed lose its effectiveness. Project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/LS_and_KD/index.html.

papers_seen.author: Galvan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Critical Technique for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression in deep learning and NLP, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach addresses the critical challenge of deploying high-performance neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive accuracy. Recent advances extend beyond traditional teacher-student paradigms to include data-free distillation, multi-teacher approaches, and domain-specific compression strategies, making knowledge distillation essential for real-world applications where computational efficiency is paramount.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that trains a smaller student network to mimic a larger teacher network, enabling deployment of high-performing models on resource-constrained devices. This approach has been successfully applied across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and generative models. The technique leverages knowledge transfer mechanisms to maintain performance while reducing computational and memory requirements, making it valuable for practical applications where efficiency is critical.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-used technique for transferring knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach has emerged as a key strategy for model compression in deep learning, with particular applications in natural language processing. By leveraging soft target probabilities and intermediate representations from teacher networks, distillation enables the deployment of high-performing models on resource-constrained devices without significant performance degradation. Recent advances have extended distillation beyond simple classification tasks to complex domains including machine translation, graph neural networks, and multimodal learning.

papers_seen.author: Zamora
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Understanding and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing neural networks by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models. This approach has been extensively applied across deep learning and NLP tasks to reduce computational costs, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining performance. This synthesis examines the theoretical foundations, practical implementations, and applications of knowledge distillation, including selective distillation strategies, data augmentation interactions, feature-level knowledge transfer, and domain-specific applications in machine translation, reading comprehension, and language model compression.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Farrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Crucial Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a vital technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By enabling the transfer of knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student models, distillation addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems to resource-constrained environments. This approach spans multiple domains including natural language processing, speech processing, graph neural networks, and computer vision, offering flexible solutions for various model compression scenarios from standard settings to data-free contexts.

papers_seen.author: Mueller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression and efficient deployment of deep learning systems. This approach involves training a smaller, lightweight student model to match the predictions of a larger, more complex teacher model, enabling significant reductions in computational cost and model size while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, reinforcement learning, and beyond, demonstrating its versatility as a general-purpose compression technique.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Approaches and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models by transferring knowledge from teacher models to student models. This approach addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, federated learning, and specialized applications like medical image segmentation and style transfer. Knowledge distillation enables significant reductions in model size and computational requirements while maintaining or improving performance compared to baseline models.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Understanding and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing neural networks by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models. This approach addresses critical deployment challenges by reducing computational requirements, memory footprint, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal learning, making knowledge distillation an essential strategy for deploying powerful deep learning models on resource-constrained devices.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a training technique that transfers knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models, enabling efficient deployment of deep learning systems while maintaining competitive performance. This approach addresses critical challenges in modern machine learning by reducing computational costs, memory requirements, and inference latency. Applications span computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains including object detection, machine translation, and federated learning, demonstrating the broad applicability of knowledge distillation as a fundamental model compression technique.

papers_seen.author: Leblanc
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Deploying Deep Learning Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining comparable performance. This review examines key approaches including structural distillation, feature-based distillation, and application-specific compression strategies across various domains. The evidence demonstrates that knowledge distillation consistently enables substantial model size reduction with minimal accuracy loss, making it an indispensable tool for practical deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Cross-modal Knowledge Distillation for Vision-to-Sensor Action Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Human activity recognition (HAR) based on multi-modal approach has been recently shown to improve the accuracy performance of HAR. However, restricted computational resources associated with wearable devices, i.e., smartwatch, failed to directly support such advanced methods. To tackle this issue, this study introduces an end-to-end Vision-to-Sensor Knowledge Distillation (VSKD) framework. In this VSKD framework, only time-series data, i.e., accelerometer data, is needed from wearable devices during the testing phase. Therefore, this framework will not only reduce the computational demands on edge devices, but also produce a learning model that closely matches the performance of the computational expensive multi-modal approach. In order to retain the local temporal relationship and facilitate visual deep learning models, we first convert time-series data to two-dimensional images by applying the Gramian Angular Field ( GAF) based encoding method. We adopted ResNet18 and multi-scale TRN with BN-Inception as teacher and student network in this study, respectively. A novel loss function, named Distance and Angle-wised Semantic Knowledge loss (DASK), is proposed to mitigate the modality variations between the vision and the sensor domain. Extensive experimental results on UTD-MHAD, MMAct, and Berkeley-MHAD datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and competitiveness of the proposed VSKD model which can deployed on wearable sensors.

papers_seen.author: Galvan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Critical Technique for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression in deep learning and NLP, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach addresses the critical challenge of deploying high-performance neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive accuracy. Recent advances extend beyond traditional teacher-student paradigms to include data-free distillation, multi-teacher approaches, and domain-specific compression strategies, making knowledge distillation essential for real-world applications where computational efficiency is paramount.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Advancing Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving performance. This approach transfers knowledge from a larger teacher model to a smaller student model, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices without sacrificing accuracy. The method extends across multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and federated learning, with applications ranging from mobile deployment to privacy-preserving distributed systems.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Highlight Every Step: Knowledge Distillation via Collaborative Teaching
papers_seen.abstract: High storage and computational costs obstruct deep neural networks to be deployed on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation aims to train a compact student network by transferring knowledge from a larger pre-trained teacher model. However, most existing methods on knowledge distillation ignore the valuable information among training process associated with training results. In this paper, we provide a new Collaborative Teaching Knowledge Distillation (CTKD) strategy which employs two special teachers. Specifically, one teacher trained from scratch (i.e., scratch teacher) assists the student step by step using its temporary outputs. It forces the student to approach the optimal path towards the final logits with high accuracy. The other pre-trained teacher (i.e., expert teacher) guides the student to focus on a critical region which is more useful for the task. The combination of the knowledge from two special teachers can significantly improve the performance of the student network in knowledge distillation. The results of experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN and Tiny ImageNet datasets verify that the proposed knowledge distillation method is efficient and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Mckee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental paradigm for model compression that enables the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach addresses the critical challenge of deploying high-performance deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation operates through diverse mechanisms including logit matching, feature-level transfer, adversarial training, and meta-learning frameworks. Applications span multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, generative models, and specialized tasks, with innovations addressing challenges such as heterogeneous architectures, domain adaptation, and data scarcity.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher networks to compact student models, enabling practical deployment of deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. Applications span natural language processing, computer vision, multi-modal learning, and specialized domains including medical imaging and machine translation. Recent advances extend beyond simple output matching to incorporate intermediate layer distillation, attention-based mechanisms, and specialized architectures for diverse compression scenarios.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Robust Cross-Modal Representation Learning with Progressive Self-Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The learning objective of vision-language approach of CLIP does not effectively account for the noisy many-to-many correspondences found in web-harvested image captioning datasets, which contributes to its compute and data inefficiency. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel training framework based on cross-modal contrastive learning that uses progressive self-distillation and soft image-text alignments to more efficiently learn robust representations from noisy data. Our model distills its own knowledge to dynamically generate soft-alignment targets for a subset of images and captions in every minibatch, which are then used to update its parameters. Extensive evaluation across 14 benchmark datasets shows that our method consistently outperforms its CLIP counterpart in multiple settings, including: (a) zero-shot classification, (b) linear probe transfer, and (c) image-text retrieval, without incurring added computational cost. Analysis using an ImageNet-based robustness test-bed reveals that our method offers better effective robustness to natural distribution shifts compared to both ImageNet-trained models and CLIP itself. Lastly, pretraining with datasets spanning two orders of magnitude in size shows that our improvements over CLIP tend to scale with number of training examples.

papers_seen.author: Cowan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression in deep learning, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large teacher models to compact student models. This approach has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and federated learning, addressing critical challenges in model efficiency while maintaining performance. The technique involves various strategies ranging from soft label matching to feature-level alignment, with ongoing research exploring optimal distillation procedures, selective knowledge transfer, and integration with complementary training methodologies.

papers_seen.author: Orr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Techniques, Applications, and Advances
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation addresses fundamental challenges in model deployment across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks. Recent advances extend beyond traditional probability matching to encompass feature-level transfer, task-aware compression, and novel distillation frameworks that improve efficiency without substantial accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Fundamental Necessity for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical and indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This method transfers knowledge from well-trained teacher models to lightweight student networks, enabling the practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications. While alternative compression methods exist, knowledge distillation stands out as a uniquely flexible and effective approach that preserves performance while dramatically reducing computational and memory requirements.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger, high-performing teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices without substantial performance degradation. Recent advances in knowledge distillation have expanded beyond simple output-level transfer to include intermediate representations, attention mechanisms, feature matching, and adversarial learning strategies. The technique has proven particularly valuable in NLP applications where pre-trained language models face computational and memory constraints, and in federated learning scenarios with heterogeneous devices. This synthesis reviews the fundamental mechanisms of knowledge distillation, its applications across different architectures and tasks, and emerging strategies for improving distillation effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Davenport
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP

Recent research reveals that distillation functions not only through explicit knowledge transfer but also as a form of learned regularization, with theoretical analyses providing deeper understanding of its mechanisms and benefits.

papers_seen.author: Phillips

Recent advances have extended knowledge distillation beyond simple output matching to include intermediate layer distillation, attention-based methods, and specialized approaches for specific architectures. Applications span from distilling transformer-based language models to compressing vision transformers, graph neural networks, and multi-modal representations.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are essential techniques for deploying deep learning and NLP models in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from larger, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This synthesis examines the theoretical foundations, methodological innovations, and practical applications of knowledge distillation across diverse domains, covering training strategies, multi-teacher approaches, data-free methods, and task-specific compression techniques, while addressing emerging challenges in maintaining model accuracy without sacrificing efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Higgins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Transferring Knowledge from Large Models to Efficient Student Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large teacher models to compact student networks. This approach addresses the critical challenge of deploying sophisticated neural networks in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. By leveraging the rich information encoded in teacher models, knowledge distillation provides effective compression across diverse applications including language understanding, machine translation, recommendation systems, and graph neural networks. The technique balances model efficiency with accuracy, making it essential for practical deployment scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Fair Feature Distillation for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Fairness is becoming an increasingly crucial issue for computer vision, especially in the human-related decision systems. However, achieving algorithmic fairness, which makes a model produce indiscriminative outcomes against protected groups, is still an unresolved problem. In this paper, we devise a systematic approach which reduces algorithmic biases via feature distillation for visual recognition tasks, dubbed as MMD-based Fair Distillation (MFD). While the distillation technique has been widely used in general to improve the prediction accuracy, to the best of our knowledge, there has been no explicit work that also tries to improve fairness via distillation. Furthermore, We give a theoretical justification of our MFD on the effect of knowledge distillation and fairness. Throughout the extensive experiments, we show our MFD significantly mitigates the bias against specific minorities without any loss of the accuracy on both synthetic and real-world face datasets.

papers_seen.author: Ball
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Essential for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and essential technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing. The versatility and effectiveness of knowledge distillation demonstrate its importance as a cornerstone technique for making state-of-the-art deep learning models practical for real-world deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Powerful Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a highly effective approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive accuracy. Evidence demonstrates that distillation can be applied effectively in NLP, computer vision, and specialized domains, and offers unique advantages over traditional compression techniques through its ability to capture and transfer both feature-level and prediction-level knowledge.

papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge by Mimicking Features
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a popular method to train efficient networks ("student") with the help of high-capacity networks ("teacher"). Traditional methods use the teacher's soft logits as extra supervision to train the student network. In this paper, we argue that it is more advantageous to make the student mimic the teacher's features in the penultimate layer. Not only the student can directly learn more effective information from the teacher feature, feature mimicking can also be applied for teachers trained without a softmax layer. Experiments show that it can achieve higher accuracy than traditional KD. To further facilitate feature mimicking, we decompose a feature vector into the magnitude and the direction. We argue that the teacher should give more freedom to the student feature's magnitude, and let the student pay more attention on mimicking the feature direction. To meet this requirement, we propose a loss term based on locality-sensitive hashing (LSH). With the help of this new loss, our method indeed mimics feature directions more accurately, relaxes constraints on feature magnitudes, and achieves state-of-the-art distillation accuracy. We provide theoretical analyses of how LSH facilitates feature direction mimicking, and further extend feature mimicking to multi-label recognition and object detection.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Deep Hierarchical Approach to Lifelong Learning in Minecraft
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a lifelong learning system that has the ability to reuse and transfer knowledge from one task to another while efficiently retaining the previously learned knowledge-base. Knowledge is transferred by learning reusable skills to solve tasks in Minecraft, a popular video game which is an unsolved and high-dimensional lifelong learning problem. These reusable skills, which we refer to as Deep Skill Networks, are then incorporated into our novel Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Network (H-DRLN) architecture using two techniques: (1) a deep skill array and (2) skill distillation, our novel variation of policy distillation (Rusu et. al. 2015) for learning skills. Skill distillation enables the HDRLN to efficiently retain knowledge and therefore scale in lifelong learning, by accumulating knowledge and encapsulating multiple reusable skills into a single distilled network. The H-DRLN exhibits superior performance and lower learning sample complexity compared to the regular Deep Q Network (Mnih et. al. 2015) in sub-domains of Minecraft.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Critical Approach to Efficient Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing neural networks while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, enabling practical deployment in resource-constrained environments. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents an essential methodology for addressing the deployment challenges of modern deep learning across diverse domains including natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression represent critical techniques for deploying deep neural networks efficiently across resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, high-capacity models (teachers) to smaller, more efficient models (students) while preserving predictive performance. This synthesis examines the fundamental approaches, applications, and innovations in knowledge distillation and model compression across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that trains a smaller student network to mimic a larger teacher network, enabling deployment of high-performing models on resource-constrained devices. This approach has been successfully applied across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and generative models. The technique leverages knowledge transfer mechanisms to maintain performance while reducing computational and memory requirements, making it valuable for practical applications where efficiency is critical.

papers_seen.author: Wong
papers_seen.title: Embracing the Dark Knowledge: Domain Generalization Using Regularized Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Though convolutional neural networks are widely used in different tasks, lack of generalization capability in the absence of sufficient and representative data is one of the challenges that hinder their practical application. In this paper, we propose a simple, effective, and plug-and-play training strategy named Knowledge Distillation for Domain Generalization (KDDG) which is built upon a knowledge distillation framework with the gradient filter as a novel regularization term. We find that both the ``richer dark knowledge" from the teacher network, as well as the gradient filter we proposed, can reduce the difficulty of learning the mapping which further improves the generalization ability of the model. We also conduct experiments extensively to show that our framework can significantly improve the generalization capability of deep neural networks in different tasks including image classification, segmentation, reinforcement learning by comparing our method with existing state-of-the-art domain generalization techniques. Last but not the least, we propose to adopt two metrics to analyze our proposed method in order to better understand how our proposed method benefits the generalization capability of deep neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Effective Techniques for Deploying Efficient Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This paper reviews the theoretical foundations, practical applications, and recent advances in knowledge distillation across various deep learning domains, demonstrating how these compression techniques enable efficient inference and broader accessibility of state-of-the-art models.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining predictive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher networks to compact student networks through various mechanisms, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices. Beyond traditional compression applications, knowledge distillation has been successfully extended to diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, domain adaptation, and privacy-preserving machine learning, demonstrating its versatility as a core paradigm for efficient deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Critical Tool for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential technique for making deep learning models practical in real-world deployments. By enabling the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller student networks, distillation addresses fundamental constraints in model deployment including computational efficiency, memory requirements, and inference speed. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is not merely an optimization technique but a foundational approach necessary for making state-of-the-art models accessible across diverse computing environments and applications.

papers_seen.author: Wise
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Review
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and natural language processing. This approach enables the deployment of large neural networks on resource-constrained devices by training smaller student networks to mimic the behavior of larger, more accurate teacher networks. Beyond simple output matching, modern distillation methods incorporate intermediate layer alignment, attention-based mechanisms, and adaptive weighting strategies. The technique demonstrates broad applicability across diverse domains including language models, computer vision, recommender systems, and multimodal learning, addressing critical challenges in model deployment while maintaining competitive performance.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Approaches and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models by transferring knowledge from teacher models to student models. This approach addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, federated learning, and specialized applications like medical image segmentation and style transfer. Knowledge distillation enables significant reductions in model size and computational requirements while maintaining or improving performance compared to baseline models.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Towards Model Agnostic Federated Learning Using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Is it possible to design an universal API for federated learning using which an ad-hoc group of data-holders (agents) collaborate with each other and perform federated learning? Such an API would necessarily need to be model-agnostic i.e. make no assumption about the model architecture being used by the agents, and also cannot rely on having representative public data at hand. Knowledge distillation (KD) is the obvious tool of choice to design such protocols. However, surprisingly, we show that most natural KD-based federated learning protocols have poor performance.   To investigate this, we propose a new theoretical framework, Federated Kernel ridge regression, which can capture both model heterogeneity as well as data heterogeneity. Our analysis shows that the degradation is largely due to a fundamental limitation of knowledge distillation under data heterogeneity. We further validate our framework by analyzing and designing new protocols based on KD. Their performance on real world experiments using neural networks, though still unsatisfactory, closely matches our theoretical predictions.

papers_seen.author: Mason
papers_seen.title: Learning Student Networks via Feature Embedding
papers_seen.abstract: Deep convolutional neural networks have been widely used in numerous applications, but their demanding storage and computational resource requirements prevent their applications on mobile devices. Knowledge distillation aims to optimize a portable student network by taking the knowledge from a well-trained heavy teacher network. Traditional teacher-student based methods used to rely on additional fully-connected layers to bridge intermediate layers of teacher and student networks, which brings in a large number of auxiliary parameters. In contrast, this paper aims to propagate information from teacher to student without introducing new variables which need to be optimized. We regard the teacher-student paradigm from a new perspective of feature embedding. By introducing the locality preserving loss, the student network is encouraged to generate the low-dimensional features which could inherit intrinsic properties of their corresponding high-dimensional features from teacher network. The resulting portable network thus can naturally maintain the performance as that of the teacher network. Theoretical analysis is provided to justify the lower computation complexity of the proposed method. Experiments on benchmark datasets and well-trained networks suggest that the proposed algorithm is superior to state-of-the-art teacher-student learning methods in terms of computational and storage complexity.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for enabling the deployment of large neural networks on resource-constrained devices. These methods address the fundamental challenge of maintaining model performance while dramatically reducing computational and storage requirements. By leveraging knowledge transfer from large teacher models to compact student models, practitioners can achieve efficient inference without substantial accuracy loss. This survey synthesizes recent advances in both classical compression approaches and innovative distillation strategies tailored for deep learning and NLP applications.

papers_seen.author: Reid
papers_seen.title: Moonshine: Distilling with Cheap Convolutions
papers_seen.abstract: Many engineers wish to deploy modern neural networks in memory-limited settings; but the development of flexible methods for reducing memory use is in its infancy, and there is little knowledge of the resulting cost-benefit. We propose structural model distillation for memory reduction using a strategy that produces a student architecture that is a simple transformation of the teacher architecture: no redesign is needed, and the same hyperparameters can be used. Using attention transfer, we provide Pareto curves/tables for distillation of residual networks with four benchmark datasets, indicating the memory versus accuracy payoff. We show that substantial memory savings are possible with very little loss of accuracy, and confirm that distillation provides student network performance that is better than training that student architecture directly on data.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning in Resource-Constrained Environments
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span computer vision, natural language processing, federated learning, and specialized domains such as recommender systems and graph neural networks. Recent advances include intermediate layer distillation, attention-based mechanisms, and task-adaptive compression strategies that further enhance the effectiveness of knowledge transfer.

papers_seen.author: Wolfe
papers_seen.title: Robust and Resource-Efficient Data-Free Knowledge Distillation by Generative Pseudo Replay
papers_seen.abstract: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation (KD) allows knowledge transfer from a trained neural network (teacher) to a more compact one (student) in the absence of original training data. Existing works use a validation set to monitor the accuracy of the student over real data and report the highest performance throughout the entire process. However, validation data may not be available at distillation time either, making it infeasible to record the student snapshot that achieved the peak accuracy. Therefore, a practical data-free KD method should be robust and ideally provide monotonically increasing student accuracy during distillation. This is challenging because the student experiences knowledge degradation due to the distribution shift of the synthetic data. A straightforward approach to overcome this issue is to store and rehearse the generated samples periodically, which increases the memory footprint and creates privacy concerns. We propose to model the distribution of the previously observed synthetic samples with a generative network. In particular, we design a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) with a training objective that is customized to learn the synthetic data representations optimally. The student is rehearsed by the generative pseudo replay technique, with samples produced by the VAE. Hence knowledge degradation can be prevented without storing any samples. Experiments on image classification benchmarks show that our method optimizes the expected value of the distilled model accuracy while eliminating the large memory overhead incurred by the sample-storing methods.

papers_seen.author: Cameron
papers_seen.title: Well-Read Students Learn Better: On the Importance of Pre-training Compact Models
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in natural language representations have been accompanied by large and expensive models that leverage vast amounts of general-domain text through self-supervised pre-training. Due to the cost of applying such models to down-stream tasks, several model compression techniques on pre-trained language representations have been proposed (Sun et al., 2019; Sanh, 2019). However, surprisingly, the simple baseline of just pre-training and fine-tuning compact models has been overlooked. In this paper, we first show that pre-training remains important in the context of smaller architectures, and fine-tuning pre-trained compact models can be competitive to more elaborate methods proposed in concurrent work. Starting with pre-trained compact models, we then explore transferring task knowledge from large fine-tuned models through standard knowledge distillation. The resulting simple, yet effective and general algorithm, Pre-trained Distillation, brings further improvements. Through extensive experiments, we more generally explore the interaction between pre-training and distillation under two variables that have been under-studied: model size and properties of unlabeled task data. One surprising observation is that they have a compound effect even when sequentially applied on the same data. To accelerate future research, we will make our 24 pre-trained miniature BERT models publicly available.

By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to compact student networks, distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. This approach has proven effective across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, establishing itself as a critical tool for making deep learning practical in real-world scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Rethinking Soft Labels for Knowledge Distillation: A Bias-Variance Tradeoff Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective approach to leverage a well-trained network or an ensemble of them, named as the teacher, to guide the training of a student network. The outputs from the teacher network are used as soft labels for supervising the training of a new network. Recent studies \citep{muller2019does,yuan2020revisiting} revealed an intriguing property of the soft labels that making labels soft serves as a good regularization to the student network. From the perspective of statistical learning, regularization aims to reduce the variance, however how bias and variance change is not clear for training with soft labels. In this paper, we investigate the bias-variance tradeoff brought by distillation with soft labels. Specifically, we observe that during training the bias-variance tradeoff varies sample-wisely. Further, under the same distillation temperature setting, we observe that the distillation performance is negatively associated with the number of some specific samples, which are named as regularization samples since these samples lead to bias increasing and variance decreasing. Nevertheless, we empirically find that completely filtering out regularization samples also deteriorates distillation performance. Our discoveries inspired us to propose the novel weighted soft labels to help the network adaptively handle the sample-wise bias-variance tradeoff. Experiments on standard evaluation benchmarks validate the effectiveness of our method. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/bellymonster/Weighted-Soft-Label-Distillation}.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are critical techniques for enabling the deployment of sophisticated deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, maintaining high performance while dramatically reducing inference time and memory requirements. This review examines the current state of knowledge distillation across computer vision and natural language processing domains, discussing key mechanisms, practical applications, and emerging challenges in the field.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Adapt-and-Distill: Developing Small, Fast and Effective Pretrained Language Models for Domains
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained models have achieved great success in many natural language processing tasks. However, when they are applied in specific domains, these models suffer from domain shift and bring challenges in fine-tuning and online serving for latency and capacity constraints. In this paper, we present a general approach to developing small, fast and effective pre-trained models for specific domains. This is achieved by adapting the off-the-shelf general pre-trained models and performing task-agnostic knowledge distillation in target domains. Specifically, we propose domain-specific vocabulary expansion in the adaptation stage and employ corpus level occurrence probability to choose the size of incremental vocabulary automatically. Then we systematically explore different strategies to compress the large pre-trained models for specific domains. We conduct our experiments in the biomedical and computer science domain. The experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves better performance over the BERT BASE model in domain-specific tasks while 3.3x smaller and 5.1x faster than BERT BASE. The code and pre-trained models are available at https://aka.ms/adalm.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Collaborative Distillation for Ultra-Resolution Universal Style Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Universal style transfer methods typically leverage rich representations from deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (e.g., VGG-19) pre-trained on large collections of images. Despite the effectiveness, its application is heavily constrained by the large model size to handle ultra-resolution images given limited memory. In this work, we present a new knowledge distillation method (named Collaborative Distillation) for encoder-decoder based neural style transfer to reduce the convolutional filters. The main idea is underpinned by a finding that the encoder-decoder pairs construct an exclusive collaborative relationship, which is regarded as a new kind of knowledge for style transfer models. Moreover, to overcome the feature size mismatch when applying collaborative distillation, a linear embedding loss is introduced to drive the student network to learn a linear embedding of the teacher's features. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method when applied to different universal style transfer approaches (WCT and AdaIN), even if the model size is reduced by 15.5 times. Especially, on WCT with the compressed models, we achieve ultra-resolution (over 40 megapixels) universal style transfer on a 12GB GPU for the first time. Further experiments on optimization-based stylization scheme show the generality of our algorithm on different stylization paradigms. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/mingsun-tse/collaborative-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: On Representation Knowledge Distillation for Graph Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a learning paradigm for boosting resource-efficient graph neural networks (GNNs) using more expressive yet cumbersome teacher models. Past work on distillation for GNNs proposed the Local Structure Preserving loss (LSP), which matches local structural relationships defined over edges across the student and teacher's node embeddings. This paper studies whether preserving the global topology of how the teacher embeds graph data can be a more effective distillation objective for GNNs, as real-world graphs often contain latent interactions and noisy edges. We propose Graph Contrastive Representation Distillation (G-CRD), which uses contrastive learning to implicitly preserve global topology by aligning the student node embeddings to those of the teacher in a shared representation space. Additionally, we introduce an expanded set of benchmarks on large-scale real-world datasets where the performance gap between teacher and student GNNs is non-negligible. Experiments across 4 datasets and 14 heterogeneous GNN architectures show that G-CRD consistently boosts the performance and robustness of lightweight GNNs, outperforming LSP (and a global structure preserving variant of LSP) as well as baselines from 2D computer vision. An analysis of the representational similarity among teacher and student embedding spaces reveals that G-CRD balances preserving local and global relationships, while structure preserving approaches are best at preserving one or the other. Our code is available at https://github.com/chaitjo/efficient-gnns

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Unified Visual Transformer Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) have gained popularity recently. Even without customized image operators such as convolutions, ViTs can yield competitive performance when properly trained on massive data. However, the computational overhead of ViTs remains prohibitive, due to stacking multi-head self-attention modules and else. Compared to the vast literature and prevailing success in compressing convolutional neural networks, the study of Vision Transformer compression has also just emerged, and existing works focused on one or two aspects of compression. This paper proposes a unified ViT compression framework that seamlessly assembles three effective techniques: pruning, layer skipping, and knowledge distillation. We formulate a budget-constrained, end-to-end optimization framework, targeting jointly learning model weights, layer-wise pruning ratios/masks, and skip configurations, under a distillation loss. The optimization problem is then solved using the primal-dual algorithm. Experiments are conducted with several ViT variants, e.g. DeiT and T2T-ViT backbones on the ImageNet dataset, and our approach consistently outperforms recent competitors. For example, DeiT-Tiny can be trimmed down to 50\% of the original FLOPs almost without losing accuracy. Codes are available online:~\url{https://github.com/VITA-Group/UVC}.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Enabling Efficient Deep Learning Through Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and NLP. By enabling compact student models to learn from larger teacher models, distillation addresses the critical challenge of deploying sophisticated neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive performance. This paper surveys the theoretical foundations and practical applications of knowledge distillation, demonstrating how this approach achieves significant model size reduction and inference speedup across diverse domains including vision, language processing, and neural architecture optimization.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Knowledge Distillation for CTR Prediction
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, deep learning-based models have been widely studied for click-through rate (CTR) prediction and lead to improved prediction accuracy in many industrial applications. However, current research focuses primarily on building complex network architectures to better capture sophisticated feature interactions and dynamic user behaviors. The increased model complexity may slow down online inference and hinder its adoption in real-time applications. Instead, our work targets at a new model training strategy based on knowledge distillation (KD). KD is a teacher-student learning framework to transfer knowledge learned from a teacher model to a student model. The KD strategy not only allows us to simplify the student model as a vanilla DNN model but also achieves significant accuracy improvements over the state-of-the-art teacher models. The benefits thus motivate us to further explore the use of a powerful ensemble of teachers for more accurate student model training. We also propose some novel techniques to facilitate ensembled CTR prediction, including teacher gating and early stopping by distillation loss. We conduct comprehensive experiments against 12 existing models and across three industrial datasets. Both offline and online A/B testing results show the effectiveness of our KD-based training strategy.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Critical Technique for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining predictive performance. This approach involves training a student model to mimic the behavior of a larger teacher model, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments. Despite its widespread adoption across various domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks, the mechanisms underlying knowledge distillation remain partially understood. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents an essential yet imperfect solution to the model compression challenge, with significant implications for practical deep learning applications while presenting important theoretical and practical limitations.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying large neural networks on resource-constrained devices. These methods enable smaller student models to learn from larger, more capable teacher models, achieving significant reductions in model size and inference time while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and graph neural networks, with various approaches addressing challenges such as heterogeneous architectures, domain adaptation, and ensemble compression.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression represent fundamental techniques for deploying deep neural networks efficiently across resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while preserving or enhancing predictive performance. This synthesis examines the core mechanisms, diverse applications, and innovations in knowledge distillation across domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks, demonstrating how distillation functions as both a compression technique and a powerful regularization mechanism.
