papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: AlphaNet: Improved Training of Supernets with Alpha-Divergence
papers_seen.abstract: Weight-sharing neural architecture search (NAS) is an effective technique for automating efficient neural architecture design. Weight-sharing NAS builds a supernet that assembles all the architectures as its sub-networks and jointly trains the supernet with the sub-networks. The success of weight-sharing NAS heavily relies on distilling the knowledge of the supernet to the sub-networks. However, we find that the widely used distillation divergence, i.e., KL divergence, may lead to student sub-networks that over-estimate or under-estimate the uncertainty of the teacher supernet, leading to inferior performance of the sub-networks. In this work, we propose to improve the supernet training with a more generalized alpha-divergence. By adaptively selecting the alpha-divergence, we simultaneously prevent the over-estimation or under-estimation of the uncertainty of the teacher model. We apply the proposed alpha-divergence based supernets training to both slimmable neural networks and weight-sharing NAS, and demonstrate significant improvements. Specifically, our discovered model family, AlphaNet, outperforms prior-art models on a wide range of FLOPs regimes, including BigNAS, Once-for-All networks, and AttentiveNAS. We achieve ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 80.0% with only 444M FLOPs. Our code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/AlphaNet.

papers_seen.author: Shaffer
papers_seen.title: Selective Knowledge Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Neural Machine Translation (NMT) models achieve state-of-the-art performance on many translation benchmarks. As an active research field in NMT, knowledge distillation is widely applied to enhance the model's performance by transferring teacher model's knowledge on each training sample. However, previous work rarely discusses the different impacts and connections among these samples, which serve as the medium for transferring teacher knowledge. In this paper, we design a novel protocol that can effectively analyze the different impacts of samples by comparing various samples' partitions. Based on above protocol, we conduct extensive experiments and find that the teacher's knowledge is not the more, the better. Knowledge over specific samples may even hurt the whole performance of knowledge distillation. Finally, to address these issues, we propose two simple yet effective strategies, i.e., batch-level and global-level selections, to pick suitable samples for distillation. We evaluate our approaches on two large-scale machine translation tasks, WMT'14 English->German and WMT'19 Chinese->English. Experimental results show that our approaches yield up to +1.28 and +0.89 BLEU points improvements over the Transformer baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-used technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining predictive performance. This approach involves transferring knowledge from a larger teacher model to a smaller student model through various mechanisms including soft label matching, feature mimicking, and adversarial training. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized tasks such as 3D object detection and information retrieval. The technique enables practical deployment of powerful models in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive accuracy with their larger counterparts.

papers_seen.author: Galvan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Critical Technique for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression in deep learning and NLP, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach addresses the critical challenge of deploying high-performance neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive accuracy. Recent advances extend beyond traditional teacher-student paradigms to include data-free distillation, multi-teacher approaches, and domain-specific compression strategies, making knowledge distillation essential for real-world applications where computational efficiency is paramount.

papers_seen.author: Whitehead
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models by transferring knowledge from a teacher model to a student model. This approach has become essential for deploying deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. KD has evolved from simple output-level distillation to sophisticated methods involving feature matching, task-specific adaptation, and multi-teacher ensembles. Recent advances span applications across natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains, with emerging research exploring the theoretical foundations of why distillation works and how to optimize knowledge transfer across heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Ortiz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as Essential Compression: Reconciling Theory and Practice in Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for deploying large neural networks on resource-constrained devices by enabling smaller student models to learn from larger teacher models. While the technique achieves significant reductions in model size and inference time, there remains considerable debate about how and why distillation works. This position argues that knowledge distillation is not merely a performance-preservation technique, but rather functions as a powerful form of learned regularization that offers benefits extending far beyond simple compression, including improved robustness and fairness, making it essential for practical deep learning deployment across diverse domains.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models by transferring knowledge from a teacher model to a student model. This approach enables the deployment of deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive performance. Model compression through KD has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, graph neural networks, and reinforcement learning. The method addresses fundamental challenges in making advanced deep learning models practical for real-world applications by reducing computational and storage requirements without substantial accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Walls
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Approaches and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying efficient neural networks across diverse domains. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from larger, complex teacher models to smaller, lightweight student models while maintaining or improving performance. This synthesis examines the current state of knowledge distillation techniques, their applications to natural language processing and computer vision tasks, and recent innovations in multi-teacher frameworks and domain-specific approaches. The research demonstrates that knowledge distillation provides a flexible and practical solution for reducing computational costs and memory requirements in both discriminative and generative models, with particular success in transformer-based language models, neural machine translation, and graph neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Rios
papers_seen.title: Improving Neural Topic Models using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Topic models are often used to identify human-interpretable topics to help make sense of large document collections. We use knowledge distillation to combine the best attributes of probabilistic topic models and pretrained transformers. Our modular method can be straightforwardly applied with any neural topic model to improve topic quality, which we demonstrate using two models having disparate architectures, obtaining state-of-the-art topic coherence. We show that our adaptable framework not only improves performance in the aggregate over all estimated topics, as is commonly reported, but also in head-to-head comparisons of aligned topics.

papers_seen.author: Tran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression in deep learning, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large teacher models to compact student networks. This approach addresses critical challenges in deploying neural networks to resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. By examining applications across natural language processing and computer vision, this paper argues that knowledge distillation is not merely an optimization technique but a necessary strategy for making state-of-the-art models practical and accessible in real-world deployment scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Moreno
papers_seen.title: Learning Perception-Aware Agile Flight in Cluttered Environments
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, neural control policies have outperformed existing model-based planning-and-control methods for autonomously navigating quadrotors through cluttered environments in minimum time. However, they are not perception aware, a crucial requirement in vision-based navigation due to the camera's limited field of view and the underactuated nature of a quadrotor. We propose a learning-based system that achieves perception-aware, agile flight in cluttered environments. Our method combines imitation learning with reinforcement learning (RL) by leveraging a privileged learning-by-cheating framework. Using RL, we first train a perception-aware teacher policy with full-state information to fly in minimum time through cluttered environments. Then, we use imitation learning to distill its knowledge into a vision-based student policy that only perceives the environment via a camera. Our approach tightly couples perception and control, showing a significant advantage in computation speed (10 times faster) and success rate. We demonstrate the closed-loop control performance using hardware-in-the-loop simulation.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge distillation from multi-modal to mono-modal segmentation networks
papers_seen.abstract: The joint use of multiple imaging modalities for medical image segmentation has been widely studied in recent years. The fusion of information from different modalities has demonstrated to improve the segmentation accuracy, with respect to mono-modal segmentations, in several applications. However, acquiring multiple modalities is usually not possible in a clinical setting due to a limited number of physicians and scanners, and to limit costs and scan time. Most of the time, only one modality is acquired. In this paper, we propose KD-Net, a framework to transfer knowledge from a trained multi-modal network (teacher) to a mono-modal one (student). The proposed method is an adaptation of the generalized distillation framework where the student network is trained on a subset (1 modality) of the teacher's inputs (n modalities). We illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in brain tumor segmentation with the BraTS 2018 dataset. Using different architectures, we show that the student network effectively learns from the teacher and always outperforms the baseline mono-modal network in terms of segmentation accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Velasquez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and transformative technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, resource-efficient student models, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices without significant accuracy degradation. The method extends across multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, federated learning, and speech recognition, addressing critical challenges of computational efficiency, memory footprint, and inference latency in modern deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Powerful Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as one of the most effective techniques for training compact, efficient neural networks without sacrificing performance. This approach enables smaller "student" models to learn from larger, high-capacity "teacher" models through knowledge transfer, making deep learning systems practical for resource-constrained environments including mobile devices and real-time applications. The technique's versatility has enabled successful applications across diverse domains from computer vision to natural language processing.

papers_seen.author: Reid
papers_seen.title: Moonshine: Distilling with Cheap Convolutions
papers_seen.abstract: Many engineers wish to deploy modern neural networks in memory-limited settings; but the development of flexible methods for reducing memory use is in its infancy, and there is little knowledge of the resulting cost-benefit. We propose structural model distillation for memory reduction using a strategy that produces a student architecture that is a simple transformation of the teacher architecture: no redesign is needed, and the same hyperparameters can be used. Using attention transfer, we provide Pareto curves/tables for distillation of residual networks with four benchmark datasets, indicating the memory versus accuracy payoff. We show that substantial memory savings are possible with very little loss of accuracy, and confirm that distillation provides student network performance that is better than training that student architecture directly on data.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying large neural networks on resource-constrained devices. These methods enable smaller student models to learn from larger, more capable teacher models, achieving significant reductions in model size and inference time while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and graph neural networks, with various approaches addressing challenges such as heterogeneous architectures, domain adaptation, and ensemble compression.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Enabling Efficient Deep Learning Through Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and NLP. By enabling compact student models to learn from larger teacher models, distillation addresses the critical challenge of deploying sophisticated neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive performance. This paper surveys the theoretical foundations and practical applications of knowledge distillation, demonstrating how this approach achieves significant model size reduction and inference speedup across diverse domains including vision, language processing, and neural architecture optimization.

papers_seen.author: Obrien
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the practical deployment of advanced deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications. By transferring knowledge from teacher models to student models through various mechanisms, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in making sophisticated neural networks accessible for real-world applications with limited computational resources.

papers_seen.author: Deleon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Yet Imperfect Solution for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining predictive performance. This approach involves training a student model to mimic the behavior of a larger teacher model, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments. Despite its widespread adoption across various domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, knowledge distillation represents an essential yet imperfect solution to the model compression challenge, with significant implications for practical deep learning applications while presenting important theoretical and practical limitations.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning: A Comprehensive Strategy for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile technique in deep learning, enabling the compression of large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from complex teacher networks to simpler student networks, addressing critical challenges in deploying deep learning models on resource-constrained devices. Recent advances span multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning, with innovations in distillation mechanisms, architectural designs, and theoretical foundations. The technique has proven effective not only for model compression but also for improving interpretability, enabling lifelong learning, and facilitating federated learning scenarios. Despite its widespread adoption, ongoing research continues to refine distillation methods and expand their applicability across diverse tasks and model types.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach involves training a student network to mimic the behavior of a larger teacher network, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, with innovations addressing challenges such as data scarcity, adversarial robustness, and multi-modal learning. Recent advances demonstrate that knowledge distillation remains essential for practical deployment of deep learning systems while addressing critical computational and memory constraints.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Distilled Semantics for Comprehensive Scene Understanding from Videos
papers_seen.abstract: Whole understanding of the surroundings is paramount to autonomous systems. Recent works have shown that deep neural networks can learn geometry (depth) and motion (optical flow) from a monocular video without any explicit supervision from ground truth annotations, particularly hard to source for these two tasks. In this paper, we take an additional step toward holistic scene understanding with monocular cameras by learning depth and motion alongside with semantics, with supervision for the latter provided by a pre-trained network distilling proxy ground truth images. We address the three tasks jointly by a) a novel training protocol based on knowledge distillation and self-supervision and b) a compact network architecture which enables efficient scene understanding on both power hungry GPUs and low-power embedded platforms. We thoroughly assess the performance of our framework and show that it yields state-of-the-art results for monocular depth estimation, optical flow and motion segmentation.

papers_seen.author: House
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Critical Technique for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models without substantial performance loss. This technique transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive accuracy. Knowledge distillation is particularly valuable in natural language processing, where modern pre-trained models like BERT impose significant computational burdens for inference. Beyond compression, distillation serves broader purposes including domain adaptation, heterogeneous federated learning, and improved model generalization. The versatility and effectiveness of knowledge distillation across diverse applications demonstrate its importance as a foundational technique in modern deep learning.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Improved Accuracy in Spoken Question Answering
papers_seen.abstract: Spoken question answering (SQA) is a challenging task that requires the machine to fully understand the complex spoken documents. Automatic speech recognition (ASR) plays a significant role in the development of QA systems. However, the recent work shows that ASR systems generate highly noisy transcripts, which critically limit the capability of machine comprehension on the SQA task. To address the issue, we present a novel distillation framework. Specifically, we devise a training strategy to perform knowledge distillation (KD) from spoken documents and written counterparts. Our work makes a step towards distilling knowledge from the language model as a supervision signal to lead to better student accuracy by reducing the misalignment between automatic and manual transcriptions. Experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms several state-of-the-art language models on the Spoken-SQuAD dataset.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Transformative Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and transformative technique for compressing large neural networks and transferring knowledge from complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems, including computational efficiency, memory footprint reduction, and inference latency, while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and federated learning, demonstrating the broad applicability and essential role of knowledge distillation in modern machine learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Towards Practical Lipreading with Distilled and Efficient Models
papers_seen.abstract: Lipreading has witnessed a lot of progress due to the resurgence of neural networks. Recent works have placed emphasis on aspects such as improving performance by finding the optimal architecture or improving generalization. However, there is still a significant gap between the current methodologies and the requirements for an effective deployment of lipreading in practical scenarios. In this work, we propose a series of innovations that significantly bridge that gap: first, we raise the state-of-the-art performance by a wide margin on LRW and LRW-1000 to 88.5% and 46.6%, respectively using self-distillation. Secondly, we propose a series of architectural changes, including a novel Depthwise Separable Temporal Convolutional Network (DS-TCN) head, that slashes the computational cost to a fraction of the (already quite efficient) original model. Thirdly, we show that knowledge distillation is a very effective tool for recovering performance of the lightweight models. This results in a range of models with different accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. However, our most promising lightweight models are on par with the current state-of-the-art while showing a reduction of 8.2x and 3.9x in terms of computational cost and number of parameters, respectively, which we hope will enable the deployment of lipreading models in practical applications.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as fundamental techniques for deploying neural networks efficiently in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable smaller student models to learn from larger, more capable teacher models, achieving significant reductions in model size and inference time while maintaining competitive performance. The approaches have become critical for practical deep learning applications across computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and other domains.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: SEED: Self-supervised Distillation For Visual Representation
papers_seen.abstract: This paper is concerned with self-supervised learning for small models. The problem is motivated by our empirical studies that while the widely used contrastive self-supervised learning method has shown great progress on large model training, it does not work well for small models. To address this problem, we propose a new learning paradigm, named SElf-SupErvised Distillation (SEED), where we leverage a larger network (as Teacher) to transfer its representational knowledge into a smaller architecture (as Student) in a self-supervised fashion. Instead of directly learning from unlabeled data, we train a student encoder to mimic the similarity score distribution inferred by a teacher over a set of instances. We show that SEED dramatically boosts the performance of small networks on downstream tasks. Compared with self-supervised baselines, SEED improves the top-1 accuracy from 42.2% to 67.6% on EfficientNet-B0 and from 36.3% to 68.2% on MobileNet-v3-Large on the ImageNet-1k dataset.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Understanding BERT Rankers Under Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep language models such as BERT pre-trained on large corpus have given a huge performance boost to the state-of-the-art information retrieval ranking systems. Knowledge embedded in such models allows them to pick up complex matching signals between passages and queries. However, the high computation cost during inference limits their deployment in real-world search scenarios. In this paper, we study if and how the knowledge for search within BERT can be transferred to a smaller ranker through distillation. Our experiments demonstrate that it is crucial to use a proper distillation procedure, which produces up to nine times speedup while preserving the state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Current Approaches
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying deep neural networks in resource-constrained environments. This synthesis examines the diverse applications and methodologies of knowledge distillation across multiple domains including natural language processing, graph neural networks, computer vision, and speech recognition. We review various distillation strategies, including soft-label matching, intermediate representation matching, and adversarial learning approaches, demonstrating how these techniques effectively compress large models while maintaining or even improving performance. Special attention is given to domain-specific innovations such as distillation for non-autoregressive translation, BERT compression, and graph neural network acceleration.

papers_seen.author: Walton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing neural networks and transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models. This approach addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems, including computational efficiency, memory footprint reduction, and inference latency. Applications span across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, speech processing, and information retrieval. Recent advances explore novel architectures, multi-teacher frameworks, data-free scenarios, and task-specific optimizations to enhance both student model performance and practical deployability.

papers_seen.author: Duncan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Methods and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student networks. This approach is increasingly applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal learning. Current methods employ various knowledge transfer mechanisms, from simple output probability matching to sophisticated feature-level and adversarial approaches. While primarily used to reduce memory footprint and computational requirements for deployment on resource-constrained devices, knowledge distillation also demonstrates benefits for robustness, fairness, and generalization. Recent work has extended distillation beyond traditional supervised settings to federated learning, multi-task learning, and generative models, establishing it as a versatile framework for neural network optimization and knowledge transfer.

papers_seen.author: Hawkins
papers_seen.title: A Fast Knowledge Distillation Framework for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: While Knowledge Distillation (KD) has been recognized as a useful tool in many visual tasks, such as supervised classification and self-supervised representation learning, the main drawback of a vanilla KD framework is its mechanism, which consumes the majority of the computational overhead on forwarding through the giant teacher networks, making the entire learning procedure inefficient and costly. ReLabel, a recently proposed solution, suggests creating a label map for the entire image. During training, it receives the cropped region-level label by RoI aligning on a pre-generated entire label map, allowing for efficient supervision generation without having to pass through the teachers many times. However, as the KD teachers are from conventional multi-crop training, there are various mismatches between the global label-map and region-level label in this technique, resulting in performance deterioration. In this study, we present a Fast Knowledge Distillation (FKD) framework that replicates the distillation training phase and generates soft labels using the multi-crop KD approach, while training faster than ReLabel since no post-processes such as RoI align and softmax operations are used. When conducting multi-crop in the same image for data loading, our FKD is even more efficient than the traditional image classification framework. On ImageNet-1K, we obtain 79.8% with ResNet-50, outperforming ReLabel by ~1.0% while being faster. On the self-supervised learning task, we also show that FKD has an efficiency advantage. Our project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/FKD/index.html, source code and models are available at: https://github.com/szq0214/FKD.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-adopted technique for model compression that enables the training of efficient student models by transferring knowledge from larger, more powerful teacher models. This approach has become fundamental in deep learning and natural language processing, addressing the critical challenge of deploying high-performance models under computational constraints. Knowledge distillation methods transfer various types of knowledge including soft logits, intermediate feature representations, and attention patterns, enabling significant model size reduction while maintaining competitive accuracy across diverse applications including computer vision, machine translation, speech recognition, and recommendation systems.

papers_seen.author: Spears
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Critical Technique for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to compact student networks, knowledge distillation enables the deployment of sophisticated deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices. This technique addresses critical challenges across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications, demonstrating significant reductions in computational cost and model size without proportional accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Green
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and increasingly indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning models in resource-constrained environments by transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student models. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized tasks, with methodologies ranging from simple output-level distillation to sophisticated multi-teacher frameworks and feature-based approaches. The technique addresses critical challenges in model efficiency while preserving accuracy, making it essential for real-world applications where computational and memory constraints are significant limiting factors.

papers_seen.author: Mckay
papers_seen.title: MixKD: Towards Efficient Distillation of Large-scale Language Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale language models have recently demonstrated impressive empirical performance. Nevertheless, the improved results are attained at the price of bigger models, more power consumption, and slower inference, which hinder their applicability to low-resource (both memory and computation) platforms. Knowledge distillation (KD) has been demonstrated as an effective framework for compressing such big models. However, large-scale neural network systems are prone to memorize training instances, and thus tend to make inconsistent predictions when the data distribution is altered slightly. Moreover, the student model has few opportunities to request useful information from the teacher model when there is limited task-specific data available. To address these issues, we propose MixKD, a data-agnostic distillation framework that leverages mixup, a simple yet efficient data augmentation approach, to endow the resulting model with stronger generalization ability. Concretely, in addition to the original training examples, the student model is encouraged to mimic the teacher's behavior on the linear interpolation of example pairs as well. We prove from a theoretical perspective that under reasonable conditions MixKD gives rise to a smaller gap between the generalization error and the empirical error. To verify its effectiveness, we conduct experiments on the GLUE benchmark, where MixKD consistently leads to significant gains over the standard KD training, and outperforms several competitive baselines. Experiments under a limited-data setting and ablation studies further demonstrate the advantages of the proposed approach.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: FedZKT: Zero-Shot Knowledge Transfer towards Resource-Constrained Federated Learning with Heterogeneous On-Device Models
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning enables multiple distributed devices to collaboratively learn a shared prediction model without centralizing their on-device data. Most of the current algorithms require comparable individual efforts for local training with the same structure and size of on-device models, which, however, impedes participation from resource-constrained devices. Given the widespread yet heterogeneous devices nowadays, in this paper, we propose an innovative federated learning framework with heterogeneous on-device models through Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer, named by FedZKT. Specifically, FedZKT allows devices to independently determine the on-device models upon their local resources. To achieve knowledge transfer across these heterogeneous on-device models, a zero-shot distillation approach is designed without any prerequisites for private on-device data, which is contrary to certain prior research based on a public dataset or a pre-trained data generator. Moreover, this compute-intensive distillation task is assigned to the server to allow the participation of resource-constrained devices, where a generator is adversarially learned with the ensemble of collected on-device models. The distilled central knowledge is then sent back in the form of the corresponding on-device model parameters, which can be easily absorbed on the device side. Extensive experimental studies demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of FedZKT towards on-device knowledge agnostic, on-device model heterogeneity, and other challenging federated learning scenarios, such as heterogeneous on-device data and straggler effects.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: ALP-KD: Attention-Based Layer Projection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is considered as a training and compression strategy in which two neural networks, namely a teacher and a student, are coupled together during training. The teacher network is supposed to be a trustworthy predictor and the student tries to mimic its predictions. Usually, a student with a lighter architecture is selected so we can achieve compression and yet deliver high-quality results. In such a setting, distillation only happens for final predictions whereas the student could also benefit from teacher's supervision for internal components.   Motivated by this, we studied the problem of distillation for intermediate layers. Since there might not be a one-to-one alignment between student and teacher layers, existing techniques skip some teacher layers and only distill from a subset of them. This shortcoming directly impacts quality, so we instead propose a combinatorial technique which relies on attention. Our model fuses teacher-side information and takes each layer's significance into consideration, then performs distillation between combined teacher layers and those of the student. Using our technique, we distilled a 12-layer BERT (Devlin et al. 2019) into 6-, 4-, and 2-layer counterparts and evaluated them on GLUE tasks (Wang et al. 2018). Experimental results show that our combinatorial approach is able to outperform other existing techniques.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Model Compression with Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation for Web Question Answering System
papers_seen.abstract: Deep pre-training and fine-tuning models (such as BERT and OpenAI GPT) have demonstrated excellent results in question answering areas. However, due to the sheer amount of model parameters, the inference speed of these models is very slow. How to apply these complex models to real business scenarios becomes a challenging but practical problem. Previous model compression methods usually suffer from information loss during the model compression procedure, leading to inferior models compared with the original one. To tackle this challenge, we propose a Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (TMKD for short) method for web Question Answering system. We first develop a general Q\&A distillation task for student model pre-training, and further fine-tune this pre-trained student model with multi-teacher knowledge distillation on downstream tasks (like Web Q\&A task, MNLI, SNLI, RTE tasks from GLUE), which effectively reduces the overfitting bias in individual teacher models, and transfers more general knowledge to the student model. The experiment results show that our method can significantly outperform the baseline methods and even achieve comparable results with the original teacher models, along with substantial speedup of model inference.

papers_seen.author: Fisher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying large neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining performance. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, these approaches enable significant reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference latency. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents an essential paradigm for making state-of-the-art deep learning models practical and accessible across diverse applications including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Does Knowledge Distillation Really Work?
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique for training a small student network to emulate a larger teacher model, such as an ensemble of networks. We show that while knowledge distillation can improve student generalization, it does not typically work as it is commonly understood: there often remains a surprisingly large discrepancy between the predictive distributions of the teacher and the student, even in cases when the student has the capacity to perfectly match the teacher. We identify difficulties in optimization as a key reason for why the student is unable to match the teacher. We also show how the details of the dataset used for distillation play a role in how closely the student matches the teacher -- and that more closely matching the teacher paradoxically does not always lead to better student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Hancock
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Approaches and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression represent fundamental techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of learned representations and knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student networks while maintaining competitive predictive performance. The approach has been extensively applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, graph neural networks, and specialized applications such as reinforcement learning and federated learning. Recent innovations span feature-level distillation, adversarial learning strategies, multi-teacher approaches, and task-specific compression methods. Knowledge distillation has become essential for practical deep learning deployment by addressing fundamental challenges in making advanced models accessible for real-world applications with limited computational and storage resources.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Online Knowledge Distillation via Mutual Contrastive Learning for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: The teacher-free online Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to train an ensemble of multiple student models collaboratively and distill knowledge from each other. Although existing online KD methods achieve desirable performance, they often focus on class probabilities as the core knowledge type, ignoring the valuable feature representational information. We present a Mutual Contrastive Learning (MCL) framework for online KD. The core idea of MCL is to perform mutual interaction and transfer of contrastive distributions among a cohort of networks in an online manner. Our MCL can aggregate cross-network embedding information and maximize the lower bound to the mutual information between two networks. This enables each network to learn extra contrastive knowledge from others, leading to better feature representations, thus improving the performance of visual recognition tasks. Beyond the final layer, we extend MCL to intermediate layers and perform an adaptive layer-matching mechanism trained by meta-optimization. Experiments on image classification and transfer learning to visual recognition tasks show that layer-wise MCL can lead to consistent performance gains against state-of-the-art online KD approaches. The superiority demonstrates that layer-wise MCL can guide the network to generate better feature representations. Our code is publicly avaliable at https://github.com/winycg/L-MCL.

papers_seen.author: Oliver
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for compressing large neural networks into efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from complex teacher models to simpler, more deployable architectures, making it particularly valuable for NLP and deep learning applications where computational efficiency is essential. Knowledge distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments, offering solutions across diverse domains from machine translation to information retrieval and speech recognition.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for transferring knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach enables model compression while maintaining competitive performance across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, recommender systems, and federated learning. The technique involves training a student network to emulate a teacher model's behavior, effectively reducing computational requirements and memory footprint for deployment on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation has been adapted and extended for various applications, including domain adaptation, privacy-preserving learning, and specialized architectures like vision transformers and graph neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Show, Attend and Distill:Knowledge Distillation via Attention-based Feature Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation extracts general knowledge from a pre-trained teacher network and provides guidance to a target student network. Most studies manually tie intermediate features of the teacher and student, and transfer knowledge through pre-defined links. However, manual selection often constructs ineffective links that limit the improvement from the distillation. There has been an attempt to address the problem, but it is still challenging to identify effective links under practical scenarios. In this paper, we introduce an effective and efficient feature distillation method utilizing all the feature levels of the teacher without manually selecting the links. Specifically, our method utilizes an attention-based meta-network that learns relative similarities between features, and applies identified similarities to control distillation intensities of all possible pairs. As a result, our method determines competent links more efficiently than the previous approach and provides better performance on model compression and transfer learning tasks. Further qualitative analyses and ablative studies describe how our method contributes to better distillation. The implementation code is available at github.com/clovaai/attention-feature-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Ware
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach addresses critical challenges in deploying state-of-the-art neural networks to resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. By examining diverse applications and methodologies across multiple domains, knowledge distillation represents not merely a supplementary compression technique, but a versatile learning paradigm essential for practical deployment of deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers with Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we study the problem of unifying knowledge from a set of classifiers with different architectures and target classes into a single classifier, given only a generic set of unlabelled data. We call this problem Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers (UHC). This problem is motivated by scenarios where data is collected from multiple sources, but the sources cannot share their data, e.g., due to privacy concerns, and only privately trained models can be shared. In addition, each source may not be able to gather data to train all classes due to data availability at each source, and may not be able to train the same classification model due to different computational resources. To tackle this problem, we propose a generalisation of knowledge distillation to merge HCs. We derive a probabilistic relation between the outputs of HCs and the probability over all classes. Based on this relation, we propose two classes of methods based on cross-entropy minimisation and matrix factorisation, which allow us to estimate soft labels over all classes from unlabelled samples and use them in lieu of ground truth labels to train a unified classifier. Our extensive experiments on ImageNet, LSUN, and Places365 datasets show that our approaches significantly outperform a naive extension of distillation and can achieve almost the same accuracy as classifiers that are trained in a centralised, supervised manner.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Less is More: Task-aware Layer-wise Distillation for Language Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Layer-wise distillation is a powerful tool to compress large models (i.e. teacher models) into small ones (i.e., student models). The student distills knowledge from the teacher by mimicking the hidden representations of the teacher at every intermediate layer. However, layer-wise distillation is difficult. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Task-aware layEr-wise Distillation (TED). TED designs task-aware filters to align the hidden representations of the student and the teacher at each layer. The filters select the knowledge that is useful for the target task from the hidden representations. As such, TED reduces the knowledge gap between the two models and helps the student to fit better on the target task. We evaluate TED in two scenarios: continual pre-training and fine-tuning. TED demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over existing distillation methods in both scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/cliang1453/task-aware-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Dudley
papers_seen.title: Attention-Guided Answer Distillation for Machine Reading Comprehension
papers_seen.abstract: Despite that current reading comprehension systems have achieved significant advancements, their promising performances are often obtained at the cost of making an ensemble of numerous models. Besides, existing approaches are also vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper tackles these problems by leveraging knowledge distillation, which aims to transfer knowledge from an ensemble model to a single model. We first demonstrate that vanilla knowledge distillation applied to answer span prediction is effective for reading comprehension systems. We then propose two novel approaches that not only penalize the prediction on confusing answers but also guide the training with alignment information distilled from the ensemble. Experiments show that our best student model has only a slight drop of 0.4% F1 on the SQuAD test set compared to the ensemble teacher, while running 12x faster during inference. It even outperforms the teacher on adversarial SQuAD datasets and NarrativeQA benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student networks. This approach has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and federated learning. By leveraging soft target probabilities and intermediate representations from teachers, knowledge distillation achieves significant reductions in model size and computational cost while maintaining competitive performance. Recent advances have extended the technique to address challenges such as data-free distillation, adversarial robustness, heterogeneous models, and task-specific compression. The method has proven particularly valuable for deploying neural networks on resource-constrained devices and enabling real-time inference in practical applications.

papers_seen.author: Davenport
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from well-trained teacher models to student networks, enabling practical deployment on resource-constrained devices. The method has been widely adopted across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications, serving multiple purposes beyond basic compression including fairness improvements, robustness transfer, and enhanced model interpretability. Recent research reveals that distillation functions not only through explicit knowledge transfer but also as a form of learned regularization, with theoretical analyses providing deeper understanding of its mechanisms and benefits.

papers_seen.author: Heath
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are critical techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These approaches enable the transfer of knowledge from large "teacher" models to smaller "student" networks, reducing computational costs and parameter counts while maintaining competitive performance. Recent work spans diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, federated learning, and reinforcement learning, demonstrating the broad applicability of these compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are critical techniques that enable the deployment of deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from larger teacher networks to smaller student networks, achieving significant reductions in model size and computational requirements while maintaining competitive performance. The field has evolved from simple logit-matching approaches to sophisticated techniques involving feature-level and attention-based knowledge transfer, with applications spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains like speech recognition and medical imaging.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning in Resource-Constrained Environments
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span computer vision, natural language processing, federated learning, and specialized domains such as recommender systems and graph neural networks. Recent advances include intermediate layer distillation, attention-based mechanisms, and task-adaptive compression strategies that further enhance the effectiveness of knowledge transfer.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Releasing Graph Neural Networks with Differential Privacy Guarantees
papers_seen.abstract: With the increasing popularity of graph neural networks (GNNs) in several sensitive applications like healthcare and medicine, concerns have been raised over the privacy aspects of trained GNNs. More notably, GNNs are vulnerable to privacy attacks, such as membership inference attacks, even if only black-box access to the trained model is granted. We propose PrivGNN, a privacy-preserving framework for releasing GNN models in a centralized setting. Assuming an access to a public unlabeled graph, PrivGNN provides a framework to release GNN models trained explicitly on public data along with knowledge obtained from the private data in a privacy preserving manner. PrivGNN combines the knowledge-distillation framework with the two noise mechanisms, random subsampling, and noisy labeling, to ensure rigorous privacy guarantees. We theoretically analyze our approach in the Renyi differential privacy framework. Besides, we show the solid experimental performance of our method compared to several baselines adapted for graph-structured data. Our code is available at https://github.com/iyempissy/privGnn.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Fundamental Approach to Model Compression and Efficiency in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a pivotal technique for compressing large neural networks into efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the deployment of sophisticated deep learning models on resource-constrained devices by transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher networks to compact student networks. Beyond traditional classification tasks, knowledge distillation demonstrates remarkable versatility across diverse domains including natural language processing, graph neural networks, and multimodal learning. The technique continues to evolve with innovations in feature matching, attention mechanisms, and integration with complementary compression methods, establishing it as an essential strategy for making state-of-the-art models practical for real-world applications.
