papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying large neural networks on resource-constrained devices. These methods enable smaller student models to learn from larger, more capable teacher models, achieving significant reductions in model size and inference time while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and graph neural networks, with various approaches addressing challenges such as heterogeneous architectures, domain adaptation, and ensemble compression.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are critical approaches for deploying deep neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These techniques enable the transfer of knowledge from large, high-performing teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student networks while maintaining competitive performance. This paper examines key advances in knowledge distillation across various domains, including computer vision, natural language processing, graph neural networks, and specialized applications. The evidence demonstrates that knowledge distillation effectively addresses computational and storage constraints without sacrificing model quality, making it an indispensable tool for practical deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Cherry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices across multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications. The method addresses critical challenges in model efficiency, computational cost reduction, and practical deployment while maintaining competitive accuracy levels.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become critical techniques for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, compute-intensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This paper synthesizes recent advances in knowledge distillation and compression, examining their applications across natural language processing, computer vision, federated learning, and domain-specific tasks. The evidence demonstrates that knowledge distillation is highly effective for model compression, though successful implementation requires careful consideration of distillation strategy, teacher selection, and task-aware design choices.

papers_seen.author: Pham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Critical Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential and transformative technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, addressing critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. Applications span natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and graph neural networks, with innovations in training strategies, multi-teacher approaches, and domain-specific optimizations. The technique simultaneously reduces computational complexity, enables privacy-preserving model transfer, and improves model interpretability, establishing it as a fundamental paradigm for practical deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Humphrey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Benefits, Applications, and Empirical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for training compact neural networks by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models. This approach enables the deployment of deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive performance across diverse applications including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph learning. This paper examines the theoretical foundations, practical applications, and empirical findings surrounding knowledge distillation and model compression, highlighting both the effectiveness of the technique and important considerations for its successful implementation.

papers_seen.author: Green
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and increasingly indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning models in resource-constrained environments by transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student models. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized tasks, with methodologies ranging from simple output-level distillation to sophisticated multi-teacher frameworks and feature-based approaches. The technique addresses critical challenges in model efficiency while preserving accuracy, making it essential for real-world applications where computational and memory constraints are significant limiting factors.

papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: AdaBERT: Task-Adaptive BERT Compression with Differentiable Neural Architecture Search
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained language models such as BERT have shown their effectiveness in various natural language processing tasks. However, the huge parameter size makes them difficult to be deployed in real-time applications that require quick inference with limited resources. Existing methods compress BERT into small models while such compression is task-independent, i.e., the same compressed BERT for all different downstream tasks. Motivated by the necessity and benefits of task-oriented BERT compression, we propose a novel compression method, AdaBERT, that leverages differentiable Neural Architecture Search to automatically compress BERT into task-adaptive small models for specific tasks. We incorporate a task-oriented knowledge distillation loss to provide search hints and an efficiency-aware loss as search constraints, which enables a good trade-off between efficiency and effectiveness for task-adaptive BERT compression. We evaluate AdaBERT on several NLP tasks, and the results demonstrate that those task-adaptive compressed models are 12.7x to 29.3x faster than BERT in inference time and 11.5x to 17.0x smaller in terms of parameter size, while comparable performance is maintained.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Fair Feature Distillation for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Fairness is becoming an increasingly crucial issue for computer vision, especially in the human-related decision systems. However, achieving algorithmic fairness, which makes a model produce indiscriminative outcomes against protected groups, is still an unresolved problem. In this paper, we devise a systematic approach which reduces algorithmic biases via feature distillation for visual recognition tasks, dubbed as MMD-based Fair Distillation (MFD). While the distillation technique has been widely used in general to improve the prediction accuracy, to the best of our knowledge, there has been no explicit work that also tries to improve fairness via distillation. Furthermore, We give a theoretical justification of our MFD on the effect of knowledge distillation and fairness. Throughout the extensive experiments, we show our MFD significantly mitigates the bias against specific minorities without any loss of the accuracy on both synthetic and real-world face datasets.

papers_seen.author: Bentley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Technique for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach addresses the critical challenge of deploying sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments by transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student networks. Beyond simple performance preservation, knowledge distillation provides broader benefits including improved interpretability, enhanced robustness, and effective implementation across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommendation systems. The technique has evolved from simple logit-matching approaches to sophisticated methods incorporating feature-level and attention-based knowledge transfer, establishing itself as an essential strategy for making state-of-the-art models practical for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential Strategy for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for enabling practical deployment of deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. This paper argues that knowledge distillation, combined with model compression strategies, is essential for bridging the gap between state-of-the-art performance and real-world computational constraints. By examining applications across diverse domains including neural machine translation, graph neural networks, speech processing, and information retrieval, this work demonstrates that knowledge distillation provides an effective, scalable solution for transferring knowledge from large teacher models to compact student models without significant performance degradation.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: An Essential Approach for Deploying Deep Learning Models in Resource-Constrained Environments
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying large deep learning models in practical applications where computational resources are limited. By transferring knowledge from a larger teacher model to a smaller student model, these approaches enable significant reductions in model size and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents an essential strategy for making state-of-the-art deep learning models accessible to real-world applications, particularly in natural language processing and computer vision domains. The evidence demonstrates that distillation can achieve substantial compression rates and speedups, making it a valuable tool for practitioners who need to balance model performance with deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: MEAL: Multi-Model Ensemble via Adversarial Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Often the best performing deep neural models are ensembles of multiple base-level networks. Unfortunately, the space required to store these many networks, and the time required to execute them at test-time, prohibits their use in applications where test sets are large (e.g., ImageNet). In this paper, we present a method for compressing large, complex trained ensembles into a single network, where knowledge from a variety of trained deep neural networks (DNNs) is distilled and transferred to a single DNN. In order to distill diverse knowledge from different trained (teacher) models, we propose to use adversarial-based learning strategy where we define a block-wise training loss to guide and optimize the predefined student network to recover the knowledge in teacher models, and to promote the discriminator network to distinguish teacher vs. student features simultaneously. The proposed ensemble method (MEAL) of transferring distilled knowledge with adversarial learning exhibits three important advantages: (1) the student network that learns the distilled knowledge with discriminators is optimized better than the original model; (2) fast inference is realized by a single forward pass, while the performance is even better than traditional ensembles from multi-original models; (3) the student network can learn the distilled knowledge from a teacher model that has arbitrary structures. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10/100, SVHN and ImageNet datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our MEAL method. On ImageNet, our ResNet-50 based MEAL achieves top-1/5 21.79%/5.99% val error, which outperforms the original model by 2.06%/1.14%. Code and models are available at: https://github.com/AaronHeee/MEAL

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression and efficient deployment of deep learning systems. By transferring knowledge from large teacher networks to compact student models, this approach maintains competitive performance while significantly reducing computational overhead and memory requirements. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is essential for making state-of-the-art deep learning models practical for real-world applications across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech processing, and graph neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Wolfe
papers_seen.title: Robust and Resource-Efficient Data-Free Knowledge Distillation by Generative Pseudo Replay
papers_seen.abstract: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation (KD) allows knowledge transfer from a trained neural network (teacher) to a more compact one (student) in the absence of original training data. Existing works use a validation set to monitor the accuracy of the student over real data and report the highest performance throughout the entire process. However, validation data may not be available at distillation time either, making it infeasible to record the student snapshot that achieved the peak accuracy. Therefore, a practical data-free KD method should be robust and ideally provide monotonically increasing student accuracy during distillation. This is challenging because the student experiences knowledge degradation due to the distribution shift of the synthetic data. A straightforward approach to overcome this issue is to store and rehearse the generated samples periodically, which increases the memory footprint and creates privacy concerns. We propose to model the distribution of the previously observed synthetic samples with a generative network. In particular, we design a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) with a training objective that is customized to learn the synthetic data representations optimally. The student is rehearsed by the generative pseudo replay technique, with samples produced by the VAE. Hence knowledge degradation can be prevented without storing any samples. Experiments on image classification benchmarks show that our method optimizes the expected value of the distilled model accuracy while eliminating the large memory overhead incurred by the sample-storing methods.

papers_seen.author: Dudley
papers_seen.title: Attention-Guided Answer Distillation for Machine Reading Comprehension
papers_seen.abstract: Despite that current reading comprehension systems have achieved significant advancements, their promising performances are often obtained at the cost of making an ensemble of numerous models. Besides, existing approaches are also vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper tackles these problems by leveraging knowledge distillation, which aims to transfer knowledge from an ensemble model to a single model. We first demonstrate that vanilla knowledge distillation applied to answer span prediction is effective for reading comprehension systems. We then propose two novel approaches that not only penalize the prediction on confusing answers but also guide the training with alignment information distilled from the ensemble. Experiments show that our best student model has only a slight drop of 0.4% F1 on the SQuAD test set compared to the ensemble teacher, while running 12x faster during inference. It even outperforms the teacher on adversarial SQuAD datasets and NarrativeQA benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Learning Compact Metrics for MT
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in machine translation and multilingual text generation have led researchers to adopt trained metrics such as COMET or BLEURT, which treat evaluation as a regression problem and use representations from multilingual pre-trained models such as XLM-RoBERTa or mBERT. Yet studies on related tasks suggest that these models are most efficient when they are large, which is costly and impractical for evaluation. We investigate the trade-off between multilinguality and model capacity with RemBERT, a state-of-the-art multilingual language model, using data from the WMT Metrics Shared Task. We present a series of experiments which show that model size is indeed a bottleneck for cross-lingual transfer, then demonstrate how distillation can help addressing this bottleneck, by leveraging synthetic data generation and transferring knowledge from one teacher to multiple students trained on related languages. Our method yields up to 10.5% improvement over vanilla fine-tuning and reaches 92.6% of RemBERT's performance using only a third of its parameters.

papers_seen.author: Pope
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying large neural networks on resource-constrained devices. These methods enable smaller student models to learn from larger, more capable teacher models, achieving significant reductions in model size and inference time while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and graph neural networks, with various approaches addressing challenges such as heterogeneous architectures, domain adaptation, and ensemble compression.

papers_seen.author: Arroyo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-adopted technique for model compression that transfers knowledge from larger teacher networks to smaller student networks, enabling efficient deployment while maintaining performance. This approach addresses critical challenges in modern machine learning by reducing computational costs, memory requirements, and inference latency. Applications span computer vision tasks such as image classification and object detection, as well as NLP applications including machine reading comprehension, question answering systems, and sequence-to-sequence models. Researchers have developed numerous extensions and refinements to address fundamental challenges including optimization difficulties, data availability constraints, and cross-modal knowledge transfer. Current work explores domain-specific applications, robustness properties, and integration with other compression techniques such as quantization and pruning.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Towards Practical Lipreading with Distilled and Efficient Models
papers_seen.abstract: Lipreading has witnessed a lot of progress due to the resurgence of neural networks. Recent works have placed emphasis on aspects such as improving performance by finding the optimal architecture or improving generalization. However, there is still a significant gap between the current methodologies and the requirements for an effective deployment of lipreading in practical scenarios. In this work, we propose a series of innovations that significantly bridge that gap: first, we raise the state-of-the-art performance by a wide margin on LRW and LRW-1000 to 88.5% and 46.6%, respectively using self-distillation. Secondly, we propose a series of architectural changes, including a novel Depthwise Separable Temporal Convolutional Network (DS-TCN) head, that slashes the computational cost to a fraction of the (already quite efficient) original model. Thirdly, we show that knowledge distillation is a very effective tool for recovering performance of the lightweight models. This results in a range of models with different accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. However, our most promising lightweight models are on par with the current state-of-the-art while showing a reduction of 8.2x and 3.9x in terms of computational cost and number of parameters, respectively, which we hope will enable the deployment of lipreading models in practical applications.

papers_seen.author: Keith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are critical techniques that enable the deployment of large, sophisticated neural networks in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models, these methods maintain competitive performance while dramatically reducing computational requirements and memory footprint. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents an essential approach for practical AI deployment across diverse applications in deep learning and natural language processing, addressing the fundamental tension between model capability and computational efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Morales
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Fundamental Paradigm for Deep Learning Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and practical approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By enabling a student model to learn from a teacher model's knowledge, distillation addresses critical deployment challenges in deep learning and NLP. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents an essential technique for making state-of-the-art models practical for real-world applications with constrained computational resources.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: ALP-KD: Attention-Based Layer Projection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is considered as a training and compression strategy in which two neural networks, namely a teacher and a student, are coupled together during training. The teacher network is supposed to be a trustworthy predictor and the student tries to mimic its predictions. Usually, a student with a lighter architecture is selected so we can achieve compression and yet deliver high-quality results. In such a setting, distillation only happens for final predictions whereas the student could also benefit from teacher's supervision for internal components.   Motivated by this, we studied the problem of distillation for intermediate layers. Since there might not be a one-to-one alignment between student and teacher layers, existing techniques skip some teacher layers and only distill from a subset of them. This shortcoming directly impacts quality, so we instead propose a combinatorial technique which relies on attention. Our model fuses teacher-side information and takes each layer's significance into consideration, then performs distillation between combined teacher layers and those of the student. Using our technique, we distilled a 12-layer BERT (Devlin et al. 2019) into 6-, 4-, and 2-layer counterparts and evaluated them on GLUE tasks (Wang et al. 2018). Experimental results show that our combinatorial approach is able to outperform other existing techniques.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, high-performing teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach has become increasingly important for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments while maintaining predictive performance. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems, with techniques addressing various challenges such as adversarial robustness, fairness, and data privacy. Recent advances have introduced specialized distillation strategies tailored to specific architectures and tasks, enabling significant reductions in model size and inference latency without substantial accuracy losses.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Highlight Every Step: Knowledge Distillation via Collaborative Teaching
papers_seen.abstract: High storage and computational costs obstruct deep neural networks to be deployed on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation aims to train a compact student network by transferring knowledge from a larger pre-trained teacher model. However, most existing methods on knowledge distillation ignore the valuable information among training process associated with training results. In this paper, we provide a new Collaborative Teaching Knowledge Distillation (CTKD) strategy which employs two special teachers. Specifically, one teacher trained from scratch (i.e., scratch teacher) assists the student step by step using its temporary outputs. It forces the student to approach the optimal path towards the final logits with high accuracy. The other pre-trained teacher (i.e., expert teacher) guides the student to focus on a critical region which is more useful for the task. The combination of the knowledge from two special teachers can significantly improve the performance of the student network in knowledge distillation. The results of experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN and Tiny ImageNet datasets verify that the proposed knowledge distillation method is efficient and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: An Essential Technique for Efficient Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to compact student networks, distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. This approach has proven effective across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, establishing itself as a critical tool for making deep learning practical in real-world scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Essential Technique for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments by enabling the transfer of knowledge from large teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach maintains competitive performance while substantially reducing model size, computational requirements, and inference latency. Knowledge distillation addresses fundamental deployment challenges across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, making state-of-the-art models practical and accessible for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Garrison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Fundamental Paradigm for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a transformative technique for model compression and knowledge transfer across deep learning and NLP applications. By enabling the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student networks, knowledge distillation addresses a critical challenge in modern machine learning: deploying sophisticated models in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. This position argues that knowledge distillation represents far more than a simple compression tool—it constitutes a fundamental paradigm shift in how we approach neural network training and deployment. The technique's effectiveness extends beyond mere efficiency gains to encompass improved robustness, reduced computational complexity, and enhanced model generalization. Through diverse applications spanning reading comprehension, machine translation, vision-language tasks, and recommender systems, knowledge distillation demonstrates remarkable versatility and reliability as a core principle for practical AI deployment.

papers_seen.author: Kidd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Strategic Transfer of Learning from Large to Small Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful paradigm for model compression that enables the transfer of knowledge from large teacher networks to smaller student models. This approach addresses critical challenges in deploying deep neural networks across resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. Through strategic knowledge transfer mechanisms, distillation techniques have proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal learning. The success of these methods relies on sophisticated mechanisms for capturing and transferring both task-relevant information and feature representations. Modern distillation frameworks continue to evolve, incorporating adaptive weighting schemes, layer-wise knowledge transfer, and adversarial learning strategies to maximize compression efficiency while minimizing performance degradation.

papers_seen.author: Leblanc
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Deploying Deep Learning Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining comparable performance. This review examines key approaches including structural distillation, feature-based distillation, and application-specific compression strategies across various domains. The evidence demonstrates that knowledge distillation consistently enables substantial model size reduction with minimal accuracy loss, making it an indispensable tool for practical deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Beck
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Strategic Approach to Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression represent essential techniques for deploying sophisticated neural networks in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. These methods transfer knowledge from large, complex teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student models, addressing critical challenges in practical deep learning applications. This paper examines the theoretical foundations, diverse applications, and empirical considerations surrounding knowledge distillation across natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Fair Feature Distillation for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Fairness is becoming an increasingly crucial issue for computer vision, especially in the human-related decision systems. However, achieving algorithmic fairness, which makes a model produce indiscriminative outcomes against protected groups, is still an unresolved problem. In this paper, we devise a systematic approach which reduces algorithmic biases via feature distillation for visual recognition tasks, dubbed as MMD-based Fair Distillation (MFD). While the distillation technique has been widely used in general to improve the prediction accuracy, to the best of our knowledge, there has been no explicit work that also tries to improve fairness via distillation. Furthermore, We give a theoretical justification of our MFD on the effect of knowledge distillation and fairness. Throughout the extensive experiments, we show our MFD significantly mitigates the bias against specific minorities without any loss of the accuracy on both synthetic and real-world face datasets.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Current Approaches
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying deep neural networks in resource-constrained environments. This synthesis examines the diverse applications and methodologies of knowledge distillation across multiple domains including natural language processing, graph neural networks, computer vision, and speech recognition. We review various distillation strategies, including soft-label matching, intermediate representation matching, and adversarial learning approaches, demonstrating how these techniques effectively compress large models while maintaining or even improving performance. Special attention is given to domain-specific innovations such as distillation for non-autoregressive translation, BERT compression, and graph neural network acceleration.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach involves training a student network to mimic the behavior of a larger teacher network, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, with innovations addressing challenges such as data scarcity, adversarial robustness, and multi-modal learning. Recent advances demonstrate that knowledge distillation remains essential for practical deployment of deep learning systems while addressing critical computational and memory constraints.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Critical Approach to Efficient Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from teacher models to student models across diverse applications in natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains. The technique encompasses various methodologies including output-level distillation, feature-based approaches, and task-aware strategies. Evidence demonstrates that distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments while addressing computational overhead and memory limitations without substantial accuracy losses.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Advancing Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving performance. This approach transfers knowledge from a larger teacher model to a smaller student model, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices without sacrificing accuracy. The method extends across multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and federated learning, with applications ranging from mobile deployment to privacy-preserving distributed systems.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Private Model Compression via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The soaring demand for intelligent mobile applications calls for deploying powerful deep neural networks (DNNs) on mobile devices. However, the outstanding performance of DNNs notoriously relies on increasingly complex models, which in turn is associated with an increase in computational expense far surpassing mobile devices' capacity. What is worse, app service providers need to collect and utilize a large volume of users' data, which contain sensitive information, to build the sophisticated DNN models. Directly deploying these models on public mobile devices presents prohibitive privacy risk. To benefit from the on-device deep learning without the capacity and privacy concerns, we design a private model compression framework RONA. Following the knowledge distillation paradigm, we jointly use hint learning, distillation learning, and self learning to train a compact and fast neural network. The knowledge distilled from the cumbersome model is adaptively bounded and carefully perturbed to enforce differential privacy. We further propose an elegant query sample selection method to reduce the number of queries and control the privacy loss. A series of empirical evaluations as well as the implementation on an Android mobile device show that RONA can not only compress cumbersome models efficiently but also provide a strong privacy guarantee. For example, on SVHN, when a meaningful $(9.83,10^{-6})$-differential privacy is guaranteed, the compact model trained by RONA can obtain 20$\times$ compression ratio and 19$\times$ speed-up with merely 0.97% accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-used technique for training compact neural networks by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models. This approach has become essential for deploying deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The technique addresses key challenges in model compression, balancing performance with computational efficiency and memory requirements. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across various domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications, enabling practical deployment of neural networks on mobile devices and edge computing systems.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Towards Model Agnostic Federated Learning Using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Is it possible to design an universal API for federated learning using which an ad-hoc group of data-holders (agents) collaborate with each other and perform federated learning? Such an API would necessarily need to be model-agnostic i.e. make no assumption about the model architecture being used by the agents, and also cannot rely on having representative public data at hand. Knowledge distillation (KD) is the obvious tool of choice to design such protocols. However, surprisingly, we show that most natural KD-based federated learning protocols have poor performance.   To investigate this, we propose a new theoretical framework, Federated Kernel ridge regression, which can capture both model heterogeneity as well as data heterogeneity. Our analysis shows that the degradation is largely due to a fundamental limitation of knowledge distillation under data heterogeneity. We further validate our framework by analyzing and designing new protocols based on KD. Their performance on real world experiments using neural networks, though still unsatisfactory, closely matches our theoretical predictions.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Reinforced Multi-Teacher Selection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In natural language processing (NLP) tasks, slow inference speed and huge footprints in GPU usage remain the bottleneck of applying pre-trained deep models in production. As a popular method for model compression, knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from one or multiple large (teacher) models to a small (student) model. When multiple teacher models are available in distillation, the state-of-the-art methods assign a fixed weight to a teacher model in the whole distillation. Furthermore, most of the existing methods allocate an equal weight to every teacher model. In this paper, we observe that, due to the complexity of training examples and the differences in student model capability, learning differentially from teacher models can lead to better performance of student models distilled. We systematically develop a reinforced method to dynamically assign weights to teacher models for different training instances and optimize the performance of student model. Our extensive experimental results on several NLP tasks clearly verify the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for enabling the deployment of large neural networks on resource-constrained devices. These methods address the fundamental challenge of maintaining model performance while dramatically reducing computational and storage requirements. By leveraging knowledge transfer from large teacher models to compact student models, practitioners can achieve efficient inference without substantial accuracy loss. This survey synthesizes recent advances in both classical compression approaches and innovative distillation strategies tailored for deep learning and NLP applications.

papers_seen.author: Novak
papers_seen.title: The Necessity and Effectiveness of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has become an essential technique for deploying deep learning models in practical, resource-constrained environments. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is not merely a performance optimization tool, but a fundamental necessity for making state-of-the-art models deployable on edge devices and in latency-sensitive applications. Through comprehensive examination of recent research, we demonstrate that knowledge distillation effectively addresses the critical gap between model capability and practical deployability, while also enabling meaningful improvements in model generalization and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Fundamental Necessity for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical and indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This method transfers knowledge from well-trained teacher models to lightweight student networks, enabling the practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications. While alternative compression methods exist, knowledge distillation stands out as a uniquely flexible and effective approach that preserves performance while dramatically reducing computational and memory requirements.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Understanding and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing neural networks by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models. This approach addresses critical deployment challenges by reducing computational requirements, memory footprint, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal learning, making knowledge distillation an essential strategy for deploying powerful deep learning models on resource-constrained devices.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These approaches enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, maintaining or improving performance while reducing computational costs and memory requirements. The techniques have been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, federated learning, and multimodal systems, addressing critical challenges in practical AI deployment.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Collaborative Distillation for Ultra-Resolution Universal Style Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Universal style transfer methods typically leverage rich representations from deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (e.g., VGG-19) pre-trained on large collections of images. Despite the effectiveness, its application is heavily constrained by the large model size to handle ultra-resolution images given limited memory. In this work, we present a new knowledge distillation method (named Collaborative Distillation) for encoder-decoder based neural style transfer to reduce the convolutional filters. The main idea is underpinned by a finding that the encoder-decoder pairs construct an exclusive collaborative relationship, which is regarded as a new kind of knowledge for style transfer models. Moreover, to overcome the feature size mismatch when applying collaborative distillation, a linear embedding loss is introduced to drive the student network to learn a linear embedding of the teacher's features. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method when applied to different universal style transfer approaches (WCT and AdaIN), even if the model size is reduced by 15.5 times. Especially, on WCT with the compressed models, we achieve ultra-resolution (over 40 megapixels) universal style transfer on a 12GB GPU for the first time. Further experiments on optimization-based stylization scheme show the generality of our algorithm on different stylization paradigms. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/mingsun-tse/collaborative-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Essential Technique for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments by enabling the transfer of knowledge from large teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach maintains competitive performance while substantially reducing model size, computational requirements, and inference latency. Knowledge distillation addresses fundamental deployment challenges across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, making state-of-the-art models practical and accessible for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Barnes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a pivotal technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach addresses critical deployment challenges where computational resources and inference speed are limited. While traditional knowledge distillation methods require access to training data, recent advances include data-free approaches and specialized variants for specific domains. Applications span natural language processing tasks, computer vision, federated learning, and other domains, with notable success in compressing BERT-based language models, improving translation systems, and enabling efficient inference on resource-constrained devices.

papers_seen.author: Powers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Essential Technique for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for compressing large neural networks into efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. Rather than being merely a supplementary compression method, knowledge distillation represents a fundamental paradigm shift in how we approach model training and deployment. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be considered not simply as model compression, but as a versatile learning framework applicable across diverse architectures, domains, and tasks in both computer vision and natural language processing. The evidence demonstrates that distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments while maintaining substantial performance gains, and its mechanisms reveal deeper insights about regularization and learning dynamics.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a training technique that transfers knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach has emerged as a critical strategy for model compression in deep learning, enabling the deployment of high-performing models on resource-constrained devices without significant performance degradation. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, graph neural networks, and multimodal learning. By leveraging soft target probabilities and intermediate representations from teacher networks, distillation enables practical deployment while maintaining competitive performance levels.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: BERT Learns to Teach: Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We present Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning (MetaDistil), a simple yet effective alternative to traditional knowledge distillation (KD) methods where the teacher model is fixed during training. We show the teacher network can learn to better transfer knowledge to the student network (i.e., learning to teach) with the feedback from the performance of the distilled student network in a meta learning framework. Moreover, we introduce a pilot update mechanism to improve the alignment between the inner-learner and meta-learner in meta learning algorithms that focus on an improved inner-learner. Experiments on various benchmarks show that MetaDistil can yield significant improvements compared with traditional KD algorithms and is less sensitive to the choice of different student capacity and hyperparameters, facilitating the use of KD on different tasks and models.

papers_seen.author: Conner
papers_seen.title: Distilling Task-Specific Knowledge from BERT into Simple Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: In the natural language processing literature, neural networks are becoming increasingly deeper and complex. The recent poster child of this trend is the deep language representation model, which includes BERT, ELMo, and GPT. These developments have led to the conviction that previous-generation, shallower neural networks for language understanding are obsolete. In this paper, however, we demonstrate that rudimentary, lightweight neural networks can still be made competitive without architecture changes, external training data, or additional input features. We propose to distill knowledge from BERT, a state-of-the-art language representation model, into a single-layer BiLSTM, as well as its siamese counterpart for sentence-pair tasks. Across multiple datasets in paraphrasing, natural language inference, and sentiment classification, we achieve comparable results with ELMo, while using roughly 100 times fewer parameters and 15 times less inference time.

papers_seen.author: Freeman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from complex teacher models to compact student networks, addressing critical deployment challenges including computational efficiency, memory requirements, and inference latency. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized areas such as federated learning and graph neural networks, making it an indispensable tool in modern deep learning practice.

papers_seen.author: Leonard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Vital Approach for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Systems
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student models, reducing inference time and memory requirements while maintaining competitive performance. This paper examines the fundamental principles, applications, and theoretical foundations of knowledge distillation across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized tasks, demonstrating how these compression techniques address real-world deployment challenges in modern deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from large teacher models to compact student networks, this approach enables deployment in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks. The technique addresses critical challenges in inference speed, memory footprint, and computational efficiency without substantial accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation in Deep Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation deals with the problem of training a smaller model (Student) from a high capacity source model (Teacher) so as to retain most of its performance. Existing approaches use either the training data or meta-data extracted from it in order to train the Student. However, accessing the dataset on which the Teacher has been trained may not always be feasible if the dataset is very large or it poses privacy or safety concerns (e.g., bio-metric or medical data). Hence, in this paper, we propose a novel data-free method to train the Student from the Teacher. Without even using any meta-data, we synthesize the Data Impressions from the complex Teacher model and utilize these as surrogates for the original training data samples to transfer its learning to Student via knowledge distillation. We, therefore, dub our method "Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation" and demonstrate that our framework results in competitive generalization performance as achieved by distillation using the actual training data samples on multiple benchmark datasets.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-used technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining predictive performance. This approach involves transferring knowledge from a larger teacher model to a smaller student model through various mechanisms including soft label matching, feature mimicking, and adversarial training. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized tasks such as 3D object detection and information retrieval. The technique enables practical deployment of powerful models in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive accuracy with their larger counterparts.

papers_seen.author: Dixon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique that enables the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach has become essential for deploying advanced deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, recommender systems, and graph neural networks, addressing critical challenges in real-world model deployment with reduced computational and memory requirements.

papers_seen.author: Ware
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach addresses critical challenges in deploying state-of-the-art neural networks to resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. By examining diverse applications and methodologies across multiple domains, knowledge distillation represents not merely a supplementary compression technique, but a versatile learning paradigm essential for practical deployment of deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Enabling Efficient Deep Learning Through Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and NLP. By enabling compact student models to learn from larger teacher models, distillation addresses the critical challenge of deploying sophisticated neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive performance. This paper surveys the theoretical foundations and practical applications of knowledge distillation, demonstrating how this approach achieves significant model size reduction and inference speedup across diverse domains including vision, language processing, and neural architecture optimization.

papers_seen.author: Joyce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models. This approach has become essential for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments and real-world applications where inference speed and memory footprint are critical constraints. The method has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks, demonstrating consistent improvements in model efficiency while maintaining competitive accuracy with the original teacher models.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: Robust Re-Identification by Multiple Views Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: To achieve robustness in Re-Identification, standard methods leverage tracking information in a Video-To-Video fashion. However, these solutions face a large drop in performance for single image queries (e.g., Image-To-Video setting). Recent works address this severe degradation by transferring temporal information from a Video-based network to an Image-based one. In this work, we devise a training strategy that allows the transfer of a superior knowledge, arising from a set of views depicting the target object. Our proposal - Views Knowledge Distillation (VKD) - pins this visual variety as a supervision signal within a teacher-student framework, where the teacher educates a student who observes fewer views. As a result, the student outperforms not only its teacher but also the current state-of-the-art in Image-To-Video by a wide margin (6.3% mAP on MARS, 8.6% on Duke-Video-ReId and 5% on VeRi-776). A thorough analysis - on Person, Vehicle and Animal Re-ID - investigates the properties of VKD from a qualitatively and quantitatively perspective. Code is available at https://github.com/aimagelab/VKD.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Compelling Strategy for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and essential technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By enabling the transfer of knowledge from large teacher networks to compact student models, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems across resource-constrained environments. This technique has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications, offering systematic solutions to reduce computational overhead and memory requirements without proportional accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Less is More: Task-aware Layer-wise Distillation for Language Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Layer-wise distillation is a powerful tool to compress large models (i.e. teacher models) into small ones (i.e., student models). The student distills knowledge from the teacher by mimicking the hidden representations of the teacher at every intermediate layer. However, layer-wise distillation is difficult. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Task-aware layEr-wise Distillation (TED). TED designs task-aware filters to align the hidden representations of the student and the teacher at each layer. The filters select the knowledge that is useful for the target task from the hidden representations. As such, TED reduces the knowledge gap between the two models and helps the student to fit better on the target task. We evaluate TED in two scenarios: continual pre-training and fine-tuning. TED demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over existing distillation methods in both scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/cliang1453/task-aware-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP
