papers_seen.author: Chandler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices. The technique is particularly valuable in natural language processing and computer vision, where modern models impose significant computational burdens. Beyond basic compression, knowledge distillation serves diverse purposes including domain adaptation, improved generalization, and efficient federated learning. Recent advances have expanded distillation methods to include intermediate layer alignment, attention-based mechanisms, and theoretical frameworks that explain its effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression and knowledge transfer across diverse domains in deep learning and natural language processing. This approach enables training of smaller, more efficient student models by leveraging knowledge from larger teacher models, addressing critical challenges of computational cost and deployment constraints. Recent advances demonstrate the versatility of distillation across multiple architectures and applications, from vision transformers to language models, with significant improvements in efficiency while maintaining or improving performance.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for enabling the deployment of large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from larger, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student networks while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and reinforcement learning, addressing the fundamental challenges of reducing computational costs, memory requirements, and inference latency. The field has progressed from simple approaches to sophisticated methods that transfer feature-level and attention-based knowledge, with recent advances including multi-teacher strategies, data-free distillation, and cross-modal knowledge transfer.

papers_seen.author: Jacobs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Fundamental Approach to Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a cornerstone technique for creating efficient, deployable deep learning models without sacrificing performance. By enabling smaller student models to learn from larger teacher models, distillation achieves substantial reductions in model size and computational requirements while maintaining competitive accuracy. This approach addresses critical practical challenges in deploying state-of-the-art neural networks across diverse domains, from natural language processing to computer vision. The technique's versatility and effectiveness make it essential for real-world AI deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger, high-performing teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices without substantial performance degradation. Recent advances in knowledge distillation have expanded beyond simple output-level transfer to include intermediate representations, attention mechanisms, feature matching, and adversarial learning strategies. The technique has proven particularly valuable in NLP applications where pre-trained language models face computational and memory constraints, and in federated learning scenarios with heterogeneous devices. This synthesis reviews the fundamental mechanisms of knowledge distillation, its applications across different architectures and tasks, and emerging strategies for improving distillation effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Kidd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Strategic Transfer of Learning from Large to Small Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful paradigm for model compression that enables the transfer of knowledge from large teacher networks to smaller student models. This approach addresses critical challenges in deploying deep neural networks across resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. Through strategic knowledge transfer mechanisms, distillation techniques have proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal learning. The success of these methods relies on sophisticated mechanisms for capturing and transferring both task-relevant information and feature representations. Modern distillation frameworks continue to evolve, incorporating adaptive weighting schemes, layer-wise knowledge transfer, and adversarial learning strategies to maximize compression efficiency while minimizing performance degradation.

papers_seen.author: Waller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Fundamental Approach to Efficient Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a dominant paradigm for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. This technique enables the transfer of knowledge from larger teacher networks to smaller student networks, making deep learning systems practical for resource-constrained environments. Beyond simple performance preservation, knowledge distillation functions as a form of learned regularization and offers broader benefits including robustness transfer, fairness improvements, and enhanced interpretability. The field has evolved significantly to address diverse scenarios and applications across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Dudley
papers_seen.title: Attention-Guided Answer Distillation for Machine Reading Comprehension
papers_seen.abstract: Despite that current reading comprehension systems have achieved significant advancements, their promising performances are often obtained at the cost of making an ensemble of numerous models. Besides, existing approaches are also vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper tackles these problems by leveraging knowledge distillation, which aims to transfer knowledge from an ensemble model to a single model. We first demonstrate that vanilla knowledge distillation applied to answer span prediction is effective for reading comprehension systems. We then propose two novel approaches that not only penalize the prediction on confusing answers but also guide the training with alignment information distilled from the ensemble. Experiments show that our best student model has only a slight drop of 0.4% F1 on the SQuAD test set compared to the ensemble teacher, while running 12x faster during inference. It even outperforms the teacher on adversarial SQuAD datasets and NarrativeQA benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from larger, more expressive teacher models to smaller student networks while maintaining competitive performance. This synthesis examines the theoretical foundations, methodological advances, and practical applications of knowledge distillation across computer vision and natural language processing tasks, including recent developments in handling soft labels, intermediate feature representations, and domain-specific adaptations.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Does Knowledge Distillation Really Work?
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique for training a small student network to emulate a larger teacher model, such as an ensemble of networks. We show that while knowledge distillation can improve student generalization, it does not typically work as it is commonly understood: there often remains a surprisingly large discrepancy between the predictive distributions of the teacher and the student, even in cases when the student has the capacity to perfectly match the teacher. We identify difficulties in optimization as a key reason for why the student is unable to match the teacher. We also show how the details of the dataset used for distillation play a role in how closely the student matches the teacher -- and that more closely matching the teacher paradoxically does not always lead to better student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Learning Student-Friendly Teacher Networks for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel knowledge distillation approach to facilitate the transfer of dark knowledge from a teacher to a student. Contrary to most of the existing methods that rely on effective training of student models given pretrained teachers, we aim to learn the teacher models that are friendly to students and, consequently, more appropriate for knowledge transfer. In other words, at the time of optimizing a teacher model, the proposed algorithm learns the student branches jointly to obtain student-friendly representations. Since the main goal of our approach lies in training teacher models and the subsequent knowledge distillation procedure is straightforward, most of the existing knowledge distillation methods can adopt this technique to improve the performance of diverse student models in terms of accuracy and convergence speed. The proposed algorithm demonstrates outstanding accuracy in several well-known knowledge distillation techniques with various combinations of teacher and student models even in the case that their architectures are heterogeneous and there is no prior knowledge about student models at the time of training teacher networks.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become indispensable techniques for deploying deep learning and NLP models in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a fundamental paradigm shift in model deployment, offering practical solutions for real-world applications where latency, memory, and computational constraints are critical considerations. We examine various distillation approaches, their applications across diverse tasks, and their effectiveness in maintaining model performance while reducing computational overhead.

papers_seen.author: Heath
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are critical techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These approaches enable the transfer of knowledge from large "teacher" models to smaller "student" networks, reducing computational costs and parameter counts while maintaining competitive performance. Recent work spans diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, federated learning, and reinforcement learning, demonstrating the broad applicability of these compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning: A Comprehensive Strategy for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile technique in deep learning, enabling the compression of large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from complex teacher networks to simpler student networks, addressing critical challenges in deploying deep learning models on resource-constrained devices. Recent advances span multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning, with innovations in distillation mechanisms, architectural designs, and theoretical foundations. The technique has proven effective not only for model compression but also for improving interpretability, enabling lifelong learning, and facilitating federated learning scenarios. Despite its widespread adoption, ongoing research continues to refine distillation methods and expand their applicability across diverse tasks and model types.

papers_seen.author: Humphrey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Benefits, Applications, and Empirical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for training compact neural networks by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models. This approach enables the deployment of deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive performance across diverse applications including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph learning. This paper examines the theoretical foundations, practical applications, and empirical findings surrounding knowledge distillation and model compression, highlighting both the effectiveness of the technique and important considerations for its successful implementation.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Show, Attend and Distill:Knowledge Distillation via Attention-based Feature Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation extracts general knowledge from a pre-trained teacher network and provides guidance to a target student network. Most studies manually tie intermediate features of the teacher and student, and transfer knowledge through pre-defined links. However, manual selection often constructs ineffective links that limit the improvement from the distillation. There has been an attempt to address the problem, but it is still challenging to identify effective links under practical scenarios. In this paper, we introduce an effective and efficient feature distillation method utilizing all the feature levels of the teacher without manually selecting the links. Specifically, our method utilizes an attention-based meta-network that learns relative similarities between features, and applies identified similarities to control distillation intensities of all possible pairs. As a result, our method determines competent links more efficiently than the previous approach and provides better performance on model compression and transfer learning tasks. Further qualitative analyses and ablative studies describe how our method contributes to better distillation. The implementation code is available at github.com/clovaai/attention-feature-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Transformative Paradigm for Deep Learning and NLP Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as one of the most effective and versatile techniques for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and NLP. Rather than treating it merely as a tool for improving accuracy, knowledge distillation represents a fundamental shift in how we approach model training and deployment. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be adopted as a core paradigm in deep learning systems because it simultaneously addresses multiple critical challenges: reducing computational complexity, enabling privacy-preserving model transfer, improving model interpretability, and facilitating the training of efficient models that match or exceed the performance of their larger counterparts. We examine diverse applications across computer vision, NLP, and graph neural networks to demonstrate the broad applicability and robustness of distillation-based approaches.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Fundamental Necessity for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical and indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This method transfers knowledge from well-trained teacher models to lightweight student networks, enabling the practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications. While alternative compression methods exist, knowledge distillation stands out as a uniquely flexible and effective approach that preserves performance while dramatically reducing computational and memory requirements.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Powerful Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as one of the most effective techniques for training compact, efficient neural networks without sacrificing performance. This approach enables smaller "student" models to learn from larger, high-capacity "teacher" models through knowledge transfer, making deep learning systems practical for resource-constrained environments including mobile devices and real-time applications. The technique's versatility has enabled successful applications across diverse domains from computer vision to natural language processing.

papers_seen.author: Lin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Transformative Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining or improving performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student models, knowledge distillation addresses fundamental challenges in deploying deep learning systems to resource-constrained environments. This approach has demonstrated significant practical benefits across diverse domains, enabling efficient inference with minimal accuracy degradation. The technique encompasses multiple strategies including soft target matching, feature-level alignment, and advanced frameworks such as federated distillation and online distillation.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation in Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Since deep learning became a key player in natural language processing (NLP), many deep learning models have been showing remarkable performances in a variety of NLP tasks, and in some cases, they are even outperforming humans. Such high performance can be explained by efficient knowledge representation of deep learning models. While many methods have been proposed to learn more efficient representation, knowledge distillation from pretrained deep networks suggest that we can use more information from the soft target probability to train other neural networks. In this paper, we propose a new knowledge distillation method self-knowledge distillation, based on the soft target probabilities of the training model itself, where multimode information is distilled from the word embedding space right below the softmax layer. Due to the time complexity, our method approximates the soft target probabilities. In experiments, we applied the proposed method to two different and fundamental NLP tasks: language model and neural machine translation. The experiment results show that our proposed method improves performance on the tasks.

papers_seen.author: Powers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Essential Technique for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for compressing large neural networks into efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. Rather than being merely a supplementary compression method, knowledge distillation represents a fundamental paradigm shift in how we approach model training and deployment. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be considered not simply as model compression, but as a versatile learning framework applicable across diverse architectures, domains, and tasks in both computer vision and natural language processing. The evidence demonstrates that distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments while maintaining substantial performance gains, and its mechanisms reveal deeper insights about regularization and learning dynamics.

papers_seen.author: Leblanc
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Deploying Deep Learning Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining comparable performance. This review examines key approaches including structural distillation, feature-based distillation, and application-specific compression strategies across various domains. The evidence demonstrates that knowledge distillation consistently enables substantial model size reduction with minimal accuracy loss, making it an indispensable tool for practical deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Cowan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression in deep learning, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large teacher models to compact student models. This approach has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and federated learning, addressing critical challenges in model efficiency while maintaining performance. The technique involves various strategies ranging from soft label matching to feature-level alignment, with ongoing research exploring optimal distillation procedures, selective knowledge transfer, and integration with complementary training methodologies.

papers_seen.author: Bentley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Technique for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach addresses the critical challenge of deploying sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments by transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact student networks. Beyond simple performance preservation, knowledge distillation provides broader benefits including improved interpretability, enhanced robustness, and effective implementation across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommendation systems. The technique has evolved from simple logit-matching approaches to sophisticated methods incorporating feature-level and attention-based knowledge transfer, establishing itself as an essential strategy for making state-of-the-art models practical for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Welch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Enabling Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression techniques have become essential approaches for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This paper synthesizes recent advances in knowledge distillation across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks, demonstrating the broad applicability and effectiveness of these compression techniques for practical deployment scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Critical Technique for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an indispensable technique for deploying powerful deep neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models, distillation addresses fundamental challenges in making advanced deep learning practical. This position argues that knowledge distillation is essential for real-world applications, demonstrates its effectiveness across diverse domains, and examines recent advances that have expanded its applicability beyond traditional supervised learning contexts.

papers_seen.author: Holmes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become essential techniques for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. This synthesis examines the state of knowledge distillation across multiple domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and 3D object detection. The research demonstrates various approaches to transferring knowledge from large teacher models to compact student networks, addressing critical challenges in model efficiency while maintaining performance. Key advances include multi-teacher distillation strategies, layer-wise knowledge transfer, attention-based mechanisms, and domain-specific applications that enable practical deployment of neural networks with reduced computational footprints and latency.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are essential techniques for deploying deep learning models efficiently in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from larger, computationally expensive models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This synthesis examines the theoretical foundations, methodological innovations, and practical applications of knowledge distillation across various domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and federated learning. The review covers training strategies, multi-teacher approaches, zero-shot methods, and task-specific compression techniques, while also addressing emerging challenges and opportunities for improving model efficiency without sacrificing accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Is Label Smoothing Truly Incompatible with Knowledge Distillation: An Empirical Study
papers_seen.abstract: This work aims to empirically clarify a recently discovered perspective that label smoothing is incompatible with knowledge distillation. We begin by introducing the motivation behind on how this incompatibility is raised, i.e., label smoothing erases relative information between teacher logits. We provide a novel connection on how label smoothing affects distributions of semantically similar and dissimilar classes. Then we propose a metric to quantitatively measure the degree of erased information in sample's representation. After that, we study its one-sidedness and imperfection of the incompatibility view through massive analyses, visualizations and comprehensive experiments on Image Classification, Binary Networks, and Neural Machine Translation. Finally, we broadly discuss several circumstances wherein label smoothing will indeed lose its effectiveness. Project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/LS_and_KD/index.html.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Critical Technique for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining predictive performance. This approach involves training a student model to mimic the behavior of a larger teacher model, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments. Despite its widespread adoption across various domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks, the mechanisms underlying knowledge distillation remain partially understood. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents an essential yet imperfect solution to the model compression challenge, with significant implications for practical deep learning applications while presenting important theoretical and practical limitations.

papers_seen.author: Green
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and increasingly indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning models in resource-constrained environments by transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student models. Applications span diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized tasks, with methodologies ranging from simple output-level distillation to sophisticated multi-teacher frameworks and feature-based approaches. The technique addresses critical challenges in model efficiency while preserving accuracy, making it essential for real-world applications where computational and memory constraints are significant limiting factors.

papers_seen.author: Shields
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach involves transferring knowledge from large teacher networks to smaller student networks through various mechanisms, enabling practical deployment in resource-constrained environments. Applications span multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and federated learning, with recent advances addressing domain adaptation, fairness concerns, adversarial robustness, and theoretical foundations of the distillation process.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge distillation from multi-modal to mono-modal segmentation networks
papers_seen.abstract: The joint use of multiple imaging modalities for medical image segmentation has been widely studied in recent years. The fusion of information from different modalities has demonstrated to improve the segmentation accuracy, with respect to mono-modal segmentations, in several applications. However, acquiring multiple modalities is usually not possible in a clinical setting due to a limited number of physicians and scanners, and to limit costs and scan time. Most of the time, only one modality is acquired. In this paper, we propose KD-Net, a framework to transfer knowledge from a trained multi-modal network (teacher) to a mono-modal one (student). The proposed method is an adaptation of the generalized distillation framework where the student network is trained on a subset (1 modality) of the teacher's inputs (n modalities). We illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in brain tumor segmentation with the BraTS 2018 dataset. Using different architectures, we show that the student network effectively learns from the teacher and always outperforms the baseline mono-modal network in terms of segmentation accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation in Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Since deep learning became a key player in natural language processing (NLP), many deep learning models have been showing remarkable performances in a variety of NLP tasks, and in some cases, they are even outperforming humans. Such high performance can be explained by efficient knowledge representation of deep learning models. While many methods have been proposed to learn more efficient representation, knowledge distillation from pretrained deep networks suggest that we can use more information from the soft target probability to train other neural networks. In this paper, we propose a new knowledge distillation method self-knowledge distillation, based on the soft target probabilities of the training model itself, where multimode information is distilled from the word embedding space right below the softmax layer. Due to the time complexity, our method approximates the soft target probabilities. In experiments, we applied the proposed method to two different and fundamental NLP tasks: language model and neural machine translation. The experiment results show that our proposed method improves performance on the tasks.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Linkless Link Prediction via Relational Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown exceptional performance in the task of link prediction. Despite their effectiveness, the high latency brought by non-trivial neighborhood data dependency limits GNNs in practical deployments. Conversely, the known efficient MLPs are much less effective than GNNs due to the lack of relational knowledge. In this work, to combine the advantages of GNNs and MLPs, we start with exploring direct knowledge distillation (KD) methods for link prediction, i.e., predicted logit-based matching and node representation-based matching. Upon observing direct KD analogs do not perform well for link prediction, we propose a relational KD framework, Linkless Link Prediction (LLP), to distill knowledge for link prediction with MLPs. Unlike simple KD methods that match independent link logits or node representations, LLP distills relational knowledge that is centered around each (anchor) node to the student MLP. Specifically, we propose rank-based matching and distribution-based matching strategies that complement each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLP boosts the link prediction performance of MLPs with significant margins, and even outperforms the teacher GNNs on 7 out of 8 benchmarks. LLP also achieves a 70.68x speedup in link prediction inference compared to GNNs on the large-scale OGB dataset.

papers_seen.author: Rivera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Transformative Paradigm Essential for Modern Deep Learning and NLP Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and transformative technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining or even improving performance. This approach enables the practical deployment of deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices and in latency-sensitive applications. Beyond simple performance optimization, knowledge distillation represents a core paradigm shift in how deep learning models are trained and deployed, addressing multiple critical challenges including computational efficiency, privacy preservation, model interpretability, and robustness enhancement. The technique has proven versatile across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized architectures, making it essential for modern deep learning applications.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression represent fundamental techniques for deploying deep neural networks efficiently across resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while preserving or enhancing predictive performance. This synthesis examines the core mechanisms, diverse applications, and innovations in knowledge distillation across domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks, demonstrating how distillation functions as both a compression technique and a powerful regularization mechanism.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Improved Feature Distillation via Projector Ensemble
papers_seen.abstract: In knowledge distillation, previous feature distillation methods mainly focus on the design of loss functions and the selection of the distilled layers, while the effect of the feature projector between the student and the teacher remains under-explored. In this paper, we first discuss a plausible mechanism of the projector with empirical evidence and then propose a new feature distillation method based on a projector ensemble for further performance improvement. We observe that the student network benefits from a projector even if the feature dimensions of the student and the teacher are the same. Training a student backbone without a projector can be considered as a multi-task learning process, namely achieving discriminative feature extraction for classification and feature matching between the student and the teacher for distillation at the same time. We hypothesize and empirically verify that without a projector, the student network tends to overfit the teacher's feature distributions despite having different architecture and weights initialization. This leads to degradation on the quality of the student's deep features that are eventually used in classification. Adding a projector, on the other hand, disentangles the two learning tasks and helps the student network to focus better on the main feature extraction task while still being able to utilize teacher features as a guidance through the projector. Motivated by the positive effect of the projector in feature distillation, we propose an ensemble of projectors to further improve the quality of student features. Experimental results on different datasets with a series of teacher-student pairs illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge From a Deep Pose Regressor Network
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a novel method to distill knowledge from a deep pose regressor network for efficient Visual Odometry (VO). Standard distillation relies on "dark knowledge" for successful knowledge transfer. As this knowledge is not available in pose regression and the teacher prediction is not always accurate, we propose to emphasize the knowledge transfer only when we trust the teacher. We achieve this by using teacher loss as a confidence score which places variable relative importance on the teacher prediction. We inject this confidence score to the main training task via Attentive Imitation Loss (AIL) and when learning the intermediate representation of the teacher through Attentive Hint Training (AHT) approach. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work which successfully distill the knowledge from a deep pose regression network. Our evaluation on the KITTI and Malaga dataset shows that we can keep the student prediction close to the teacher with up to 92.95% parameter reduction and 2.12x faster in computation time.

papers_seen.author: House
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Critical Technique for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models without substantial performance loss. This technique transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive accuracy. Knowledge distillation is particularly valuable in natural language processing, where modern pre-trained models like BERT impose significant computational burdens for inference. Beyond compression, distillation serves broader purposes including domain adaptation, heterogeneous federated learning, and improved model generalization. The versatility and effectiveness of knowledge distillation across diverse applications demonstrate its importance as a foundational technique in modern deep learning.

papers_seen.author: Hickman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Critical Approach to Efficient Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing deep neural networks while maintaining competitive performance. Rather than developing entirely new lightweight architectures, distillation enables the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller student models, addressing a fundamental challenge in deploying deep learning systems to resource-constrained environments. This approach has demonstrated success across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, offering a practical pathway to reduce computational costs without sacrificing model quality.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer via Adversarial Belief Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Performing knowledge transfer from a large teacher network to a smaller student is a popular task in modern deep learning applications. However, due to growing dataset sizes and stricter privacy regulations, it is increasingly common not to have access to the data that was used to train the teacher. We propose a novel method which trains a student to match the predictions of its teacher without using any data or metadata. We achieve this by training an adversarial generator to search for images on which the student poorly matches the teacher, and then using them to train the student. Our resulting student closely approximates its teacher for simple datasets like SVHN, and on CIFAR10 we improve on the state-of-the-art for few-shot distillation (with 100 images per class), despite using no data. Finally, we also propose a metric to quantify the degree of belief matching between teacher and student in the vicinity of decision boundaries, and observe a significantly higher match between our zero-shot student and the teacher, than between a student distilled with real data and the teacher. Code available at: https://github.com/polo5/ZeroShotKnowledgeTransfer

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are essential techniques for deploying deep learning models efficiently in resource-constrained environments. The review covers training strategies, multi-teacher approaches, zero-shot methods, and task-specific compression techniques, while also addressing emerging challenges and opportunities for improving model efficiency without sacrificing accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Approaches and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models by transferring knowledge from teacher models to student models. This approach addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, federated learning, and specialized applications like medical image segmentation and style transfer. Knowledge distillation enables significant reductions in model size and computational requirements while maintaining or improving performance compared to baseline models.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Feature-map-level Online Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Feature maps contain rich information about image intensity and spatial correlation. However, previous online knowledge distillation methods only utilize the class probabilities. Thus in this paper, we propose an online knowledge distillation method that transfers not only the knowledge of the class probabilities but also that of the feature map using the adversarial training framework. We train multiple networks simultaneously by employing discriminators to distinguish the feature map distributions of different networks. Each network has its corresponding discriminator which discriminates the feature map from its own as fake while classifying that of the other network as real. By training a network to fool the corresponding discriminator, it can learn the other network's feature map distribution. We show that our method performs better than the conventional direct alignment method such as L1 and is more suitable for online distillation. Also, we propose a novel cyclic learning scheme for training more than two networks together. We have applied our method to various network architectures on the classification task and discovered a significant improvement of performance especially in the case of training a pair of a small network and a large one.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Revisiting Knowledge Distillation via Label Smoothing Regularization
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to distill the knowledge of a cumbersome teacher model into a lightweight student model. Its success is generally attributed to the privileged information on similarities among categories provided by the teacher model, and in this sense, only strong teacher models are deployed to teach weaker students in practice. In this work, we challenge this common belief by following experimental observations: 1) beyond the acknowledgment that the teacher can improve the student, the student can also enhance the teacher significantly by reversing the KD procedure; 2) a poorly-trained teacher with much lower accuracy than the student can still improve the latter significantly. To explain these observations, we provide a theoretical analysis of the relationships between KD and label smoothing regularization. We prove that 1) KD is a type of learned label smoothing regularization and 2) label smoothing regularization provides a virtual teacher model for KD. From these results, we argue that the success of KD is not fully due to the similarity information between categories from teachers, but also to the regularization of soft targets, which is equally or even more important.   Based on these analyses, we further propose a novel Teacher-free Knowledge Distillation (Tf-KD) framework, where a student model learns from itself or manuallydesigned regularization distribution. The Tf-KD achieves comparable performance with normal KD from a superior teacher, which is well applied when a stronger teacher model is unavailable. Meanwhile, Tf-KD is generic and can be directly deployed for training deep neural networks. Without any extra computation cost, Tf-KD achieves up to 0.65\% improvement on ImageNet over well-established baseline models, which is superior to label smoothing regularization.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger, high-performing teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices without substantial performance degradation. Recent advances in knowledge distillation have expanded beyond simple output-level transfer to include intermediate representations, attention mechanisms, feature matching, and adversarial learning strategies. The technique has proven particularly valuable in NLP applications where pre-trained language models face computational and memory constraints, and in federated learning scenarios with heterogeneous devices. This synthesis reviews the fundamental mechanisms of knowledge distillation, its applications across different architectures and tasks, and emerging strategies for improving distillation effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Harmon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for developing efficient neural networks capable of deployment in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from larger, well-trained teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, reducing computational requirements while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation operates through various mechanisms including soft label matching, feature-level alignment, and adversarial training frameworks. Applications span across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, federated learning, and specialized tasks such as visual-linguistic models and 3D object detection. Recent advances have expanded the field beyond simple logit matching to encompass intermediate representation transfer, data-free scenarios, multi-teacher frameworks, and task-specific optimizations, making knowledge distillation an increasingly versatile and essential approach for modern deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Towards Model Agnostic Federated Learning Using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Is it possible to design an universal API for federated learning using which an ad-hoc group of data-holders (agents) collaborate with each other and perform federated learning? Such an API would necessarily need to be model-agnostic i.e. make no assumption about the model architecture being used by the agents, and also cannot rely on having representative public data at hand. Knowledge distillation (KD) is the obvious tool of choice to design such protocols. However, surprisingly, we show that most natural KD-based federated learning protocols have poor performance.   To investigate this, we propose a new theoretical framework, Federated Kernel ridge regression, which can capture both model heterogeneity as well as data heterogeneity. Our analysis shows that the degradation is largely due to a fundamental limitation of knowledge distillation under data heterogeneity. We further validate our framework by analyzing and designing new protocols based on KD. Their performance on real world experiments using neural networks, though still unsatisfactory, closely matches our theoretical predictions.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are essential techniques for deploying deep learning and NLP models in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from larger, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This synthesis examines the theoretical foundations, methodological innovations, and practical applications of knowledge distillation across diverse domains, covering training strategies, multi-teacher approaches, data-free methods, and task-specific compression techniques, while addressing emerging challenges in maintaining model accuracy without sacrificing efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, well-trained teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student networks. This approach has become increasingly important for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. The technique applies broadly across computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and other domains, enabling practical deployment on mobile and embedded devices. Knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in model deployment by reducing computational costs, memory requirements, and inference latency while preserving or even improving model accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation for Deep Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in model compression have provided procedures for compressing large neural networks to a fraction of their original size while retaining most if not all of their accuracy. However, all of these approaches rely on access to the original training set, which might not always be possible if the network to be compressed was trained on a very large dataset, or on a dataset whose release poses privacy or safety concerns as may be the case for biometrics tasks. We present a method for data-free knowledge distillation, which is able to compress deep neural networks trained on large-scale datasets to a fraction of their size leveraging only some extra metadata to be provided with a pretrained model release. We also explore different kinds of metadata that can be used with our method, and discuss tradeoffs involved in using each of them.

papers_seen.author: Deleon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Yet Imperfect Solution for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining predictive performance. This approach involves training a student model to mimic the behavior of a larger teacher model, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments. Despite its widespread adoption across various domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications, knowledge distillation represents an essential yet imperfect solution to the model compression challenge, with significant implications for practical deep learning applications while presenting important theoretical and practical limitations.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Advances and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression and efficient neural network training, enabling the transfer of knowledge from larger teacher models to compact student networks. This paper surveys the current state of knowledge distillation research across multiple domains, examining its applications to language models, computer vision tasks, and federated learning scenarios. We discuss key methodological advances including intermediate layer distillation, feature-based matching approaches, and attention-based mechanisms for improved knowledge transfer. Furthermore, we explore how distillation addresses practical challenges such as domain adaptation, model heterogeneity, and resource constraints in edge computing environments. The evidence demonstrates that distillation remains a versatile and effective strategy for creating deployable, efficient models without substantial sacrifice in performance.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Improved Accuracy in Spoken Question Answering
papers_seen.abstract: Spoken question answering (SQA) is a challenging task that requires the machine to fully understand the complex spoken documents. Automatic speech recognition (ASR) plays a significant role in the development of QA systems. However, the recent work shows that ASR systems generate highly noisy transcripts, which critically limit the capability of machine comprehension on the SQA task. To address the issue, we present a novel distillation framework. Specifically, we devise a training strategy to perform knowledge distillation (KD) from spoken documents and written counterparts. Our work makes a step towards distilling knowledge from the language model as a supervision signal to lead to better student accuracy by reducing the misalignment between automatic and manual transcriptions. Experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms several state-of-the-art language models on the Spoken-SQuAD dataset.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Critical Technique for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student networks while maintaining competitive performance. By addressing deployment challenges in resource-constrained environments, knowledge distillation has become fundamental to making state-of-the-art deep learning models practical and accessible across diverse applications.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Adversarial Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) has made remarkable progress in the last few years and become a popular paradigm for model compression and knowledge transfer. However, almost all existing KD algorithms are data-driven, i.e., relying on a large amount of original training data or alternative data, which is usually unavailable in real-world scenarios. In this paper, we devote ourselves to this challenging problem and propose a novel adversarial distillation mechanism to craft a compact student model without any real-world data. We introduce a model discrepancy to quantificationally measure the difference between student and teacher models and construct an optimizable upper bound. In our work, the student and the teacher jointly act the role of the discriminator to reduce this discrepancy, when a generator adversarially produces some "hard samples" to enlarge it. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed data-free method yields comparable performance to existing data-driven methods. More strikingly, our approach can be directly extended to semantic segmentation, which is more complicated than classification, and our approach achieves state-of-the-art results. Code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/VainF/Data-Free-Adversarial-Distillation.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that trains a smaller student network to mimic a larger teacher network, enabling deployment of high-performing models on resource-constrained devices. This approach has been successfully applied across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and generative models. The technique leverages knowledge transfer mechanisms to maintain performance while reducing computational and memory requirements, making it valuable for practical applications where efficiency is critical.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression in deep learning and NLP, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach addresses the critical challenge of deploying high-performance neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive accuracy. Recent advances extend beyond traditional teacher-student paradigms to include data-free distillation, multi-teacher approaches, and domain-specific compression strategies, making knowledge distillation essential for real-world applications where computational efficiency is paramount.
